scenarios.name: Cloudburst Oil-Film Spinout
scenarios.description: Five minutes into a sudden cloudburst on a 100 km/h highway, the first rain lifts months of oil film; the lead sedan brakes hard and spins sideways across the ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced tire grip from the oil-water film makes the lead car's emergency stop rotate it into ego's path, creating a lateral avoidance demand within 1.5s.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥2.5s headway and completes avoidance with heading deviation <10° and no lane-exit beyond shoulder line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches gap management tuned to first-rain friction loss rather than steady-state wet grip.

scenarios.name: Wiper Failure Whiteout
scenarios.description: A downburst at 80 km/h on an arterial overwhelms then disables the wipers; the water sheet blinds all forward perception while traffic continues at speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Full windscreen water sheeting removes visual evidence of a braking lead car, forcing the ego to decelerate and stop using radar-only evidence.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates to <20 km/h within 3s of visibility loss with TTC-to-lead never below 2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers graceful degradation when the primary perception channel fails mid-maneuver in weather.

scenarios.name: Overpass Gutter Cascade
scenarios.description: Under an overpass, a clogged gutter dumps a curtain of runoff onto lane 2 during a rain transition; the sedan ahead hits it and brakes hard mid-span.
scenarios.mechanism: The localized water curtain causes an abrupt traction change under the lead car, triggering an unannounced hard brake that becomes ego's stopping demand.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops with ≥1m clearance; required decel ≤6 m/s² without wheel lock indication.
scenarios.trainingValue: Localizes hydro risk to mapable infrastructure features so planners pre-slow at overpasses in rain transitions.

scenarios.name: Hidden-Pothole Swerve Through Standing Water
scenarios.description: On a flooded residential collector at 50 km/h, standing water hides a deep pothole; the oncoming SUV swerves around it directly into ego's lane at closing speed 100 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Submerged pothole makes the SUV's wheel drop and jolt, causing its driver to swerve into ego's lane; the water surface itself is the occluder that hides the cause.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields ≥0.8m lateral clearance by slowing to ≤30 km/h before sightline opens; no evasive swerve needed.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains prediction of other drivers' hidden-hazard reactions, not just detection of visible hazards.

scenarios.name: Truck Rooster-Tail Spray Curtain
scenarios.description: At 90 km/h in moderate rain, a loaded tractor-trailer throws a 40m spray wall behind it; inside that wall a stopped queue is invisible until 25m.
scenarios.mechanism: Tire-spray aerosol from the truck's duals creates a moving occlusion volume that hides the queue, converting normal headway into insufficient stopping distance.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego drops back to ≥120m before entering the spray wall; detected queue TTC ≥4s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Encodes weather-dependent headway inflation for large-vehicle spray volumes.

scenarios.name: Median Drainage Sheet Lateral Push
scenarios.description: A blocked median drain spreads a 3cm sheet across both lanes of a 110 km/h highway curve; crossing it at speed, ego experiences transient lateral drift toward the guardrail.
scenarios.mechanism: Crossflowing water reduces lateral tire force asymmetrically as the right wheels enter first, steering the vehicle several degrees off-heading over ~50m.
scenarios.successSignature: Heading error stays <3° with steering correction completed within 1s; no rail proximity closer than 1.5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exercises low-grip disturbance rejection distinct from obstacle avoidance.

scenarios.name: Plowed Slush Ridge Lane-Skew
scenarios.description: After plowing leaves a 30cm slush ridge between lanes of an arterial at 60 km/h, the ego must merge left past a stopped bus and the wheels dropping into the ridge pull the nose toward a parked car.
scenarios.mechanism: Slush ridge resists tire traversal asymmetrically, yawing the vehicle left mid-lane-change exactly when the merge demands precision.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral position error during merge <0.4m; no contact within 1m of parked car.
scenarios.trainingValue: Combines trajectory planning with known low-friction strip geometry from weather residue.

scenarios.name: Refrozen Slush Ruts Capture Steering
scenarios.description: Overnight refreeze turns afternoon slush ruts into ice grooves on a 50 km/h arterial; the transit bus ahead crosses the ruts and fishtails sideways into ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Frozen ruts trap the bus's rear axle and kick it into yaw when it climbs out, swinging its tail across the adjacent lane at ego.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects bus yaw rate >10°/s and achieves ≥2m separation or full stop before tail crosses centerline.
scenarios.trainingValue: Predictive reaction to temperature-cycled surface states rather than static road class friction.

scenarios.name: Wet-Leaf Slick Rural Curve Fall
scenarios.description: A layer of soaked oak leaves on a 70 km/h rural curve behaves like ice; a cyclist ahead lowsides entering the curve and slides into ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Wet leaf litter drops available friction below 0.2, so the cyclist's routine lean exceeds grip and the fall injects a sliding obstacle into the travel path.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥1m short of sliding cyclist; decel initiated within 0.7s of fall detection.
scenarios.trainingValue: Links seasonal surface contamination (leaves+water) to vulnerable-actor instability.

scenarios.name: Oncoming Plow Throwback Blind
scenarios.description: An oncoming snowplow at combined 110 km/h throws a dense snow-and-grit cloud over ego's half of a rural two-lane; a stopped mailbox-checking car sits inside the cloud.
scenarios.mechanism: Plow blade ejecta forms an instant whiteout volume that conceals the stationary car until ego exits the cloud at reduced separation.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pre-slows to ≤35 km/h when plow is identified; stationary car detected with TTC ≥3s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches anticipatory slowdown for predictable occlusion sources rather than waiting for lost detection.

scenarios.name: Wind-Blown Snow Drift Lane Cutoff
scenarios.description: Gusting crosswind fills the right lane of a flat rural highway with a 40cm drift; the pickup ahead strikes it at 90 km/h and yanks left into ego's lane with no signal.
scenarios.mechanism: Drift impact decelerates and yaws the pickup abruptly, converting its lane position into ego's immediate cut-in problem.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥1.2m clearance via pre-emptive left offset or decel; response within 0.8s of drift sighting.
scenarios.trainingValue: Treats wind-deposited geometry as a dynamic hazard that induces third-party maneuvers.

scenarios.name: Shade-Line Black Ice Transition
scenarios.description: Morning sun crosses a tree line on a rural curve: the dry stretch gives way to a shaded ribbon of transparent ice exactly where the lead hatchback enters, and it spins across the centerline.
scenarios.mechanism: Shading keeps deck temperature below freezing while sunlit sections are dry, producing a step-change in friction that causes the lead car's spinout at unchanged speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies shade boundary ≥100m prior and enters at ≤45 km/h; stops clear of spinning car.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grounds black-ice risk in observable sun/shade geometry instead of uniform road state assumptions.

scenarios.name: Bridge-Deck Frost Patch
scenarios.description: At dawn on an otherwise dry arterial, only the 60m bridge deck holds frost; the sedan ahead brakes onto the deck and rotates 90° blocking both through lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Bridge decks lose heat faster than approach roads, so frost persists solely on the structure; the friction cliff triggers the lead car's rotation into ego's path.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates to ≤40 km/h approaching the structure; avoids rotated sedan with ≥1m margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Isolates structure-specific thermal behavior as the causal trigger, not ambient weather.

scenarios.name: Freezing-Fog Signal Glaze Misread
scenarios.description: Freezing fog coats a suburban signal head with clear glaze; lens scatter makes red and green indistinguishable and the lead car stops abruptly at what is actually a green.
scenarios.mechanism: Ice glaze on the optic diffuses color and shape cues, so the lead driver misreads state and performs an unsignalized stop that becomes ego's mid-block demand.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego resolves true signal state via secondary head or context and stops ≥2m behind lead without rear-end conflict.
scenarios.trainingValue: Decouples signal-state inference from degraded optics under icing conditions.

scenarios.name: Hailfield Stop-Line Slide
scenarios.description: A 3cm hail layer on a roundabout entry at 40 km/h leaves vehicles unable to hold the yield line; the SUV ahead slides through its entry across ego's circulating path.
scenarios.mechanism: Loose hailstones roll under tires reducing effective friction near zero, so the entering SUV cannot stop at the line and violates ego's right-of-way geometrically.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego modulates speed so encroaching SUV clears with ≥1.5s gap; no collision despite right-of-way violation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Right-of-way compliance must be re-derived from surface state, not assumed from rules.

scenarios.name: Hail Squall Sudden Braking Wall
scenarios.description: A hail squall with 10mm stones and 200m visibility sweeps a 100 km/h highway; three vehicles ahead brake simultaneously to a crawl inside the falling hail.
scenarios.mechanism: Impact noise plus visibility collapse drives multiple leaders to panic-brake concurrently, stacking a deceleration wall in front of ego within seconds.
scenarios.successSignature: Controlled decel ≤5 m/s² maintaining ≥2s gaps throughout; final standstill spacing ≥8m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-agent synchronized panic-braking under rapid weather fronts tests longitudinal coordination.

scenarios.name: Hail Panic Shoulder Cut-In
scenarios.description: Mid-hailstorm, a sedan darts from lane 1 onto the narrow shoulder directly across ego's path at 70 km/h without signaling.
scenarios.mechanism: Hail damage fear makes the driver abandon the lane instantly; the unsignaled diagonal cut compresses ego's reaction envelope during already-reduced grip.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego concedes space with smooth decel; minimum lateral gap ≥0.7m during cut-in.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-induced erratic human maneuvers layered on degraded-triction handling.

scenarios.name: Gust-Buffeted Box Truck Lean-In
scenarios.description: Sustained 70 km/h gusts on an exposed river bridge rock an empty box truck so its cab-body oscillates 1m laterally into ego's adjacent lane at 85 km/h closing speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Gust loading on the high empty box produces quasi-periodic lateral excursions of the whole vehicle, repeatedly violating ego's lane boundary.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego tracks truck sway phase and holds ≥1.5m peak clearance or drops back 3s before mid-span.
scenarios.trainingValue: Models oscillatory encroachment requiring phase-aware spacing rather than static buffers.

scenarios.name: High-Side Van Snaking in Gusts
scenarios.description: A lightly loaded high-roof van ahead snakes visibly in crosswinds at 65 km/h on a prairie highway, drifting up to 0.9m across the lane edge toward ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Low cargo mass plus tall side area yields high sensitivity to gust steps, making the van's lane discipline unreliable and ego's passing decision unsafe mid-overtake.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts or defers overtake when van yaw rate exceeds threshold; completes pass only with ≥2m lateral margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Overtake go/no-go conditioned on observed target-vehicle wind susceptibility.

scenarios.name: Tumbleweed Barrage Rural Highway
scenarios.description: A windstorm propels a stream of 1m tumbleweeds across a 90 km/h rural highway; one bounces off a leading pickup's hood and the pickup swerves into the oncoming lane where ego travels.
scenarios.mechanism: Repeated impacts startle the pickup driver into an overcorrection, turning scattered light debris into a head-on avoidance event for ego.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego slows to ≤50 km/h upon swarm identification and clears the errant pickup with ≥1m margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-mass wind-driven debris chains into high-consequence third-party maneuvers.

scenarios.name: Wind-Rolled Trash Bins Residential
scenarios.description: Pre-storm gusts roll wheeled trash bins downhill across a residential street; the minivan ahead brakes for a bin and a second bin wedges under its bumper, halting it diagonally in ego's 45 km/h lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Wind supplies continuous object motion across the roadway; the resulting blockage forces ego to route around a diagonally stalled vehicle between parked cars.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥3m short and executes a verified-clear pass-around with pedestrian scan; no contact with bins or vehicles.
scenarios.trainingValue: Moving low-mass obstacles interacting with traffic flow in constrained residential geometry.

scenarios.name: Wind-Toppled Work-Zone Sign
scenarios.description: A 70 km/h gust topples a portable work-zone arrow board across the closed lane of a work zone taper; the box truck ahead swerves late from the blocked lane into ego's open lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Debris physically blocks the guided path mid-taper, forcing an unplanned merge wave that reaches ego at closing speed with workers adjacent.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields merge space ≥25m before the truck's cut-in point; no barrier proximity <1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-induced failure of temporary traffic control devices cascading into merge conflicts.

scenarios.name: Valley-Dip Fog Bank Stalled Car
scenarios.description: Descending into a river-valley dip at 80 km/h, ego enters a fog bank where a fuel-starved car has stalled in-lane; the sedan just ahead brakes hard upon spotting it.
scenarios.mechanism: Cold-air pooling concentrates radiation fog precisely in the dip, hiding the stall until penetration; the leader's late discovery converts it into ego's emergency stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves queued stop with TTC ≥2s and hazard visibility asserted before restart.
scenarios.trainingValue: Terrain-predicted fog pockets justify pre-emptive speed reduction independent of current visibility.

scenarios.name: Underpass Fog Gradient Speed Trap
scenarios.description: Visibility alternates 300m in fog to 1km under successive underpasses on an urban expressway; the SUV ahead accelerates in each clear span then slams brakes re-entering fog, three times in 2km.
scenarios.mechanism: Periodic visibility steps induce matching speed oscillations in followers, generating repeated hard-brake events exactly at fog boundaries where ego must anticipate them.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds constant ≤60 km/h profile; anticipates each brake with TTC ≥3s, no ABS events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Learning spatially periodic visibility structure to suppress induced speed oscillation.

scenarios.name: Drizzle Headlamp Glare Wall
scenarios.description: In evening drizzle at 50 km/h, oncoming high-beams create a forward light wall; a disabled sedan without lights sits inside the glare volume, invisible until 30m.
scenarios.mechanism: Mie scattering from droplets turns opposing headlights into a veiling luminance source that masks unlit obstacles embedded within it.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects low-contrast obstacle with ≥1.5s TTC margin and passes with ≥1m clearance after confirmatory slow-down.
scenarios.trainingValue: Adverse-contrast target detection inside active glare sources, a known sensor stack weakness.

scenarios.name: Post-Rain Low-Sun Specular Washout
scenarios.description: Minutes after rain ends, a 6° sun reflects specularly off the wet arterial; brake lights of the queue ahead wash out completely inside the reflection band and the queue stops short.
scenarios.mechanism: Forward-scattered glare saturates camera exposure across the reflection stripe, deleting the contrast that marks the stopped queue until range closes under 35m.
scenarios.successSignature: Queue detected with TTC ≥2.5s; ego stops with ≥5m terminal gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Geometry-specific glare saturation handling tied to sun-road alignment angle.

scenarios.name: Mist Backscatter Sun Blinding Turn
scenarios.description: Low sun behind a hillside mist bank backscatters into ego's sensors exactly as the lead car executes an unsignaled right turn at a rural junction, hiding both its turn indicator and body.
scenarios.mechanism: Backscatter bloom from forward mist erases mid-gray targets against the bright field, so the turning car appears only as motion at close range, demanding instant yield.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields with ≥1.5m lateral clearance; turn completion detected before ego reaches conflict point.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sensor degradation correlated with sun-mist geometry and intersecting maneuvers.

scenarios.name: Long-Shadow Stripe Pedestrian Contrast Loss
scenarios.description: A winter sun casts alternating 2m shadow stripes from fence posts across a residential street; a pedestrian walking along the shadow band is invisible to contrast-based detection until stepping into a lit stripe 12m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: Periodic shadow/lit striping defeats appearance-based detection in the shadow band, so the pedestrian materializes mid-crossing with minimal remaining stopping distance at 40 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Pedestrian resolved with ≥1.2s to conflict point; controlled stop ≥1m shy.
scenarios.trainingValue: Structured illumination artifacts (striping) as systematic perception blind zones.

scenarios.name: Frost Melt/Shade Split Lane Crossover
scenarios.description: Sun melts frost off the eastbound lane of a paired rural road but the westbound lane stays shaded and frosted; a commuter crosses from melted to frosted lane at 80 km/h, loses grip and slides across both lanes into ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane-asymmetric thaw creates a lateral friction discontinuity; the crossing maneuver itself triggers the loss of control that intersects ego's path.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies friction split ≥150m early, slows to ≤50 km/h, avoids slide with ≥1m margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Spatially varying friction fields from differential solar heating, not corridor-uniform conditions.

scenarios.name: Freeze-Thaw Pothole Collapse Under Bus
scenarios.description: A water-filled pothole refrozen overnight collapses under a transit bus's front axle at 55 km/h; the bus lurches 1.5m right into ego's adjacent lane then brakes.
scenarios.mechanism: Freeze expansion hollows the substrate so the axle drop imparts a sharp yaw impulse, displacing the bus laterally immediately followed by an emergency stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego registers bus lateral displacement ≥0.8m and achieves ≥2m clearance or complete stop pre-contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Seasonal substrate failure producing compound displacement-then-brake threats.

scenarios.name: Dusk Flash-Freeze Braking Point Shift
scenarios.description: Wet pavement flash-freezes at sunset as temperature crosses 0°C on a 90 km/h expressway; every vehicle ahead begins sliding at a previously safe braking marker, and the queue stacks up mid-lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Phase change at 0°C moves the achievable decel floor from 6 to under 2 m/s² within minutes, invalidating learned braking distances fleet-wide and creating pileup geometry for ego.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego infers transition from environmental trend, caps decel demand ≤2.5 m/s², and stops with ≥8m gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporal friction nonstationarity requiring environment-conditioned replanning, not cached profiles.

scenarios.name: Roof-Snow Slab Launch From Bus
scenarios.description: Following a transit bus at 60 km/h after heavy snow, a 2m roof slab slides off its roof onto the road and the bus brakes hard simultaneously to avoid the debris it sheds.
scenarios.mechanism: Aerodynamic lift plus cabin heat softening releases the slab directly into ego's path while the generator brakes, coupling an impact threat with a stopping demand.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego drops back ≥40m before slab release zone; avoids chunk ≥1m and stops behind bus cleanly.
scenarios.trainingValue: Vehicle-borne weather mass ejection as coupled obstacle-plus-braking scenario.

scenarios.name: Truck Wheel-Spray Brake-Light Bloom
scenarios.description: Behind a waterlogged dump truck at 85 km/h in rain, its sudden braking throws forward a mist surge that scatters its own brake lights into a featureless red bloom, masking the stopped car beyond it.
scenarios.mechanism: Spray density spike coincident with braking saturates local pixels red, destroying depth ordering so the second stationary vehicle emerges only at short range.
scenarios.successSignature: Second vehicle detected with TTC ≥2s; ego stops ≥4m behind with no false-clear through bloom.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion-by-sensor-saturation compounding multi-vehicle depth ambiguity.

scenarios.name: Motorcycle Lowside on Wet Rail Crossing
scenarios.description: A motorcyclist crosses tram rails at a shallow 20° angle on a rain-slicked arterial; the front wheel slips into the groove and the rider lowsides, sliding across ego's 50 km/h path.
scenarios.mechanism: Wet steel rail offers near-zero lateral grip so shallow-angle crossing deflects the wheel into the flangeway, converting a routine crossing into a sliding rider obstacle.
scenarios.successSignature: Rider detected at fall onset with ≥1s to conflict; ego stops ≥1.5m from sliding rider.
scenarios.trainingValue: Surface-material friction interfaces producing vulnerable-actor falls in ego's trajectory.

scenarios.name: Puddle Splash Pedestrian Startle
scenarios.description: A delivery van at 55 km/h blasts a 2m puddle beside a bus stop, soaking a waiting pedestrian who jumps backward off the curb into ego's 45 km/h lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Splash impact provokes a reflex retreat off the sidewalk, injecting a pedestrian into the roadway with under 1.5s of warning.
scenarios.successSignature: Pedestrian yield with required decel ≤5 m/s²; clearance ≥1m maintained.
scenarios.trainingValue: Indirect weather causation: water dynamics altering third-party behavior into ego's path.

scenarios.name: Trailer Aquaplane Jackknife on Ramp Pool
scenarios.description: Pooled water at the sag of a freeway exit ramp hydroplanes the trailer axles of a tractor-trailer at 70 km/h; the trailer swings 25° jackknifing across both ramp lanes ahead of ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Loss of trailer-axle lateral grip while drive axles retain traction converts braking input into articulation angle growth, sweeping the trailer across ego's deceleration path.
scenarios.successSignature: Articulation growth detected within 0.5s; ego stops on ramp with ≥3m to swept trailer.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound vehicle-dynamics failure triggered by localized water pooling geometry.

scenarios.name: Rut-Pond Intersection Red-Light Skid
scenarios.description: Wheel-path ruts pond 3cm of water at a signalized arterial intersection; crossing traffic entering on green skids through on the ponded ruts and crosses ego's legal path on a 60 km/h arterial.
scenarios.mechanism: Rut ponding strips braking friction precisely within the intersection box, so compliant-looking entries become uncontrolled violations intersecting ego's green phase.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego performs defensive look and holds ≥1.5s gap or stops; no intersection contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intersection-specific friction degradation defeating right-of-way reliance.

scenarios.name: Meltstream Ice Ribbon at Dusk
scenarios.description: Snowbank meltwater runs 30m across a rural two-lane and refreezes at dusk into an ice ribbon; the sedan ahead crosses it at 85 km/h, spins 180° and stalls facing ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Daytime melt feeds a recurring flow line that freezes after sundown exactly on the travel path, so unchanged speed meets a friction step and produces a facing stall blocking the lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reads melt line + dusk cue, pre-slows to ≤50 km/h; avoids stalled vehicle ≥2m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Diurnal cycle coupling (melt by day, freeze by night) as predictive surface-risk model.

scenarios.name: Sandblow Friction Loss in Rural Cut
scenarios.description: Sustained wind blows drifted sand 5cm deep across a sunken rural highway section; the pickup ahead brakes at 95 km/h, locks and rotates 90° blocking both lanes inside the sand band.
scenarios.mechanism: Loose sand annihilates braking friction only within the cut where drift accumulates, inducing the lead vehicle's rotational stall directly in ego's sealed corridor.
scenarios.successSignature: Sand band identified visually ≥120m out; entry speed ≤55 km/h; stop clear of spun pickup.
scenarios.trainingValue: Wind-deposited particulate friction zones mapped to topographic containment geometry.

scenarios.name: Dust Wall Hiding Stopped Equipment
scenarios.description: A dust wall kicked up by 80 km/h gusts off a harvested field rolls across a rural road, and a parked grain cart sits fully concealed inside it at the crest of a rise.
scenarios.mechanism: The mobile dust volume provides total optical occlusion synchronized with a fixed obstruction, so ego exits the wall at speed directly toward the cart with under 2s to react.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pre-slows on dust-wall sighting; cart resolved with TTC ≥2s; pass-around ≥1.5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Transient regional occlusion events requiring conservative speed floors until cleared.

scenarios.name: Lake-Effect Squall Whiteout Entry
scenarios.description: A lake-effect snow squall wall 100m deep crosses the highway; inside it a three-car chain collision has already formed, invisible from the clear air where ego approaches at 105 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Sharp mesoscale visibility gradient conceals an existing crash mass; ego must decelerate based on the visible squall edge alone before losing all confirmation.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed ≤50 km/h achieved before wall entry; interior collision cluster detected with TTC ≥2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Entry decisions under imminent total sensory blackout with inferred interior hazards.

scenarios.name: Hoarfrost Limb Drop in Wind
scenarios.description: Freezing fog has coated roadside limbs with hoarfrost; a gust snaps a 4m ice-laden branch into ego's lane at 75 km/h and the sedan ahead swerves into the adjacent lane where a cyclist rides.
scenarios.mechanism: Accumulated rime adds canopy load until wind stress exceeds wood strength, releasing debris whose evasion cascade endangers a third party in the escape lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates secondary swerve, shields cyclist with ≥1m clearance; debris avoided or straddled safely at ≤40 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-load canopy failure driving multi-agent cascade avoidance including VRU protection.

scenarios.name: Clogged Drain River Across Arterial
scenarios.description: A storm-drain clog sends a 5cm river flowing across two arterial lanes; a sedan entering at 60 km/h planes and its bow-wave drift carries it 1.2m into ego's adjacent lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Flow direction plus planing loss combine to translate the crossing vehicle laterally along the water gradient into ego's lane space during its turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego grants dynamic buffer ≥1.5m or delays entry; conflict resolved with TTC ≥2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Water-flow vector fields as directional hazard gradients displacing other traffic.

scenarios.name: Cyclist Slip on Wet Manhole in Curve
scenarios.description: A cyclist leaning through a 40 km/h urban curve crosses a rain-filmed manhole cover and lowsides, sliding 6m along ego's inner path.
scenarios.mechanism: Metal coefficient drop on wet film removes mid-corner grip exactly at maximum lean, ejecting the rider tangentially into the ego vehicle's racing line.
scenarios.successSignature: Fall detected at initiation; ego stops ≥1m from rider with decel ≤6 m/s² on wet surface.
scenarios.trainingValue: Material-specific micro-hazards producing VRU ejections in geometrically predictable spots.

scenarios.name: Ground Blizzard Buried Stall
scenarios.description: Despite clear sky, 70 km/h wind lofts fallen snow across a flat highway cutting visibility to 80m; a previously disabled hatchback sits half-buried in the right lane with no lights.
scenarios.mechanism: Wind-driven surface loft sustains whiteout without new snowfall, while drifting re-buries the stall and drains its battery so neither visibility nor reflectivity marks it.
scenarios.successSignature: Buried obstacle detected with TTC ≥2.5s; pass-around executed with ≥1.5m clearance at ≤45 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Clear-weather whiteout decouples sky condition from visibility, defeating naive sensor gating.

scenarios.name: Hail-Clog Underpass Ponding With Stalled Cars
scenarios.description: Hail accumulates 4cm and clogs the underpass drain; ponded water stalls two sedans mid-underpass and their occupants begin exiting toward ego's single navigable gap at 30 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Hail volume defeats drainage capacity creating rapid ponding; stalled vehicles plus exiting occupants compress ego's passage into a narrow dynamic gap between water and doors.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego threads gap with ≥0.8m to vehicles, ≤15 km/h past occupants, no wake push into waterline.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound weather event chaining debris→drainage→stalls→VRU exposure in one constraint set.

scenarios.name: Frost-Blind Windshield Pullout
scenarios.description: A resident scrapes a palm-sized porthole in a frosted windshield and pulls out of residential parking into ego's 40 km/h lane, stopping broadside across half of it.
scenarios.mechanism: Near-zero visibility makes the driver commit blindly to the pullout; incomplete clearing guarantees they cannot see ego, converting parking egress into a fixed obstruction at closing speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Pullout intent read from wheel rotation ≥2s early; ego stops ≥2m short with no horn-dependent resolution.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-impaired other-driver perception modeled as predictable blind commitment behavior.

scenarios.name: Parking-Garage Ramp Ice Slide Into Aisle
scenarios.description: A shaded parking-garage ramp holds patchy ice; a descending crossover SUV cannot hold the turn, slides backward and pivots into the ground-level driving aisle where ego rolls at 15 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Patchy ice under the inside wheels reverses the intended turn into a controlled-loss slide that terminates in the live aisle, presenting ego with an angled moving block.
scenarios.successSignature: Slide detected on entry; ego stops ≥2.5m from aisle mouth; resumes only post-settle with ≥1.5m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Infrastructure shading plus weather producing vehicle dynamics failures at facility chokepoints.

scenarios.name: Loading Dock Ramp Glaze Rollback
scenarios.description: Freezing rain glazes a loading dock apron; a departing delivery van fails the 8% grade, rolls backward down the ramp and pivots across the service road where ego transits at 30 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Glazed slope exceeds available grade-start friction so the van's launch degrades into an accelerating rollback sweeping across the service road's only lane.
environment: industrial loading dock apron, 30 km/h service road
scenarios.successSignature: Rollback predicted from slip at launch; ego stops ≥3m from sweep arc; no dock-worker endangerment.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grade-ice interaction at commercial infrastructure converting departure attempts into moving blocks.

scenarios.name: Work-Zone Gravel Shoulder Slump in Rain
scenarios.description: Rain saturates the temporary gravel shoulder of a work-zone lane shift; a concrete truck's outer wheels punch through the softened edge at 55 km/h and the cab tilts 15° into ego's open lane before recovering.
scenarios.mechanism: Saturation collapses engineered bearing capacity of the temporary shoulder, so routine edge-tracking loads produce sudden tilt and intrusion into the adjacent live lane ego occupies.
scenarios.successSignature: Shoulder-edge risk inferred ≥80m early; ego offsets left within lane and holds ≥1.2m during tilt event.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-modified bearing capacity of temporary construction surfaces as lane-intrusion source.

scenarios.name: bus-stop-jaywalker-emergence
scenarios.description: City bus stopped at a near-side bus stop fully occludes a pedestrian who then steps out from in front of it.
scenarios.mechanism: The 12m bus body hides the pedestrian until they emerge into ego's lane ~2m ahead at walking speed, forcing an emergency stop within a 1.2s window.
scenarios.successSignature: Brake initiated within 0.5s of emergence; required decel <=6 m/s^2; no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Canonical dynamic occlusion: a 'parked bus' assumption becomes wrong mid-plan.

scenarios.name: double-occlusion-truck-bus-cyclist
scenarios.description: A cyclist is hidden by a stopped bus which is itself hidden by a slow box truck in ego's lane; the bus pulls out revealing the cyclist late.
scenarios.mechanism: Nested occluders keep the cyclist invisible until the bus departs; ego must brake for a target it never tracked.
scenarios.successSignature: Cyclist handled within one frame of geometric reveal; TTC margin >=1.5s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests reasoning over nested occluders, not single-object shadowing.

scenarios.name: turning-van-hides-crosser
scenarios.description: A van turning across ego's lane temporarily blocks the crosswalk it just cut through, hiding a pedestrian crossing behind it.
scenarios.mechanism: The van body occludes the crosswalk ~1.5s; the pedestrian emerges onto ego's conflict path as the van clears.
scenarios.successSignature: Path predicted pre-reveal or braked within 0.4s; no crosswalk encroachment.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion by a moving actor whose own trajectory implies the hidden region.

scenarios.name: delivery-truck-hides-wheelchair
scenarios.description: A parked delivery truck blocks sight of a wheelchair user crossing slowly between it and traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Low seated profile below the 2.5m sightline keeps the occupant invisible until ego is ~5m away; <1.5s remains.
scenarios.successSignature: Offset or decel begun before reveal line; clearance >=1m at pass.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low, slow actors behind tall occluders are worst-case for detection latency and gap math.

scenarios.name: far-side-bus-departure-reveal
scenarios.description: Ego yields to a far-side bus departing its stop; pedestrians who waited beside the bus step into the crosswalk as it moves.
scenarios.mechanism: Bus departure opens a moving screen; peds appear mid-crosswalk at 1.4 m/s exactly as ego accelerates from stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Re-acceleration aborted; stopped >=1m before crosswalk.
scenarios.trainingValue: Go-decision must survive occlusion reversal right after commitment.

scenarios.name: boarding-crowd-screen
scenarios.description: A crowd boarding a bus spills over the curb line, screening one member who steps backward into ego's travel lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The dense cluster masks a single reverse-step into the roadway; the individual is untrackable inside the group blob until separation.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral drift plus partial brake keeping >=0.8m from the curb-most group member.
scenarios.trainingValue: Group-vs-individual tracking failure under dense clustering.

scenarios.name: crest-hidden-centerline-straddler
scenarios.description: Over a blind crest an oncoming car overtaking another straddles ego's lane, hidden until ego crosses the apex.
scenarios.mechanism: Passing geometry is below the crest sightline; revealed head-on closure at combined 140 km/h forces an immediate edge escape.
scenarios.successSignature: Right-edge escape <0.8s post-reveal; lateral clearance >=1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Head-on avoidance from a blind crest is the highest-consequence occlusion class.

scenarios.name: crest-hidden-crosswalk-pedestrian
scenarios.description: A marked crosswalk sits 15m past a blind crest; a jogger enters it below the sightline.
scenarios.mechanism: The marking is invisible before the crest, removing its cue value; the jogger appears inside braking distance at 60 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed <=45 km/h at crest, or full stop >=1m short.
scenarios.trainingValue: Geometry-aware speed choice when markings lie beyond sightlines.

scenarios.name: queue-gap-cyclist-sightline
scenarios.description: Ego creeps left through a gap past queued vehicles to turn; a cyclist in the bike lane is hidden by the queue's rear SUV.
scenarios.mechanism: The queued SUV cuts the bike-lane sightline; the cyclist emerges into the exact gap ego is entering, 10 km/h vs 25 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Creep paused on reveal; no lateral overlap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Left-turn creep is the classic cyclist killer via queue occlusion.

scenarios.name: hedge-corner-rollout
scenarios.description: At a stop-sign corner a tall hedge hides a cross-street vehicle doing a rolling stop into ego's path.
scenarios.mechanism: Vegetation caps the sight triangle at 3m; the conflicting car appears at intersection center already at 15 km/h without stopping.
scenarios.successSignature: Covered approach <=15 km/h; yield completed on reveal.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sight-triangle-limited speed policy, not reaction, is the tested skill.

scenarios.name: unlit-road-deer-at-beam-edge
scenarios.description: On an unlit rural road a deer stands motionless at the pavement edge beyond low-beam range, then steps out.
scenarios.mechanism: Detection only at the ~50m low-beam limit; the deer steps laterally at 55 km/h leaving ~2.5s and no ambient cues.
scenarios.successSignature: Brake-only response; controlled stop or stable steer-around with >=1m margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Beam-range physics sets a hard detection horizon; tests range-limited planning.

scenarios.name: dark-clothed-roadside-walker
scenarios.description: An unlit road with a pedestrian in black clothing walking along the lane edge facing away from traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: No retroreflection and near-zero contrast against the dark verge: detectable only when headlights are nearly abeam; ~1.8s at 50 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral shift >=1m plus decel; clearance >=1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Near-zero-contrast vulnerable actor; classic nighttime fatality pattern.

scenarios.name: stalled-unlit-vehicle-darkness
scenarios.description: A stalled sedan with all lights dead sits in the far lane around a slight curve on an unlit road.
scenarios.mechanism: Curve geometry plus a dead vehicle removes every active cue; it appears as an unlit mass only inside 60m at 65 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane change or decel decided within 1.2s of first return; no off-road excursion.
scenarios.trainingValue: Unlit stationary obstacles defeat brightness-based saliency.

scenarios.name: unlit-washed-out-shoulder
scenarios.description: Night rain has washed out a 3m shoulder section on an unlit country road with no guardrail marking the drop.
scenarios.mechanism: Missing edge cues corrupt the inferred pavement boundary; the only evidence is a cone cluster visible late under low beams.
scenarios.successSignature: Tracking maintained through the zone; no wheel past the edge line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Negative obstacles (absence of surface) in darkness.

scenarios.name: high-beam-ped-between-oncoming
scenarios.description: Two oncoming cars with high beams sandwich a gap; a pedestrian crosses inside the glare wedge between them.
scenarios.mechanism: Glare saturates exposure exactly where the pedestrian appears; the dark gap between bright blobs hides a 1.7 m/s crosser until ~15m.
scenarios.successSignature: Glare-heuristic decel engaged pre-confirmation; stop clear of the crosser.
scenarios.trainingValue: Treat saturated image regions as unknown-hold, not free space.

scenarios.name: glare-during-unprotected-left-gap
scenarios.description: During a nighttime unprotected left, oncoming high beams wash out the far lanes, hiding a fast closer inside the gap ego accepts.
scenarios.mechanism: The gap is judged from visible cars only; a glare-masked vehicle closes at 80 km/h within the accepted window.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn aborted or reversed on late reveal; TTC >=1s restored.
scenarios.trainingValue: Uncertainty-inflated gap acceptance under glare.

scenarios.name: rear-glare-mirror-camera-washout
scenarios.description: A lifted pickup tailgating runs high beams into ego's rear camera and mirrors, blinding rearward checks during a merge-back.
scenarios.mechanism: Rear-channel saturation removes trailing-traffic evidence exactly when ego must judge the merge gap.
scenarios.successSignature: Merge executed with conservative gap or deferred; no reliance on the washed-out channel.
scenarios.trainingValue: Degraded rear sensing must force conservative maneuvers.

scenarios.name: sun-glare-left-turn-signal-invisible
scenarios.description: Low sun sits directly behind the traffic signal during ego's left turn; the signal state is unreadable and opposing cars become silhouettes.
scenarios.mechanism: Backlit saturation erases signal lamps and oncoming detail simultaneously at the moment of commitment.
scenarios.successSignature: Treat-as-unplanned: wait or proceed only with a confirmed gap; no assumed green.
scenarios.trainingValue: Joint loss of signal state and object contrast at the decision instant.

scenarios.name: wet-road-glare-hides-crest-queue
scenarios.description: Sun glare reflecting off wet uphill pavement blanks the view over a crest where traffic is queued.
scenarios.mechanism: Specular sheet dominates pixels above the crest line; the stopped queue appears only after ego tops it at 55 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Pre-crest slowdown on the wet+glare heuristic; stopped >=2m short of the queue tail.
scenarios.trainingValue: Specular washout compounding geometric occlusion.

scenarios.name: backlit-pedestrian-silhouette
scenarios.description: A pedestrian crosses directly in front of the setting sun, rendered as a featureless silhouette against glare.
scenarios.mechanism: Contrast inversion merges the figure with background bloom; evidence arrives only via motion differential late in the crossing.
scenarios.successSignature: Silhouette treated as an actor; yield complete before the conflict point.
scenarios.trainingValue: Appearance-free detection relying on temporal motion cues.

scenarios.name: tunnel-transition-adaptation-zone
scenarios.description: Entering a dark tunnel at noon, a broken-down motorcycle sits 25m inside the transition zone.
scenarios.mechanism: Exposure adaptation lag (~1-2s) renders the interior near-black; the small dark object is inside braking distance at an 80 km/h entry.
scenarios.successSignature: Reduced entry speed or early lane offset chosen; obstacle cleared >=1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exposure-transient blindness with known spatial extent.

scenarios.name: lit-station-pop-in-from-dark-road
scenarios.description: Pulling from an unlit road into a brightly lit gas station forecourt, parked cars appear only after crossing the illumination boundary.
scenarios.mechanism: Local adaptation flips exposure; parked cars pop in late, one directly into the turn-in path.
environment: gas station entrance from unlit road
scenarios.successSignature: Forecourt entry at crawl speed; no late braking inside the forecourt.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dark-to-light pop-in of static actors at lighting discontinuities.

scenarios.name: wet-lens-droplet-ped-smear
scenarios.description: Drizzle beads on the forward camera lens; a curbside pedestrian smears into background streaks exactly when they lean toward the roadway.
scenarios.mechanism: Droplet optics blur the low-contrast region, destroying the lean-out precursor and delaying prediction ~1s.
scenarios.successSignature: Confidence-gated hedge (decel/offset) triggered despite no clean detection.
scenarios.trainingValue: Behavioral conservatism gated by degradation confidence, not detection.

scenarios.name: lens-sheet-after-tunnel-exit
scenarios.description: Condensation sheets across the camera dome on humid-day tunnel exit; lane lines vanish for ~2 seconds at highway speed.
scenarios.mechanism: The moisture film removes all lane evidence mid-curve, forcing a dead-reckon lateral hold while a truck drifts toward the lane edge ahead.
scenarios.successSignature: Heading held within +/-0.3m of pre-degradation lane position until lines re-acquire.
scenarios.trainingValue: Open-loop lateral dead-reckoning through total lane-loss windows.

scenarios.name: slush-film-hides-tire-fragment
scenarios.description: Winter slush film on the bumper camera suppresses low-contrast returns; a dark tire-tread fragment in-lane goes undetected until 20m.
scenarios.mechanism: The film's salt haze raises the detection floor exactly at asphalt-fragment contrast; at 70 km/h braking alone no longer suffices, forcing a lane-change decision on partial evidence.
scenarios.successSignature: Swerve or combined maneuver initiated by 25m; no fragment contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sensor-film degradation shifting the solution from brake to steer.

scenarios.name: motion-blur-debris-vs-shadow
scenarios.description: At 120 km/h a small retread fragment on dry pavement is motion-blurred into an elongated smear indistinguishable from a pavement shadow patch.
scenarios.mechanism: Sub-frame blur destroys shape evidence; the classifier must resolve shadow-vs-solid from parallax alone inside 1.5s, deciding brake vs ignore.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct classification: brake if solid, steady track if shadow; no false emergency event either way.
scenarios.trainingValue: Speed-induced blur collapsing shape cues; parallax-only disambiguation.

scenarios.name: night-rain-brake-light-smear
scenarios.description: Night rain turns the lead truck's brake lights into vertical streaks; the smear masks the onset time of actual deceleration.
scenarios.mechanism: Streak elongation makes the brake-lamp step ambiguous, delaying closure-rate estimation ~0.7s at a 100 km/h follow.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decel matched within 1 m/s^2 of lead; gap never under 1.2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Photometric artifact corrupting the highest-weight cue (lead brake state).

scenarios.name: radar-ghost-gantry-phantom-brake
scenarios.description: An overhead sign gantry on a crest returns a radar ghost of a car in ego's empty lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Multipath off the gantry fabricates a stationary object at ego's height; the planner must brake or verify-and-overrule on camera-only evidence.
scenarios.successSignature: No unnecessary hard brake (decel <=3 m/s^2) and no collision; ghost correctly rejected.
scenarios.trainingValue: Behavioral model of sensor ghosting: false-positive suppression under real geometry.

scenarios.name: bridge-joint-ghost-phantom-brake
scenarios.description: An expansion joint on a bridge deck produces intermittent double returns read as a low object 30m ahead in-lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The flickering phantom appears only at specific approach angles, so it validates on some frames; ego must hold course while the phantom flickers at 90 km/h with traffic behind.
scenarios.successSignature: Track continuity maintained through the joint; no phantom-brake below 3 m/s^2 and no rear-end risk created.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intermittent false positives requiring temporal persistence logic.

scenarios.name: guardrail-curve-multipath-ghost
scenarios.description: On a tight ramp curve, radar multipath along a continuous guardrail fabricates a slow vehicle ghost hugging the lane's inside edge.
scenarios.mechanism: The ghost's range rate mimics a slow lead, tempting an unnecessary slowdown that a real trailing car then punishes.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed held within 5 km/h of nominal; ghost not tracked as a lead.
scenarios.trainingValue: Curve-geometry-correlated ghosting; tests map-aware false-positive rejection.

scenarios.name: dusk-mattress-debris-asphalt-matched
scenarios.description: At dusk a flattened dark mattress piece lies in-lane, its albedo nearly identical to worn asphalt.
scenarios.mechanism: Contrast below threshold delays classification until headlight range; at 60 km/h the stop/swerve decision arrives with ~2s margin and oncoming traffic blocks a left swerve.
scenarios.successSignature: Right-lane change or controlled stop completed; no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Albedo-matched low objects at the edge of headlight range.

scenarios.name: tire-tread-wet-asphalt-camouflage
scenarios.description: A wet black tire-tread fragment on glossy wet asphalt is visible to humans only by its slight sheen difference.
scenarios.mechanism: Wet-on-wet contrast defeats texture cues; detection at 25m at 70 km/h leaves a swerve-vs-brake tradeoff with an adjacent car present.
scenarios.successSignature: Maneuver chosen with >=1m clearance to both fragment and adjacent car.
scenarios.trainingValue: Camouflaged small obstacles forcing joint lateral-longitudinal planning.

scenarios.name: windblown-cardboard-static-dynamic
scenarios.description: A large cardboard box tumbles across a multilane arterial in gusts, alternating between sliding and stopping dead in-lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Intermittent zero-velocity breaks motion-based tracking; the planner must reclassify dynamic-vs-static twice within 2s while closing at 50 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Track held through motion discontinuities; avoid maneuver consistent with final state.
scenarios.trainingValue: Motion-model failure on wind-driven actors.

scenarios.name: fresh-paint-reflective-lane-offset
scenarios.description: Fresh glass-bead thermoplastic stripes on night rain retroreflect so strongly that dashes bloom, and a neighboring lane's bloomed line reads as ego's own.
scenarios.mechanism: Bloomed specular dashes shift the inferred lane center ~0.4m toward the adjacent lane exactly where a truck runs close in that lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral position kept >=1m from the truck despite inference offset.
scenarios.trainingValue: Retroreflective markings corrupting lane inference under wet-night conditions.

scenarios.name: glossy-workzone-tape-lane-boundary
scenarios.description: Reflective construction tape strung on low posts parallels the true lane through a work zone; in headlight glow the tape reads as the stronger lane boundary.
scenarios.mechanism: Tape retroreflectivity outcompetes worn paint, biasing the lateral controller toward a line that pinches 0.5m at a barrier pinch-point.
scenarios.successSignature: No barrier contact; min clearance >=0.5m at the pinch.
scenarios.trainingValue: Competing boundary cues where the stronger visual line is wrong.

scenarios.name: puddle-mirrored-lane-lines
scenarios.description: A broad smooth puddle mirrors the lane dashes above it, projecting a phantom shifted line pattern into the ego lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The mirrored pattern is brighter than the true worn paint, dragging the inferred lane center across the puddle where the true lane is offset 0.6m.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral error <=0.3m through the puddle stretch.
scenarios.trainingValue: Reflection-induced lane geometry corruption.

scenarios.name: tree-shadow-phantom-obstacle
scenarios.description: Low-sun tree shadows stripe an empty lane with high-contrast bands; one band edge reads as a stationary obstacle.
scenarios.mechanism: A shadow boundary with road-texture discontinuity passes the obstacle gate, triggering phantom braking in a clear lane with a tailgating follower.
scenarios.successSignature: Decel <=2.5 m/s^2 or correctly rejected; no rear-end risk introduced.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shadow-as-obstacle false positives under realistic illumination.

scenarios.name: overpass-shadow-band-flicker
scenarios.description: Closely spaced overpass ribs cast alternating light/dark bands the ego traverses at 15 Hz effective flicker.
scenarios.mechanism: Frame-to-frame illumination flips defeat appearance consistency checks, fragmenting a real pedestrian on the shoulder into intermittent ghosts.
scenarios.successSignature: Pedestrian track persisted across flicker; hedge behavior if not.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporal aliasing from structured shadow bands breaking track persistence.

scenarios.name: sign-shadow-stopped-vehicle-mirage
scenarios.description: At distance an overhead sign's sharp shadow on the pavement forms a rectangle resembling a stopped dark vehicle in-lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Range-uncertain classification wastes a full braking episode or, worse, the mirage masks a real debris item 40m beyond it in the same lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Both the mirage dismissed and the real debris handled.
scenarios.trainingValue: Distractor masking: the false object consuming attention from the true one.

scenarios.name: wiper-arc-vision-wedge
scenarios.description: Heavy rain with one working wiper leaves a clear vision wedge sweeping the windshield; a pedestrian crossing ahead is visible only when inside the arc.
scenarios.mechanism: The pedestrian appears and disappears at ~1 Hz as the blade sweeps, so existence confidence oscillates while closing at 40 km/h in an unprotected turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Conservative envelope maintained across occlusion flicker; yield completed.
scenarios.trainingValue: Periodic partial visibility requiring existence-belief persistence.

scenarios.name: rain-beads-split-ped-fragments
scenarios.description: Rain beads on the camera dome split an oncoming cyclist into disconnected fragments (wheel blob, torso smear) at dusk.
scenarios.mechanism: Fragmented returns fail instance clustering; the wheel blob alone is classified as debris while the torso is noise, corrupting the prediction until 20m.
scenarios.successSignature: Cyclist-level response (full yield) not debris-level response; clearance >=1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Fragmentation-induced class downgrade of a vulnerable actor.

scenarios.name: iced-sensor-quadrant-blind-merge
scenarios.description: An ice patch covers one camera quadrant overnight; on a ramp merge, a car enters exactly from the blinded quadrant.
scenarios.mechanism: The frozen housing removes ~90 degrees of coverage with no self-diagnostic flag; the merging car is unseen until radar-only returns at 30m.
scenarios.successSignature: Merge aborted or gap opened on radar-only evidence; no sideswipe.
scenarios.trainingValue: Partial field-of-view loss without detection; cross-modal fallback.

scenarios.name: mud-splash-bumper-camera-outage
scenarios.description: Hitting a puddle splashes mud over the bumper camera cluster 3s before a required lane change around a stopped car.
scenarios.mechanism: The splash degrades exactly the sensors needed for the maneuver; ego must execute or defer using remaining coverage and map priors.
scenarios.successSignature: Degraded-mode maneuver completed with >=1m clearance or safe stop.
scenarios.trainingValue: Abrupt mid-task sensor loss with a maneuver already in flight.

scenarios.name: crest-oncoming-bus-high-beam-glare
scenarios.description: On a crest curve at night an oncoming bus's roof-line high beams rake across ego's camera just as a cyclist crosses beyond the crest.
scenarios.mechanism: Glare recovery (~1s) spans the exact reveal window of the cyclist; ego crests at 60 km/h with the conflict hidden inside the recovery period.
scenarios.successSignature: Post-glare scan catches cyclist with >=1.2s to react; speed pre-managed for blind crest.
scenarios.trainingValue: Glare timing aligned to occlusion reveal; compound perception attack.

scenarios.name: night-umbrella-legs-only
scenarios.description: In night rain a pedestrian crosses holding a large umbrella that blocks the torso and head from ego's low-mounted cameras; only legs are visible.
scenarios.mechanism: Legs-only returns fail the pedestrian classifier (reads as two small moving objects), so no crossing-intent prediction forms while ego approaches at 45 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Yield behavior triggered from leg-motion evidence; stop before crosswalk.
scenarios.trainingValue: Partial-body detection forcing behavior inference from atypical signatures.

scenarios.name: fog-patch-slow-tractor-emergence
scenarios.description: A 100m fog patch on a rural road conceals a tractor doing 12 km/h in-lane; it emerges from the fog at 60m at ego's 80 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Fog caps detection range below braking-comfort distance; the tractor's near-zero closing-rate signature is misread initially as a static object, corrupting the approach plan.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed <=50 km/h inside fog patch or stop achieved >=2m short.
scenarios.trainingValue: Range-limited perception plus speed-misclassification of slow movers.

scenarios.name: truck-spray-whiteout-lead-brake
scenarios.description: Following a truck in heavy rain, its wheel spray creates a 30m whiteout; the truck brakes hard for a queue hidden inside the spray.
scenarios.mechanism: The lead is the only tracked object and its visual signature vanishes in spray exactly when it decelerates; closure is detectable only via radar for ~1.5s at 90 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Decel within 0.8s of lead brake onset; min gap >=0.8s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Total visual loss on the primary lead during its most critical action.

scenarios.name: gravel-dust-concealed-pullout
scenarios.description: A truck on a gravel shoulder kicks a dust cloud across both lanes, hiding a car accelerating out of a field entrance inside the cloud.
scenarios.mechanism: The pulling car is inside the dust when it commits to the lane; it emerges at 30 km/h across ego's path at 70 km/h with ~2s to act.
scenarios.successSignature: Reveal-to-response <=0.7s; lateral or longitudinal solution with >=1m margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Self-generated obscurant: ego's own environment destroys its sensing.

scenarios.name: snow-spray-hides-overtaking-motorcycle
scenarios.description: An opposing truck's snow spray whites out the oncoming lane, inside which a motorcycle is overtaking the truck at 40 km/h closing delta.
scenarios.mechanism: The motorcycle is invisible until it exits the spray cloud ~70m ahead; combined closure ~160 km/h leaves under 1.6s to hold lane and speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane position held, no evasive swerve into shoulder drop; clearance >=1m at pass.
scenarios.trainingValue: Third-party occlusion plus high-delta closing on a small vulnerable actor.

scenarios.name: led-billboard-flicker-aliasing-pedestrian
scenarios.description: A flickering LED billboard at night strobes the adjacent sidewalk at ~12 Hz, aliasing a pedestrian's walking gait on camera.
scenarios.mechanism: Strobe sampling makes the pedestrian's limbs appear near-stationary frame-to-frame, defeating motion-gated detection while they approach the curb at 1.5 m/s.
scenarios.successSignature: Pedestrian detected despite aliasing; preemptive yield before curb.
scenarios.trainingValue: Environmental strobe aliasing suppressing motion cues for vulnerable actors.

scenarios.name: unprotected-left-false-gap-from-braking-leader
scenarios.description: Ego waits in a left-turn pocket for a gap in 55 km/h oncoming traffic; the platoon leader brakes hard for debris, and followers interpret the brake lights as a signal to follow-through, compressing gaps to under 2s.
scenarios.mechanism: Leader's hard braking creates an apparent large gap that closes rapidly as followers accelerate around him, so a gap that looks acceptable at decision time is consumed before ego can clear the far lanes.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either rejects the gap (stays stopped) or completes the turn with ≥1.5s TTC margin against the second follower; lateral clearance ≥2m at crossing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gap acceptance must account for gap-closing dynamics of following traffic, not just instantaneous spacing.

scenarios.name: stale-green-high-speed-dilemma-zone
scenarios.description: Ego approaches at 65 km/h on a green that has been up 40+ seconds with no cross demand; it must decide whether the green will hold before reaching the point-of-no-return.
scenarios.mechanism: Long-stale green raises probability of abrupt phase change; if it changes inside the dilemma zone, neither comfortable braking nor maintaining speed clears the intersection on yellow.
actors: cross traffic waiting on side street
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥3 m/s² decel margin or clears stop line with ≥0.5s before yellow onset prediction error; never enters box on red.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches time-based staleness estimation rather than treating green as indefinite.

scenarios.name: yellow-boundary-45mph-can-i-stop
scenarios.description: Yellow appears when ego is 60m from stop line at 72 km/h on wet asphalt.
scenarios.mechanism: Required deceleration (~3.5 m/s²) sits just above comfortable-wet threshold, so both stopping and proceeding are physically feasible; correct action depends on precise distance/µ estimation, and rear follower at 15m gap constrains hard braking.
scenarios.successSignature: Chosen maneuver keeps |decel| ≤ 4.5 m/s² and stops before line or enters on yellow with ≥0.3s margin; no skid or rear-end conflict.
scenarios.trainingValue: Boundary case where the safe answer flips with small errors in friction estimate — punishes conservative bias in both directions.

scenarios.name: short-yellow-mistimed-phase
scenarios.description: A mis-programmed controller gives 2.8s yellow on a 60 km/h approach where ITE guidelines require ~4.7s, leaving drivers who legally entered on green unable to clear.
scenarios.mechanism: Insufficient yellow + all-red means vehicles past the stop line at yellow onset cannot clear before cross traffic releases, manufacturing red-light conflicts from normal driving.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego predicts the trap and stops early if feasible; if committed, clears far edge with ≥0.8s before cross green; flags timing anomaly.
scenarios.trainingValue: AV must not blindly trust signal timing legality; clearance-time feasibility check needed.

scenarios.name: flashing-red-all-approaches-malfunction
scenarios.description: Controller fault puts main street into flashing red while side street stays normal, creating asymmetric right-of-way nobody follows consistently.
scenarios.mechanism: Main-street drivers treat flashing red as a brief pause-and-roll; their rolling violations collide with legitimate side-street greens, forcing ego to defend a legal movement against illegal flow.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields to actual occupying/clearing traffic regardless of nominal ROW and crosses with zero conflicts within a 10s window.
scenarios.trainingValue: Right-of-law vs right-of-way divergence; behavior must track what actors do, not what rules say.

scenarios.name: flashing-yellow-arrow-reverts-mid-turn
scenarios.description: Ego begins a permissive left on flashing yellow arrow; the phase terminates abruptly and the arrow goes solid red while ego is mid-intersection facing oncoming 50 km/h traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal-state change invalidates the premise of the committed turn; ego must either complete against closing oncoming headway or yield-in-place and block the box.
scenarios.successSignature: Complete turn with ≥1.2s TTC to oncoming, or controlled stop clear of opposing lanes; never reverses or freezes in path.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mid-maneuver signal invalidation tests replanning under commitment.

scenarios.name: intermittent-signal-flicker-blackout
scenarios.description: Signal browns out repeatedly (0.5–3s dark flashes) during a storm; each blackout technically converts the junction to all-way stop but traffic behavior lags reality.
scenarios.mechanism: Dark intervals shorter than reaction time mean different drivers observe different states — some see green remnants, some see darkness — producing inconsistent ROW claims that ego must arbitrate online.
actors: sedan that entered during dark interval
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats every observed transition conservatively, enters only after confirming all approaches yielding, zero conflicts over 3 cycles.
scenarios.trainingValue: State estimation under non-stationary signal semantics; blackout rule application with partial observability.

scenarios.name: right-on-red-crossing-cyclist-overtaking
scenarios.description: Ego stops for red, intends right-on-red; a cyclist traveling straight in the bike lane to ego's right approaches at 25 km/h exactly as ego would launch.
scenarios.mechanism: Cyclist has green and rides in ego's blind side arc; launching on the gap in motor traffic hides the conflict until the cyclist is alongside, causing a classic right-hook geometry.
environment: junction with bike lane through the corner
scenarios.successSignature: Ego launches only with ≥2.5s predicted TTC to cyclist and hugs right curb post-turn; lateral pass margin ≥1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Red does not clear vulnerable road users already in motion on ego's right flank.

scenarios.name: left-onset-vs-oncoming-speeder
scenarios.description: Ego starts its left on a fresh green as oncoming traffic queues release; one oncoming sedan accelerates hard to beat the phase change, arriving at 75 km/h instead of expected 50.
scenarios.mechanism: Speed misestimate inflates apparent gap adequacy: ego commits based on typical launch speeds, but outlier acceleration collapses TTC mid-turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts or accelerates to complete with ≥1.0s final TTC; heading rate stays within 30°/s comfort envelope.
scenarios.trainingValue: Launch-phase gap estimation must include acceleration outliers, not mean traffic speed.

scenarios.name: queue-spillback-blocks-the-box
scenarios.description: Cross-street queue backs past the junction; ego's green arrives but exiting space on the far side is occupied, and a delivery van ahead enters anyway, wedging sideways in the box.
scenarios.mechanism: Downstream storage exhaustion makes legal entry a gridlock contribution; ego must predict spillback from visible far-side queue length before committing, then handle the wedged blocker.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops before stop line when downstream gap < vehicle length + 1m buffer; navigates around wedge without entering opposing lanes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Don't-block-the-box requires predictive storage checks — a rule humans break constantly and AVs must enforce.

scenarios.name: four-way-simultaneous-arrival-deadlock
scenarios.description: All four approaches have one vehicle arriving at the two-way stop-equivalent moment (signal dark); each driver hesitates differently — one waves, one creeps, one asserts.
scenarios.mechanism: Simultaneous arrival voids deterministic ordering; resolution depends on reading micro-behaviors (creep depth, wheel angle, gesture), and misreading any one produces a collision course.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego establishes ordered passage resolving all three within 15s using creep-and-yield protocol; zero standoffs >5s and zero conflicts.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-agent negotiation with ambiguous protocol — measures social inference, not rules.

scenarios.name: protected-permissive-arrow-drop-mid-clearance
scenarios.description: Ego is halfway through a protected left when the green arrow ends and the through phase for cross traffic begins earlier than the all-red allows ego to finish.
scenarios.mechanism: Controller skips expected all-red (lead-lag swap), releasing cross traffic while ego occupies their lanes; ego must clear a conflict zone that was guaranteed empty seconds ago.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects early release and clears conflict lanes with ≥0.5s margin or stops short of cross-path; no collision-course entry.
scenarios.trainingValue: Non-standard phasing breaks the all-red safety assumption baked into most planners.

scenarios.name: late-signal-change-during-committed-crossing
scenarios.description: Ego enters a wide 40m junction on late yellow; the transverse signal turns green for pedestrians and cross traffic while ego is still traversing lanes 3–4.
scenarios.mechanism: Junction width exceeds clearance provided by the yellow interval for ego's speed, so the signal state inverts mid-traversal and every new-green actor becomes an emerging threat vector.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥20 km/h progress and clears all conflict paths before nearest new-green actor reaches shared geometry, or executes preemptive stop in the safe gap between directional lanes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Clearance-time feasibility for oversized junctions; teaches lane-by-lane threat scheduling mid-crossing.

scenarios.name: opposing-left-under-your-terminating-arrow
scenarios.description: Dual left-turn phases: ego turns left on arrow while an opposing-facing left (from cross street with lagging phase) jumps early, converging on the same exit lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Lagging-phase driver anticipates his green and launches on the tail of ego's arrow; both lefts converge on one receiving lane with <1.5s separation.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego takes the outer receiving lane or yields lane choice; merge resolved with ≥1m lateral gap and no brake-check below 2 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Exit-lane contention during phase transitions; target-lane assignment must be dynamic.

scenarios.name: red-runner-crossing-perpendicular-flow
scenarios.description: Two seconds after ego's green starts, a pickup runs the cross red at 70 km/h through the middle lanes while front-row cars in other lanes have begun moving.
scenarios.mechanism: The runner's path threads between launched vehicles; ego's launch trajectory intersects the runner's lane specifically because ego started latest from the rearmost queue position.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects runner within 0.5s of green onset and achieves ≥2m longitudinal standoff or aborts launch; no entry into runner's corridor while he's within 30m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Green onset is the highest-risk instant; first-two-second surveillance must override launch commitment.

scenarios.name: pedestrian-countdown-expires-mid-crossing
scenarios.description: Pedestrian starts on 4s countdown, moves at 0.9 m/s (elderly), and is still in ego's receiving lane when parallel traffic gets green and ego begins its right turn.
scenarios.mechanism: Countdown expiry doesn't remove the pedestrian — it removes other drivers' expectation of him; the slow walker becomes invisible to traffic logic exactly when ego's turning path sweeps his position.
environment: right-turn slip path crossing two lanes
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields until pedestrian's trailing edge clears turn path with ≥1m margin, even though display shows zero and other traffic flows.
scenarios.trainingValue: Countdown displays are advisory; actual body position governs. Tests display-vs-reality arbitration.

scenarios.name: t-junction-hidden-crosswalk-launch
scenarios.description: At a T-junction, ego turns right on red; pedestrians from the terminated stem cross behind parked vans and appear inside ego's turn radius with no crosswalk warning possible.
scenarios.mechanism: The stem's sidewalk feeds directly into the corner at an angle hidden by near-side parked vans; red-right launch assumption 'no crossing traffic' fails because the stem has no signal to violate.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego creeps with ≤5 km/h until the entire corner arc is visually confirmed; yields with ≥2m margin to any stem user.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occluded unsignalized legs defeat signal-state reasoning; geometry-specific blind-corner protocols required.

scenarios.name: offset-intersection-weave-trap
scenarios.description: Two closely spaced T-junctions offset by 25m create a short two-way section; ego exits the first junction as cross traffic simultaneously exits the second into the same connector lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Neither driver sees the other's approach leg; both receive green-equivalent gaps and enter the 25m connector head-on or side-swipe.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds back from connector until opposing entry is ruled out (≥3s observation); resolves with ≥1.5s headway if both commit.
scenarios.trainingValue: Offset junctions are compound hazards — treat as single fused intersection, not sequential independent ones.

scenarios.name: five-leg-convergence-conflict
scenarios.description: Five-leg junction where two minor legs feed diagonal streams that both cut across ego's left-turn exit path at unsignalized yield priority.
scenarios.mechanism: Diagonal legs produce conflict points outside standard 4-leg conflict matrices; ego's gap model calibrated for perpendicular traffic misses the 45°-approach stream whose closing speed is 1.4× higher.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego accepts gaps computed with true closing speeds (≥4s on diagonals); zero conflicts including the diagonal stream.
scenarios.trainingValue: Non-standard topology breaks template conflict models; closing-speed-aware gap acceptance needed.

scenarios.name: motorcycle-filters-into-left-turn-gap
scenarios.description: Ego judges a gap adequate against visible cars; a motorcycle overtaking the stopped oncoming queue at 60 km/h occupies that gap invisibly between two cars.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane-filtering rider fills inter-vehicle gaps that gap-acceptance logic reads as empty; his closing speed triples effective danger of an apparently safe turn.
environment: bright sun glinting off car roofs
scenarios.successSignature: Ego scans gap interior (not just boundaries) and rejects filtered-gap acceptance; if turning, maintains ≥2s TTC to rider.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gap emptiness must be verified volumetrically, not inferred from flanking vehicles.

scenarios.name: heavy-truck-dilemma-zone-speed-trap
scenarios.description: Ego trails a loaded truck downhill toward a stale green; truck masks the signal and decelerates unpredictably, putting ego in a dilemma zone it couldn't observe.
scenarios.mechanism: Truck occlusion prevents seeing the signal change; when truck brakes for the yellow, ego discovers the state change at 40m instead of 150m, leaving insufficient stopping distance at 65 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains following distance ≥3.5s uphill-masked so yellow discovery leaves ≥3 m/s² feasible stop, or uses truck's wake-gap to clear on yellow legally.
scenarios.trainingValue: Signal visibility budgeting behind tall vehicles on grades — occlusion converts stale greens into traps.

scenarios.name: permissive-left-yellow-trap
scenarios.description: Permissive left: ego waits in intersection for oncoming gap; oncoming through gets yellow and stops, but ego's own signal yellows simultaneously and cross traffic launches while ego still faces oncoming straggler.
scenarios.mechanism: Classic yellow trap — lagging oncoming phase means ego's yellow doesn't guarantee oncoming has stopped; cross release catches ego stranded center-box.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego predicts straggler clearance before committing to wait-in-box strategy; if stranded, completes turn ahead of cross bus with ≥1s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Phasing-pattern awareness determines whether waiting in the box is survivable — core yellow-trap reasoning.

scenarios.name: leading-pedestrian-interval-surprise
scenarios.description: Walk signal starts 5s before parallel traffic green; ego's fresh green arrives just as late-starting pedestrians from the far curb are mid-crossing in ego's right-turn sweep.
scenarios.mechanism: LPI gives pedestrians a head start that expires unevenly — fast ones clear, slow ones are exactly in turn paths when vehicles release; ego's green implies empty crosswalk but isn't.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego launches only after confirming sweep-arc clear of LPI stragglers; yields with ≥1.5m margin if occupied.
scenarios.trainingValue: Phase-design features (LPI) alter the meaning of green; AV must know signal-program conventions.

scenarios.name: obscured-no-turn-on-red-sign
scenarios.description: Right-on-red is prohibited but foliage obscures the plaque; cross-stream cyclist has green and the absence of visible prohibition tempts the launch the law forbids.
scenarios.mechanism: Sign occlusion removes the legal gate while physical gap remains tempting; the conflict arises from information asymmetry — cyclist correctly expects no red-right launches.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego remains stopped through full red despite gap temptation; launches only at green with cyclist scan.
scenarios.trainingValue: Legal-knowledge grounding must survive degraded signage perception — missing evidence ≠ permission.

scenarios.name: u-turn-overlapping-right-turn-conflict
scenarios.description: Ego executes right-on-green as a car from the cross street performs an overlapping U-turn that sweeps into ego's receiving lane from the opposite direction.
scenarios.mechanism: U-turn geometry occupies the exact receiving lane ego targets, arriving from an unexpected heading; conflict emerges 1.5s post-entry when both are committed.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego selects alternate receiving lane or yields with ≥1.2s TTC; resolved merge without horn-forced correction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Receiving-lane threats arrive from reversed headings; turn planning must enumerate U-turn trajectories.

scenarios.name: jaywalk-through-stopped-queue-between-lanes
scenarios.description: Traffic is stopped at red; a pedestrian weaves between queued vehicles in the travel lanes themselves, appearing in ego's lane gap 8m before the crosswalk.
scenarios.mechanism: Queue creates a canyon walls hide; pedestrian's zig-zag path crosses ego's lane at a point where no crosswalk logic applies and sightlines are 2m long.
actors: rear car creeping for gap view
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≤10 km/h in queue with ≥2m gap discipline enabling stop within 3m of appearing pedestrian.
scenarios.trainingValue: Queues generate indoor-like pedestrian environments; crosswalk assumptions invert inside them.

scenarios.name: emergency-preemption-sudden-red
scenarios.description: Approaching on stale green, ego's signal snaps to red instantly via emergency-vehicle preemption with shortened yellow; ego at 55 km/h is 70m out.
scenarios.mechanism: Preemption truncates normal phase transitions (skips yellow extension), creating an artificially compressed stop decision with an ambulance bearing down on the cross axis.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves firm stop (≥4 m/s², ABS-limited but controlled) before line or clears fully; yields corridor afterward; no panic stop in the box.
