scenarios.trainingValue: Priority-control systems distort standard timing envelopes; recognition of preemption signature matters.

scenarios.name: far-side-bus-hides-crossing-pedestrians
scenarios.description: Ego turns left; a bus stopped at the far-side bus stop occludes the entire far crosswalk; three pedestrians emerge from in front of the bus into ego's exit path.
scenarios.mechanism: Far-side transit stops place static occlusion exactly where turning paths meet crosswalks; pedestrians step out at walking speed into a corridor ego believed vacated.
environment: left-turn exit path across bus zone
scenarios.successSignature: Ego creeps exit arc at ≤8 km/h with continuous occlusion-edge scanning; yields ≥2m before any pedestrian.
scenarios.trainingValue: Transit infrastructure dictates occlusion-aware turn speeds; map-layer knowledge (stops) informs scanning.

scenarios.name: sun-washout-unreadable-signal-head
scenarios.description: Low sun aligns with signal face at 8° elevation; lens flare renders the through-ball color indeterminate while a stale-looking green may actually be yellow.
scenarios.mechanism: Perception uncertainty about signal state forces behavior arbitration between signal evidence and contextual evidence (cross-traffic posture, queue behavior), and these disagree.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego resolves state within 1.5s using multi-modal evidence; proceeds only on confirmed green or stops safely; documents low-confidence.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sensor-level signal ambiguity is common; fusion fallback strategies need training coverage.

scenarios.name: van-occludes-oncoming-cyclist-during-left
scenarios.description: Ego turns left behind/beside a large oncoming van in the adjacent oncoming lane; a cyclist riding at 30 km/h is completely hidden by the van until ego is mid-turn.
scenarios.mechanism: Two-lane oncoming stream lets the van mask the faster, narrower cyclist in the inner lane; the reveal occurs at 15m closure leaving ~0.8s to react at turn completion.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays turn initiation until inner-lane occupancy confirmed, or executes evasive slow-down yielding ≥1m clearance to revealed cyclist.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion-aware gap acceptance: gaps behind large vehicles carry hidden-fast-user risk proportional to lane count.

scenarios.name: double-left-lane-tracking-divergence
scenarios.description: Dual left-turn lanes: the truck beside ego swings wide and his trailer sweeps into ego's lane mid-turn, while a car in the outer dual-left cuts inside to ego's target lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Off-tracking geometry plus opportunistic lane-cutting compresses a two-lane receiving area into contested single-file, forcing ego to re-target mid-manuver.
environment: receiving street with parked cars narrowing to one usable lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego completes with ≥0.5m trailer clearance and abandons contested lane assignment cleanly; no stop inside box >2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Coordinated multi-actor turn dynamics; ego's path plan must be robust to neighbors' geometric drift.

scenarios.name: truck-offtrack-encroaches-during-his-left
scenarios.description: Turning truck's rear wheels off-track across ego's stopped position line in the adjacent through lane while ego holds at the stop bar.
scenarios.mechanism: Cab completes the visual promise of clearance but the trailer path sweeps 1.2m into the through lane; ego's instinctive creep-forward for position places it in trailer path.
environment: ego in adjacent lane at stop bar
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds ≥1.5m from predicted trailer sweep path until trailer axles clear; no creep during articulated-turn occupancy.
scenarios.trainingValue: Predicting articulated off-tracking protects ego during others' turns — passive-threat anticipation.

scenarios.name: walk-sign-contradicts-vehicle-signal
scenarios.description: Controller fault shows WALK to pedestrians while parallel traffic shows green (should be conflicting); pedestrians legitimately cross into ego's green path.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal desync manufactures a conflict that both parties are 'correct' to trust; ego's green promise is broken by infrastructure error, not actor misbehavior.
actors: parallel through car also trusting green
scenarios.successSignature: Ego prioritizes detected VRUs over own signal indication; proceeds only post-clearance; logs contradiction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Infrastructure faults pit trusted sources against each other; physical truth overrides signal authority.

scenarios.name: temporary-work-zone-short-cycle-signal
scenarios.description: Portable work-zone signal runs a 20s cycle with 3s yellow; queue discharge from prior cycle still crossing when green snaps away mid-platoon.
scenarios.mechanism: Short-cycle timing assumes low demand but a tour bus discharges slowly; ego mid-platoon faces yellow with insufficient spacing to either stop comfortably or clear before the opposing release.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego times platoon position to avoid yellow-trap: stops with ≥3 m/s² max or clears with ≥1s margin; never stalls in conflict zone.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporary signals violate permanent-signal timing priors; context classification must retune expectations.

scenarios.name: protected-left-chevron-violator-cutacross
scenarios.description: Dedicated protected-only left phase; an impatient driver from the oncoming through queue launches across ego's arrow-protected path believing the phase belongs to him too.
scenarios.mechanism: Protected-only phasing gives ego lawful priority, but the violator's 55 km/h crossing converts right-of-way into a physical evasion problem requiring ego to brake mid-turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego modulates turn to maintain ≥1s TTC despite violator, or aborts to safe position; retains lane discipline without freezing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Having right-of-way ≠ having safety; protected phases breed violators precisely because they feel exclusive.

scenarios.name: bike-box-encroachment-at-red
scenarios.description: Advanced stop line (bike box) ahead of ego at red; two cyclists filter forward into the box as ego creeps forward over the stop line chasing queue gaps.
scenarios.mechanism: Bike box exists to give cyclists head-start priority; ego's encroachment eliminates their refuge and positions them in ego's blind right-front at green onset.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego respects bike box boundary at red (stop ≥0.5m behind); launches with cyclist head-start honored, passing margin ≥1.5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Junction VRU infrastructure alters stop-line semantics; spatial compliance precedes behavioral compliance.

scenarios.name: ego-right-hook-cyclist-straight
scenarios.description: Ego right-turns on green as a cyclist going straight passes on ego's right side in the bike lane — the canonical right-hook with tight timing: cyclist at 22 km/h reaches corner 0.8s after ego initiates.
scenarios.mechanism: Turn initiation precedes cyclist arrival, so mirrors checked at initiation show clear; cyclist closes the arc during ego's yaw, colliding at the apex if ego maintains turn rate.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego monitors arc throughout yaw; yields mid-turn with ≥1m clearance or delays initiation by ≥1.5s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Continuous-threat monitoring during committed maneuvers — mirror checks don't substitute for tracking.

scenarios.name: queued-platoon-launch-race-permissive-left
scenarios.description: Oncoming stream is queued at red upstream; light turns green for oncoming and platoon launches as coordinated wall; ego attempts left through the 1.5s window before wall forms.
scenarios.mechanism: Launch synchronization means individual gaps close simultaneously rather than sequentially — the last viable gap evaporates at a predictable-but-tight instant that ego must nail.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either clears before first oncomer reaches conflict point (≥2s margin) or declines entirely; no hesitation-in-box.
scenarios.trainingValue: Platoon-launch dynamics make gap windows quantal, not gradual — accept-or-reject decisiveness under social pressure.

scenarios.name: insufficient-all-red-cross-clearance-conflict
scenarios.description: All-red interval programmed at 1s for a 35m junction; a slow truck needs 4s to clear and is still crossing when ego's green releases.
scenarios.mechanism: Timing error converts the previous phase's legal entrant into ego's obstacle; ego's green is real but the box is occupied by a vehicle that also had green.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego scans box before launch, detects clearing vehicle, delays entry until truck's trailing axle clears ego's lane path with ≥1s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Green-onset box-scanning defends against clearance failures — a systematic infrastructure weakness class.

scenarios.name: late-detector-triggered-pedestrian-phase
scenarios.description: Ego mid-approach on green; push-button activation injects an unplanned pedestrian phase 3s later, terminating ego's green earlier than any projection assumed.
scenarios.mechanism: Actuated controllers extend/truncate phases dynamically; ego's planning horizon built on minimum green is invalidated mid-approach, converting a cruise into a stop-go decision at 50m.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego adapts phase-length estimate within one detection frame; stops comfortably (≤3.5 m/s²) or clears before truncation with ≥0.5s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Actuated signals make green length stochastic; plans must carry phase-duration uncertainty.

scenarios.name: near-corner-parked-truck-sightline-block
scenarios.description: Delivery truck parked 3m from the corner blocks ego's view of the cross street as ego prepares to turn right on green; a car appears at 40 km/h from complete occlusion.
scenarios.mechanism: Near-side parking at corners destroys the turning sight triangle; ego must commit to creep-based incremental exposure rather than continuous-view turns.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego advances in ≤1m increments with full stop capability maintained; yields immediately on reveal with ≥1.5s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Corner parking transforms signalized turns into unsignalized-style blind negotiations.

scenarios.name: wrong-way-entry-one-way-pair
scenarios.description: One-way street pair: a confused driver enters the wrong direction toward ego as ego turns left onto the correct one-way, meeting nose-to-nose in the junction.
scenarios.mechanism: Wrong-way entry inverts all gap predictions — the oncoming stream ego yielded to contains a contraflow vehicle occupying the lane ego planned to receive into.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects contraflow heading within 1s of reveal and selects escape (stop/yield lane) achieving ≥2m separation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Heading-validation of all junction users, not just presence detection — topology violations need dedicated response policies.

scenarios.name: left-pocket-overflow-blocks-through-lane
scenarios.description: Left-turn demand exceeds pocket capacity; queue tails out of the pocket into the through lane, and ego must decide whether to pass the tail on the right within the same green.
scenarios.mechanism: Pocket spillover merges two movement streams; passing the tail means sharing the through lane with left-turners who will swing left across ego's path individually as their gaps open.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego passes overflow with ≥1.5m lateral margin and ≥2s TTC to each successive left-swing; or queues behind with safe gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Pocket saturation creates serial dynamic obstacles inside one's own lane — a distinct hazard from cross traffic.

scenarios.name: free-right-slip-lane-yield-ambiguity
scenarios.description: Channelized free-right slip lane with yield triangle: ego in slip must merge with cross traffic that has varying expectations — some drivers assume slip always yields, one waves ego in aggressively.
scenarios.mechanism: Yield semantics at slips are socially unstable; the waving driver creates a gap that a second vehicle in the adjacent lane does not honor, converting courtesy into a multi-lane trap.
actors: non-yielding car in lane 2 at 45 km/h
cyclist using crosswalk at slip exit
scenarios.successSignature: Ego accepts waved gaps only after verifying all lanes; enters with ≥3s TTC to fastest lane; handles slip-exit crosswalk yield.
scenarios.trainingValue: Courtesy gaps are lane-local; multi-lane verification must override single-actor invitations.

scenarios.name: adaptive-signal-green-extension-whiplash
scenarios.description: Adaptive controller extends ego's green twice (holding cross queue) then truncates abruptly as priority shifts; ego's third-gap decision meets a green that dies 2s early.
scenarios.mechanism: Adaptive timing breaks periodicity priors — ego's learned rhythm of this corridor mispredicts phase life, placing the go/no-go boundary at the wrong distance.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego carries ≥20% phase-duration uncertainty margin; decision boundary placed conservatively enough that truncation costs ≤4 m/s² braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Corridor learning must detect control-regime changes (fixed-time vs adaptive) and retune risk margins.

scenarios.name: standing-water-stall-mid-box
scenarios.description: Deep ponding in the junction dip (blocked drain); the lead car entering on green hydroplanes and stalls dead center; ego's green continues with stalled obstacle and cross phase approaching in 12s.
scenarios.mechanism: Weather-induced immobilization converts a moving-conflict model into a static-obstacle-plus-clock problem: ego must route around within remaining phase time before cross traffic launches.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego routes around stall with ≥1m clearance and completes exit before cross green minus 2s safety pad; no entry into deepest water (depth >15cm avoided).
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound events (weather + drainage + stall) require joint routing-timing optimization under deadline pressure.

scenarios.name: procession-gap-threading-through-red
scenarios.description: A funeral procession threads the junction on red in linked groups; ego's green arrives between two procession clusters, and a straggler car with headlights on runs the red 2s into ego's phase.
scenarios.mechanism: Procession cohesion obligations make stragglers run reds predictably-but-irregularly; ego must distinguish procession members (follow-me behavior) from ordinary red-runners.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies procession membership and yields to coherent groups while asserting against isolated violators; zero contact, minimal delay.
scenarios.trainingValue: Group-behavior classification changes right-of-way computation — membership inference affects gap policy.

scenarios.name: transit-priority-white-bar-confusion
scenarios.description: Bus rapid transit signal shows vertical white bars granting the bus lane a phase while general traffic faces red; a confused driver launches on the bus signal, crossing ego's queued path.
scenarios.mechanism: Unusual signal indications get misread by untrained humans; the misreader creates cross-flow that ego's own red correctly warned about, testing ego's defense-in-depth at red.
actors: confused driver launching on BRT signal
environment: BPT corridor junction with quadra-pole transit signals
scenarios.successSignature: Ego remains stopped despite tempting gap opened by confused launcher; avoids secondary conflict with actual BRT buses at ≥3s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-signal junctions contain indication sets that humans misread; ego must model other agents' signal comprehension errors.

scenarios.name: rail-crossing-adjacent-queue-spillback-trap
scenarios.description: Junction sits 20m from a rail crossing; ego's green releases into available 20m, but cross-street queue growth during ego's approach means the exit path now ends on active tracks as gates begin descending.
scenarios.mechanism: Storage between junction and tracks is the binding constraint — visible at approach time only if ego projects cross-queue growth; committing traps ego on tracks with gates lowering.
actors: car ahead that stopped ON tracks
scenarios.successSignature: Ego refuses entry when projected downstream storage < ego length + 3m; if trapped ahead-of-gate, evacuates clear of tracks within gate-warning window.
scenarios.trainingValue: Coupled junction-rail topologies make green lights lethal; storage projection is survival-critical, not convenience.

scenarios.name: school-release-wave-across-green
scenarios.description: School dismissal floods the junction with children in loose groups; ego's green arrives while the tail of a 30-child crossing wave is still dispersing across two lanes with no adult supervision at that corner.
scenarios.mechanism: Group crossings have fuzzy boundaries — the 'wave' has no clear trailing edge, so binary clear/not-clear decisions fail; individual stragglers emerge at random points for 10+ seconds after the mass passes.
actors: crossing guard on opposite corner only
scenarios.successSignature: Ego waits until zero VRUs within 5m of turn arc for continuous 3s; tolerates honking; launches with full arc confirmation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Stochastic group-tail modeling — patience calibration against social pressure with measurable straggler statistics.

scenarios.name: ball-precedes-child-between-parked-cars
scenarios.description: A ball rolls out from between parked cars into the ego lane on a residential street, followed 1–2 seconds later by a six-year-old sprinting after it at ~4 m/s.
scenarios.mechanism: The ball precedes the child through the identical occlusion gap, so the AV first receives a small fast-moving non-pedestrian object; the child becomes trackable only after physically entering the gap, collapsing usable reaction time to roughly one second.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego infers risk from the ball alone and achieves ≥0.35 g deceleration before the child's silhouette clears the gap; final lateral clearance ≥1.5 m or full stop ≥2 m upstream.
scenarios.trainingValue: Forces precursor-object reasoning instead of waiting for pedestrian confirmation — the canonical occluded-child failure mode with a learnable causal cue.

scenarios.name: earbud-walker-zero-gaze-stepout
scenarios.description: A pedestrian wearing over-ear headphones and looking down at a phone steps from behind a parked box truck mid-block into the ego lane at a shallow oblique angle, never raising his head.
scenarios.mechanism: There is no gaze raise, no hesitation, no deceleration — the intent classifier sees a continuous walking trajectory intersecting the lane with zero pre-entry kinematic cues, so prediction holds 'parallel to curb' until physical lane entry.
actors: adult pedestrian with headphones and phone, ~1.4 m/s
environment: urban collector, one lane each direction
scenarios.successSignature: Stop initiated within 1.5 s of first visible limb movement; required decel ≤4 m/s² from 40 km/h; clearance ≥0.8 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains prediction robustness to absent intent signals — success cannot rely on the pedestrian yielding or telegraphing.

scenarios.name: four-person-diagonal-jaywalk-stagger
scenarios.description: Four adults cross diagonally mid-block between two intersections outside any crosswalk, entering at staggered times so later members reach the ego lane after earlier members have cleared it.
scenarios.mechanism: Staggered entries mean the group occupies the ego lane only after the nearest member vacates it; cluster tracking merges and splits identities, silently dropping the last entrant from the active obstacle set.
actors: 4 adult pedestrians, 1.2–1.6 m/s, staggered 2–4 s apart
environment: two-lane urban street, 300 m from nearest signal
scenarios.successSignature: Track identity preserved for all four through merge/split; ego yields with TTC margin ≥2 s to the last entrant.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exercises multi-object association stability — the failure is a data-association bug manifesting as a safety event, common in production stacks.

scenarios.name: wheelchair-user-travel-lane-follow
scenarios.description: With the sidewalk closed by scaffolding, a power-wheelchair user travels in the right travel lane at 5 km/h facing forward; ego must follow at walking pace until a driveway gap allows a full-lane pass.
scenarios.mechanism: The sub-meter seat height degrades radar returns beyond ~40 m and the demand is sustained constrained following plus a merge into opposing traffic — not a braking event — so conventional stop-distance metrics don't apply.
environment: sidewalk blocked by scaffolding with closure signage
one lane each direction, no shoulders
scenarios.successSignature: Follow distance ≥6 m at ≤8 km/h held ≥60 s, then completed pass with ≥1.2 m lateral gap and no forced opposing-vehicle braking harder than 0.15 g.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers low-profile vulnerable road users and sustained-nuisance handling that planners tuned for discrete events systematically mishandle.

scenarios.name: mobility-scooter-wrong-way-drift
scenarios.description: A mobility scooter travels against the traffic direction in the curb/bike lane at 8 km/h, swerving toward the lane center each time the rider avoids a pothole.
scenarios.mechanism: Wrong-way motion invalidates direction priors from the HD map, and the drift events are stochastic responses to surface defects, so lateral prediction error exceeds the corridor width within about three seconds.
actors: mobility scooter rider, ~8 km/h, against traffic
environment: patched asphalt with potholes near the curb line
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reduces to ≤15 km/h within 30 m and passes with ≥1.5 m clearance timed against observed drift amplitude; no closer than 0.8 m at any instant.
scenarios.trainingValue: Combines counterflow motion with surface-driven erratic lateral dynamics — two predictor-hostile properties in one actor.

scenarios.name: jogger-against-traffic-puddle-swing
scenarios.description: A jogger runs toward the ego at ~3.5 m/s along the road edge (facing traffic) and swings out around a puddle directly into the ego lane 25 m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: Closing speed is the sum of both velocities (~65 km/h combined), halving decision time relative to a crossing pedestrian, and the swing trigger is a surface feature the ego itself can barely resolve at that range.
environment: large puddle at the road edge after rain
scenarios.successSignature: Required decel held ≤4.5 m/s² with ≥1 m lateral clearance achieved by pass-by; heading-rate change of ego ≤3°/s unless full stop needed.
scenarios.trainingValue: Highlights closing-rate arithmetic on same-corridor VRUs — a class of timing errors simulators routinely underestimate.

scenarios.name: conflicting-flagger-hand-signals
scenarios.description: Two flaggers at opposite ends of a one-lane work zone gesture at the ego simultaneously — the near one waves through, the far one shows an upheld palm ordering halt.
scenarios.mechanism: Command arbitration is genuinely ambiguous; resolving it correctly (halt dominates, or obey the controller governing your direction) must happen while the wave-through gesture actively invites acceleration toward the opposing worker.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego comes to a complete hold within one reaction cycle and does not accelerate for ≥3 s until receiving one unambiguous gesture; resume only with clear wave-through plus visible spotter.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests gesture semantics, conflict resolution between authority sources, and conservative tie-breaking under social pressure to proceed.

scenarios.name: backward-walking-escort-worker
scenarios.description: A worker walks backward at 5 km/h directly ahead of the ego, arm-waving a wide-load convoy through a lane narrowed to 3 m by concrete barriers.
scenarios.mechanism: Backward gait defeats gait-based intent and fall-risk models, and the worker is simultaneously obstacle and controller — ego must mirror his unplanned pace changes within ~0.5 s to maintain the escort envelope.
actors: escort worker walking backward, variable 3–6 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Following distance held 4–8 m with ego speed error ≤1 km/h against worker pace changes; zero barrier proximity violations (<0.3 m).
scenarios.trainingValue: Rare coupling of speed control, gesture compliance, and tight-corridor tracking in a single scenario; exposes cruise-controller brittleness at walking speeds.

scenarios.name: bus-queue-front-crossers
scenarios.description: Three buses are bunched at a stop; passengers alighting from the rearmost bus walk forward across the road directly in front of the stationary lead bus, entering the ego lane from total occlusion.
scenarios.mechanism: The lead bus occludes the crossing path completely, and the first revealed crosser implies a continuous queue behind — the ego must generalize from one pedestrian to a sustained stream, not treat it as a singleton event.
environment: transit stop on a two-lane arterial
buses aligned nose-to-tail along the curb
scenarios.successSignature: Ego creeps past the bus front at ≤5 km/h with stop achievable within 1 m of travel upon each new reveal; zero clearance violations under 0.5 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches occlusion-aware flow inference — treating one reveal as evidence of a queue — which single-object planners miss.

scenarios.name: tram-nonplatform-door-alight
scenarios.description: A light-rail vehicle stopped mid-street by a queue ahead unexpectedly opens doors on the traffic side; passengers step directly into lane 1 and fan toward the curb.
scenarios.mechanism: Non-platform door release is rare, so the ego has no prior for it; passengers emerge at half-meter spacing with no curb buffer, converting stopped traffic into a continuous pedestrian stream across the lane within seconds.
environment: median-running tram on a four-lane avenue
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds ≥3 m standoff from the tram flank while the stream persists; any creep limited to ≤3 km/h; no contact and no blocking of the far crosswalk.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers rare-mode transitions in transit behavior; the mechanism punishes priors learned only from scheduled platform stops.

scenarios.name: dismissal-surge-after-guard-departs
scenarios.description: Twenty minutes after the crossing guard leaves, groups of students cross mid-block at the abandoned guard post in loose clusters, some breaking into runs mid-road.
scenarios.mechanism: No signal or supervisor remains, so entries are probabilistic and tightly clustered; children change speed mid-crossing, breaking the constant-velocity gap-acceptance model calibrated on adult walkers.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields to every cluster with TTC ≥2.5 s at yield initiation and tolerates mid-crossing speed jumps of +100% without clearance loss below 1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Population-specific gap acceptance (children run, hesitate, regroup) — a distribution shift most pedestrian models trained on adults fail.

scenarios.name: fence-gap-shortcut-teens
scenarios.description: Three teenagers cut through a broken fence gap that empties directly onto the roadway 30 m before the signaled crosswalk, angling downstream toward it while already inside the travel lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The path originates inside the roadway rather than at a curb, so there is no curb-entry event to trigger pedestrian classification — they are detected as in-lane objects moving parallel, then turning across ego's path.
environment: school-adjacent street with damaged perimeter fence
scenarios.successSignature: In-lane pedestrian classified within 0.5 s of first detection; ego slows to ≤15 km/h until all three clear the traveled way.
scenarios.trainingValue: Region-based perception fails when pedestrians start in the road; forces class-agnostic dynamic-object handling near attractor shortcuts.

scenarios.name: intoxicated-stumble-shuffle
scenarios.description: An intoxicated man shuffles along the curb line at ~0.8 m/s with a ±1 m sinusoidal weave, then stumbles forward 1.5 m into lane 1 with no preparatory motion.
scenarios.mechanism: Lateral variance is high enough that any trajectory prediction is void beyond one second, and the fall event is a discontinuous displacement — the largest possible positional jump with the smallest possible warning.
environment: two lanes, 30 km/h, active nightlife foot traffic
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥1.2 m dynamic standoff tracking the weave envelope and arrests the stumble incursion with ≤5 m/s² decel; no oscillating stop-and-go artifacts.
scenarios.trainingValue: Stress-tests trajectory uncertainty propagation — correct behavior demands planning against a covariance cloud, not a predicted path.

scenarios.name: intoxicated-midcross-reversal
scenarios.description: An intoxicated pedestrian starts a legal crossing of a four-lane road, stalls in lane 2, turns around, and walks back toward his origin just as the ego's lane clears and traffic launches.
scenarios.mechanism: The 180° mid-crossing reversal violates one-way-crossing priors, and the reversal executes precisely in the lane the ego's planner had just declared resolved, forcing replanning under launch pressure.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays launch ≥1.5 s after green when the reversal is detected; accelerates only after the pedestrian's body exits ego's lane footprint by ≥3 m laterally.
scenarios.trainingValue: Reversal and loitering behaviors are systematically underrepresented; this targets planner state-machine transitions (yield→proceed→re-yield).

scenarios.name: wardrobe-box-carrier-keypoint-loss
scenarios.description: A person carries a 1.8 m × 1 m wardrobe box across the street mid-block; the box hides arms, legs below the knee, and all head orientation cues.
scenarios.mechanism: Occluded keypoints defeat pose-based intent estimation — the visible signature is a featureless rectangle whose bulk velocity carries no limb-phase or gaze information, delaying crossing-intent classification by more than a second.
actors: adult carrying oversized flat-pack box, 1.1 m/s
scenarios.successSignature: Crossing intent recognized within 1 s of curb alignment even without pose cues; ego yields with ≥2 s TTC margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Keypoint-free fallback behavior — real deployments fail exactly when the pose network's assumptions (visible limbs/head) evaporate.

scenarios.name: long-ladder-corner-sweep
scenarios.description: Two workers carry a 6 m ladder horizontally around a building corner onto the roadway; the leading end sweeps across the ego lane while both carriers remain on the sidewalk.
scenarios.mechanism: Perception anchors on the carrier bodies, which never enter the road; the ladder tip intrudes as an unlabeled elongated object, producing a physical strike hazard with no pedestrian-region alert fired.
environment: building corner abutting a two-lane road
scenarios.successSignature: Ladder end detected as in-lane obstacle ≥1.5 s before sweep-through; ego slows or offsets laterally ≥0.8 m from the swept volume.
scenarios.trainingValue: Connected-object geometry: hazard extent decoupled from agent location — a systematic blind spot in region-gated safety monitors.

scenarios.name: dropped-phone-retrieval-crouch
scenarios.description: A pedestrian halfway through a legal crosswalk drops her phone, turns, crouches in lane 2, and reaches for it as the ego approaches on green.
scenarios.mechanism: The crouch collapses the standing-person detector template — height halves in ~0.7 s and the track often dies entirely — leaving a static low object indistinguishable from roadside clutter at classifier level.
scenarios.successSignature: Track retained (or re-associated within 0.3 s) through the crouch; full stop achieved with ≥1 m clearance from the crouched figure.
scenarios.trainingValue: Detector-template fragility under posture collapse is a top real-world dropout cause; pairs perception recovery with legal-priority logic.

scenarios.name: extendable-leash-lane-span
scenarios.description: A dog-walker halts at the curb, but a 3 m retractable leash lets the dog stand at the lane center circling; the thin leash spans the ego's path while both endpoints look harmless.
scenarios.mechanism: Dog and owner form separate tracks — one small and mobile, one stationary at the curb — and the taut tether between them is optically undetectable, creating a physical trip/strike line across the lane with no labeled hazard present.
actors: medium dog on 3 m retractable leash
approaching rideshare car in adjacent lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats the pair as one extended unit, holding ≥2.5 m standoff from the dog's instantaneous position and never crossing the implied leash segment.
scenarios.trainingValue: Relational reasoning over detectable endpoints to infer an undetectable connection — classic symbolic-composition gap in learned stacks.

scenarios.name: spooked-dog-owner-drag-down
scenarios.description: A car backfires; a leashed dog bolts across the road dragging its owner, who loses footing and slides into the lane behind it.
scenarios.mechanism: The acoustic impulse precedes any visual change by ~200 ms, and the bolt is maximal acceleration from rest (0→4 m/s in under a second) with a falling human attached — the fastest legal-scene onset from a stationary curb state.
environment: owner and dog on sidewalk verge
scenarios.successSignature: Reaction initiated within 250 ms of the acoustic event or first dog motion; stop completed with ≥1 m clearance to the fallen owner.
scenarios.trainingValue: Audio-visual causal triggering plus worst-case onset dynamics — measures raw end-to-end latency under a benign-looking baseline scene.

scenarios.name: courier-rounds-van-rear-doors
scenarios.description: A courier carrying two stacked boxes rounds the open rear doors of a double-parked delivery van straight into lane 1 without checking, the boxes blocking his own downward-forward view.
scenarios.mechanism: The van body occludes him until his torso clears the door plane roughly half a meter from the ego lane, and the cargo blocks his situational awareness, so neither party perceives the conflict before the ego's reaction window opens.
actors: delivery courier with two box stacks, 1.8 m/s
environment: lane 1 blocked by the van, ego passing at 30 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: First-visible-to-stop ≤1.2 s; lateral clearance ≥0.8 m or complete stop ≥1.5 m shy; no evasive swerve into the adjacent lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Double occlusion (ego's view and the pedestrian's own) is the compound structure behind most urban delivery-fatality mechanisms.

scenarios.name: gig-ebike-dismount-scuttle
scenarios.description: A food courier dismounts, leaves the e-bike standing in lane 1, and scuttles between queued cars toward a restaurant door while the unattended bike wobbles and topples.
scenarios.mechanism: One track forks into two divergent hazards: the rider becomes a fast low-visibility pedestrian weaving vehicle gaps while the riderless bike becomes a falling obstacle — the tracker must hand off cleanly or lose both.
scenarios.successSignature: Both entities tracked independently within 0.5 s of the fork; ego stops ≥2 m from the falling bike's sweep envelope and yields to the scuttling rider.
scenarios.trainingValue: Object-splitting events break identity persistence; this trains joint pedestrian-plus-prop dynamics from a single origin.

scenarios.name: dark-clothing-unlit-midblock-dash
scenarios.description: On an unlit collector at midnight, a pedestrian in a black jacket steps from between parked vehicles into a 55 km/h traffic lane with essentially zero retroreflectivity.
scenarios.mechanism: Camera detection range for ~5% reflectance clothing in an unlit scene drops below 15 m — under one second to collision at 55 km/h — so radar/LiDAR micro-motion must carry detection that vision structurally cannot.
environment: unlit arterial, no streetlights for 200 m
scenarios.successSignature: Non-visual modality detection at ≥20 m; controlled stop or ≥1.5 m offset achieved with required decel ≤6 m/s²; no high-jerk false panic on parked-car edges.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sensor-modality floor test: quantifies whether the stack survives its documented vision dark-zone rather than failing silently.

scenarios.name: umbrella-tilt-mutual-blind-jaywalk
scenarios.description: In heavy rain a pedestrian tilts his umbrella forward against the wind, blind to traffic, and steps off the curb into the ego lane 12 m out.
scenarios.mechanism: Mutual blindness compounds: his view of the ego is fully blocked so no yielding response will occur, and the wet canopy corrupts LiDAR returns and camera segmentation at head height, masking the walking body underneath.
actors: pedestrian with forward-tilted golf umbrella, 1.3 m/s
environment: arterial with curb-side bus stop nearby
scenarios.successSignature: Body-below-canopy detected by ≥1.5 s TTC; stop or offset executed without relying on any pedestrian-side response.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-degraded perception fused with a guaranteed-noncompliant actor — the pessimistic prior case for rain packages.

scenarios.name: speed-misjudge-commit-step
scenarios.description: A pedestrian looks directly at the ego from 60 m, judges it slower than its actual 50 km/h, and commits to a steady 1.4 m/s crossing of two lanes with no hesitation.
scenarios.mechanism: Direct eye contact reads socially as yielded priority, and his constant-velocity plan deterministically intersects the ego's lane at the moment of arrival — the conflict is fixed from commitment time yet invisible to models expecting pre-crossing hesitation.
scenarios.successSignature: Conflict identified via geometric intersection within 0.5 s of commitment; smooth decel ≥0.25 g begun ≥2.5 s before the crossing point; no harsh 0.6 g emergency event.
scenarios.trainingValue: Separates eye-contact-as-yield folklore from kinematic truth — trains planners to compute, not negotiate, mid-block conflicts.

scenarios.name: platoon-gap-dart-intersection
scenarios.description: A pedestrian darts through a 2 m gap between two trucks platooning through an intersection at 35 km/h, surfacing in the ego's adjacent lane and continuing across in front of the ego.
scenarios.mechanism: The lead truck occludes him until he emerges inside the inter-vehicle gap, granting under a second of visibility; his path is timed to vehicle gaps rather than signals, so signal-state priors predict nothing.
actors: pedestrian sprinting 3 m/s through vehicle gap
scenarios.successSignature: Recognition within 0.4 s of gap emergence; decel ≤5.5 m/s² achieving ≥0.5 m clearance, with no counter-steer into the truck.
scenarios.trainingValue: Vehicle-gap-timed crossing defeats both signal logic and occlusion compensation; measures worst-case latency at intersection boxes.

scenarios.name: legal-multilane-median-reversal-dash
scenarios.description: An older pedestrian legally starts crossing a four-lane arterial on Walk, strands himself at the narrow painted median as far lanes stay green, then dashes BACK across the ego's lane toward his origin during a brief platoon gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Ego's lane was verified empty and committed-through; the reversal from the median re-contaminates a lane the planner considered resolved milliseconds earlier, demanding rollback of an in-progress maneuver.
actors: older pedestrian, 1.0 m/s then 2.2 m/s dash
environment: four-lane arterial, 1 m painted median refuge
scenarios.successSignature: Reversal detected and ego decel initiated within 0.6 s; abort/hold executed without exceeding 5 m/s² and without rear-end-inducing jerk (>3 m/s³).
scenarios.trainingValue: Plan-rollback behavior — the hardest planner transition — exercised by a fully legal actor doing something legal-adjacent and lethal.

scenarios.name: rtor-apillar-late-reveal
scenarios.description: The ego turns right on red; a pedestrian crossing the side street lawfully on her Walk signal is hidden behind a stopped box truck until she is 4 m into the ego's turn arc.
scenarios.mechanism: Turn geometry plus the truck's box compress detection into the final degrees of the steering arc, and her legal priority means the ego must concede mid-turn with yaw rate already committed.
actors: stopped box truck occluding the near crosswalk
environment: truck in the adjacent queued lane
scenarios.successSignature: Yield executed within one control cycle of reveal; ego stops with ≥1 m clearance and yaw rate arrested ≤5°/s without swinging into the adjacent lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Committed-maneuver yielding under geometric occlusion — the defining RTOR crash mechanism for automated systems.

scenarios.name: countdown-sprint-final-lanes
scenarios.description: A pedestrian sprints at 3 m/s to finish a legal crossing as the countdown hits 1, entering the ego's outbound lane while the Walk indication is technically still displayed.
scenarios.mechanism: Entry speed triples the planner's extrapolated crossing-time error; using his initial 1.2 m/s pace, the position estimate at the critical moment is wrong by more than three meters, flipping a planned pass into a conflict.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed update reflected in prediction within 0.3 s; ego yields or offsets such that clearance ≥1 m despite a 3× velocity misestimate window.
scenarios.trainingValue: Adaptive velocity tracking on gait regime change — tests estimator bandwidth, not just policy.

scenarios.name: slip-lane-freeflow-no-yield-posture
scenarios.description: In a channelized free-flow right slip lane with a yield-marked crosswalk, a pedestrian crosses legally, upright and unhesitating, never glancing at the 30 km/h ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Geometry and yield-only signage provide no stopping cue, and the pedestrian's non-negotiating posture removes the usual mutual-adjustment dance — the conflict is purely geometric with zero behavioral warnings.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields with decel ≤3.5 m/s² initiated ≥2.5 s TTC before the crosswalk, independent of any pedestrian behavioral cue.
scenarios.trainingValue: Right-of-way compliance without social negotiation — catches systems that implicitly require pedestrian deference signals to brake politely.

scenarios.name: diagonal-desire-line-cut
scenarios.description: During a standard (non-scramble) walk phase, a commuter cuts the diagonal across the intersection, abandoning the crosswalk and exiting into the outbound lane the ego occupies.
scenarios.mechanism: Departure from the mapped crosswalk polygon mid-phase demotes him to generic-motion prediction, and his exit angle intersects the ego's lane from behind adjacent queued vehicles, hiding the trajectory bend.
actors: commuter with briefcase, diagonal cut at 1.7 m/s
queued vehicles at the near curb
scenarios.successSignature: Off-crosswalk deviation flagged within 0.5 s; ego's lane conflict resolved with ≥1.5 s TTC margin at his lane entry.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mapped-region dependence: prediction quality cliff at polygon boundaries is a known architectural weakness worth targeted data.

scenarios.name: family-split-median-regroup-dash
scenarios.description: A family of five crosses a six-lane road; three strand at the one-meter median, and when a platoon gap opens the stranded three — one carrying a toddler — dash to rejoin the others.
scenarios.mechanism: Group-cohesion motive overrides individual gap judgment, synchronizing multiple entries into the exact lane the ego's planner had already processed as cleared by the first three members.
actors: family of five, mixed ages, toddler carried
scenarios.successSignature: All five tracked as a related group; second-wave dash met with decel initiated ≥2 s TTC and clearance ≥1 m for every member including the carried toddler.
scenarios.trainingValue: Group-level intent (regrouping) as a causal driver of synchronized re-entry — individual-agent models miss the correlation structure.

scenarios.name: rideshare-hail-incremental-encroach
scenarios.description: A pedestrian waiting at a bus shelter steps into the bike lane waving at an approaching rideshare car, then backs progressively farther out as the car slows short of him.
scenarios.mechanism: Hailing posture encodes intent toward a vehicle, not the roadway, and his incremental retreat-steps track the stopping car — a continuously escalating encroachment that never produces a discrete lane-entry event to key on.
environment: bike lane between curb lane and travel lane
scenarios.successSignature: Encroachment envelope tracked continuously; ego holds ≥1 m clearance from his extremity throughout the hail sequence without full-stop oscillation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Continuous-threat modeling versus event-triggered logic — graded encroachment defeats threshold-based intervention designs.

scenarios.name: ambulance-gap-follower-stream
scenarios.description: Seconds after an ambulance runs the red light, three pedestrians cross through the intersection in its wake, against their Don't Walk indication.
scenarios.mechanism: The emergency vehicle's passage validates a perceived 'all-clear' gap, and followers enter from behind its body within one second — exploiting the same opening while their own signal still prohibits crossing.
actors: ambulance at speed, lights and siren
scenarios.successSignature: Followers detected despite fresh occlusion by the ambulance body; ego (with green) holds or yields with TTC ≥2 s to the last follower.
scenarios.trainingValue: Social-proof violation cascades: one rule-breaking leader recruits followers — tests whether prediction generalizes from norm-violation events.

scenarios.name: march-fragment-route-stray
scenarios.description: A permitted march fills the cross street; a six-person fragment waving flags drifts off the approved route into the ego's inbound lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Dense-cluster perception merges people and flags into one blob spanning the lane, individual trajectories become unobservable, and the fragment's drift is orthogonal to the march's mapped route, defeating route-conditioned priors.
environment: inbound lane adjacent to the march
scenarios.successSignature: Fragment separation from cluster tracked; ego stops ≥5 m short of the blob boundary and holds until the fragment clears or marshals intervene.
scenarios.trainingValue: Crowded-event partial breakdowns sit between crowd handling and individual tracking — a sparse training region with real incident history.

scenarios.name: vendor-bumper-hop-lane-one
scenarios.description: A windshield-washer vendor works car-to-car along stopped traffic and cuts between bumpers into moving lane 1 just as the ego passes the queue tail.
scenarios.mechanism: Stationary-among-cars context keeps him classified inert, and the inter-bumper hop is a sub-meter lateral displacement into live traffic executed in under a second with no approach phase to forecast.
actors: vendor with squeegee, hop at 2 m/s
environment: queue in lanes 2–3, ego in free lane 1 at 40 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Hop detected within 0.4 s; ego decel ≤5 m/s² achieving ≥0.8 m clearance; no lane change into queue traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Context-conditioned inertia assumptions (person among parked/queued cars is safe) are exactly how vendors and couriers get struck.

scenarios.name: panhandler-light-change-launch
scenarios.description: A panhandler circulating stopped cars at a red light is positioned between lanes 1 and 2 when the signal changes and traffic launches around him on both sides.
scenarios.mechanism: The phase change converts a protected pedestrian pocket into live traffic within about a second; his between-lane position hides him from lane-following planners until he stumbles clear of bumper shadows mid-launch.
environment: long red cycle at a major intersection
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays launch ≥1 s relative to platoon when the between-lane figure is detected; clearance ≥1 m maintained during his extraction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Green-wave launch discipline conditioned on residual in-lane pedestrians — a systematic fleet-wide risk at long cycles.

scenarios.name: skateboard-ramp-brake-fail-crossing
scenarios.description: A teenager rides a skateboard down a steep residential driveway, finds the damp pavement offers no foot-brake grip, and shoots across the sidewalk into the road 8 m ahead of the ego.
scenarios.mechanism: A sidewalk-region wheeled object inherits cyclist-class priors (predictable along-sidewalk travel); the driveway ramp converts him into a ballistic crossing at up to 15 km/h with no propulsion signature to re-classify on.
actors: teenager on skateboard, exit speed ~12–15 km/h
environment: steep driveway ramp meeting the sidewalk
scenarios.successSignature: Trajectory re-forecast at ramp mouth; ego achieves ≥1.5 m clearance or stop with decel ≤5.5 m/s² from 35 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Class-conditional motion priors misfiring on hybrid actors (pedestrian on wheels) — a recurring taxonomy gap in production ontologies.

scenarios.name: scooter-slide-lunge-chase
scenarios.description: A rider dismounts a shared e-scooter on the sidewalk, the kicked scooter slides across the curb ramp into the bike lane, and the rider immediately lunges after it.
scenarios.mechanism: A two-stage chained hazard: first a sliding object to which no agent model applies, then a lunging human whose trajectory mirrors the scooter's slide — prediction must propagate object physics into the human chase within ~0.7 s.
environment: sidewalk with curb ramp at a crossing
scenarios.successSignature: Chase trajectory anticipated from the slide vector; ego clears or stops with ≥1 m margin to both the scooter's rest point and the rider's path.
scenarios.trainingValue: Physics-chained secondary actors — cause propagates from object dynamics to human response, which decoupled predictors cannot compose.

scenarios.name: stroller-wheel-jam-midcross
scenarios.description: A parent's stroller front wheel jams on the curb-ramp lip mid-crossing; she spends four seconds wrestling it inside lane 1 as the ego's green phase begins.
scenarios.mechanism: The stall occurs inside the crosswalk after lawful entry, forcing the ego to override green-phase momentum assumptions, and the stroller's low frame hides the infant payload in ground-plane LiDAR shadow.
environment: signalized crossing with worn curb ramp
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds ≥1.5 s after green before creeping; stall recognized as immovable within 1 s and routed-around only with ≥1.2 m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Lawful-entry-then-disable events invert fault intuition and stress signal-compliance overrides plus low-child detection.

scenarios.name: toddler-lag-bolt-catchup
scenarios.description: A parent crosses on the Walk signal; a three-year-old lags six meters back at the curb, then bolts at 2.5 m/s across the ego's lane to catch up.
scenarios.mechanism: Sub-meter stature keeps the toddler below the bumper-line occlusion of queued vehicles until launch, and standstill-to-sprint burst acceleration leaves under one second between first visibility and lane center.
actors: queued sedans/SUVs at the near curb
scenarios.successSignature: Burst detected within 0.3 s of curb departure; stop achieved with decel ≤6 m/s² and ≥0.5 m clearance, no overcorrection into the parent.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion-height thresholds plus pediatric burst dynamics — the smallest, fastest-reacting actor class with the least warning.

scenarios.name: tourist-backstep-framing
scenarios.description: A tourist walks along the curb backwards while framing a photo of a landmark, stepping off the curb into lane 1 without ever facing the roadway.
scenarios.mechanism: Backward gait breaks heading-versus-body-orientation priors — the motion vector points into the lane while pose reads as sidewalk strolling, so orientation-anchored trajectory prediction lags reality by roughly a second.
actors: tourist with phone camera, backstepping 1 m/s
scenarios.successSignature: Lane intrusion projected from motion vector (not pose) within 0.5 s; ego offsets laterally ≥1 m or slows to ≤10 km/h during the backstep sequence.
scenarios.trainingValue: Orientation-independent motion estimation — pose-cue overfitting is a measurable, fixable failure axis this isolates cleanly.

scenarios.name: passenger-farside-bag-rejoin
scenarios.description: A rideshare passenger dropped at the curb realizes his bag is still in the car and jaywalks mid-block toward the vehicle now stopped in lane 2, curving his path to intercept it.
scenarios.mechanism: His goal is the vehicle itself, so his path bends with increasing urgency toward the neighboring lane — pedestrian prediction becomes coupled to the surrounding traffic state, which isolated-agent models ignore.
actors: ego passing in lane 1 at 40 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Intercept intent recognized via path curvature toward the stopped car; ego decel initiated ≥2 s TTC with clearance ≥1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Traffic-state-coupled pedestrian goals (chasing vehicles) — a feedback loop between ego-world prediction and actor intent.

scenarios.name: sidewalk-closure-cone-lane-back-to-traffic
scenarios.description: Construction closes the sidewalk and signs a detour routing pedestrians through a coned section of the curb lane at a 25 km/h limit; one walker follows the cone line with his back to the ego.
scenarios.mechanism: The occupancy is legally sanctioned, so the ego must treat the cone corridor as pedestrian space, yet the walker faces away (no gaze or yielding cues) and the cones themselves occlude his lateral drift toward live traffic.
actors: detoured pedestrian walking with traffic, 1.4 m/s
environment: urban work zone, sidewalk closure signage
scenarios.successSignature: Ego transits at ≤15 km/h holding ≥1 m from the cone line, tracking drift continuously; zero cone strikes and no unnecessary full stops.
scenarios.trainingValue: Legal-shared-space logic plus back-to-traffic actors — combines right-of-way nuance with degraded cue availability in one package.

scenarios.name: trash-day-bin-bypass-behind-truck
scenarios.description: On collection day, bins fully occupy the sidewalk, so a pedestrian steps into the travel lane around them, walking with traffic behind a stopped collection truck, then ducks back to the sidewalk after each bin cluster.
scenarios.mechanism: The collection truck occludes the pedestrian until the ego overtakes, his back-to-traffic posture gives no cue, and his sawtooth sidewalk-return pattern makes lane occupancy intermittent — unpredictable in-lane presence without a fixed path.
actors: waste collector at the truck's controls
environment: narrow residential street, bins every 10 m
scenarios.successSignature: Ego overtakes at ≤15 km/h with ≥1.2 m lateral clearance and anticipates at least one sidewalk-return without hard braking; no bin contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intermittent in-lane occupancy with occlusion rhythm — trains patience policies and overtaking gap logic on service days.

scenarios.name: ponded-curb-ramp-fan-out
scenarios.description: After heavy rain, the curb ramp at a crossing sits under 8 cm of ponded water; crossing pedestrians wade around it, fanning their paths up to 1.5 m beyond the crosswalk stripes into the ego's turn arc.
scenarios.mechanism: Standing water legally and practically displaces the crossing, so paths curve dynamically as each individual picks a personal dry line — a spread of trajectories outside mapped crosswalk polygons intersecting turning geometry.
actors: 4 pedestrians choosing individual detour lines, 1.0–1.5 m/s
environment: rain just ended, ego executing a right turn at 15 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Fan-out envelope respected: ego's turn path keeps ≥1 m from every pedestrian's actual curved line, requiring mid-turn radius adjustment of ≥1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Environment-forced path deformation — teaches that crosswalk geometry is a soft prior, not a hard invariant, under surface water conditions.

scenarios.name: snowbank-singlefile-lane-walk-dawn
scenarios.description: Plowed snowbanks leave a 40 cm sidewalk ledge, so three commuters walk single-file in the outer meter of the travel lane with their backs to the ego at dawn.
scenarios.mechanism: Sustained in-lane occupancy with zero escape room (a snowbank wall on one side) forbids the standard brake-and-swerve solution — the ego must execute a full opposing-lane pass or crawl indefinitely, testing constraint satisfaction rather than reflexes.
actors: 3 commuters single-file, 1.4 m/s, backs to traffic
environment: snowbanks 0.6 m high along the curb
dawn glare, -5°C, salted lane surface, 40 km/h limit
scenarios.successSignature: Full opposing-lane pass completed only with confirmed-opposing-clear (headway ≥3 s) and ≥1 m clearance, else sustained ≤10 km/h follow; zero snowbank contact by pedestrians.
scenarios.trainingValue: No-escape-room encounters eliminate evasion as an option and expose planner deadlock/handling of indefinite low-speed constraints.

scenarios.name: paratransit-lift-lane-extension
scenarios.description: A wheelchair-accessible van curbside (no bus bay) deploys its lift platform with an attendant assisting a boarding passenger, extending 1.2 m into lane 1 for the ~90-second operation.
scenarios.mechanism: A quasi-static but unexpected structure with a fragile occupant occupies the lane; the challenge is long-duration negotiation around a non-vehicle obstacle that map and planner layers classify as transient and therefore handle badly.
environment: lane 1 partially blocked, ego diverting at 30 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Diversion executed with ≥0.5 m clearance from the lift envelope and attendant; no stop-and-go churn (≤2 speed dips) across the 90 s window.
scenarios.trainingValue: Minute-scale static hazards with human occupants blur the vehicle/pedestrian/structure taxonomy and punish transient-obstacle assumptions.

scenarios.name: hospital-gurney-emergency-cross
scenarios.description: Two staff rush a patient on a gurney across the hospital ambulance-drive entrance at a jogging pace while one staffer waves the ego down mid-push.
scenarios.mechanism: Simultaneous hand-signal control and a high-speed low-agility crossing (gurney wheels resist course correction) mean the wave-down gesture must preempt the ego's right-of-way, and the gurney cannot dodge if the ego errs.
scenarios.successSignature: Wave-down honored with stop initiated within one cycle; ≥2 m standoff held until gurney fully clears; no reliance on gurney course corrections.
scenarios.trainingValue: Institutional hand-signal authority in a non-work-zone context plus a rigid, non-evasive multi-party actor — special-site generalization test.

scenarios.name: stadium-exit-gate-density-spill
scenarios.description: After a match, the crowd exits through a gate emptying directly onto the roadway shoulder; a density wave pushes dozens outward until the front rank stands inside lane 1 regardless of individual intent.
scenarios.mechanism: Crowd pressure produces motion decoupled from personal decisions — individuals are displaced into the lane at walking pace with no entry decision to detect, and per-agent tracking collapses above roughly two persons per square meter.
actors: crowd of 50+ exiting, front rank in lane 1
environment: stadium exit gate onto a four-lane street
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥5 m from the crowd front and holds; no creep into the density mass and no isolation of false individuals inside the blob; resumes only on marshal clearance or genuine gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Density-wave mechanics where agency is distributed — the anti-pattern for per-agent prediction and the strongest argument for crowd-level policies.

scenarios.name: transfer-sprint-fourlane-beeline
scenarios.description: A bus pulls away from a far-side stop; a passenger sprints from the near side diagonally across four mid-block lanes at 4 m/s to flag it, entering the ego's lane on a straight beeline.
scenarios.mechanism: A fixed external goal generates maximum-speed, straight-line traffic disregard, and ego and sprinter converge on the same point — sprint gait resists mid-course correction, so avoidance burden falls entirely on the ego with sub-two-second margins.
environment: four-lane arterial, mid-block near a far-side stop
scenarios.successSignature: Convergence computed within 0.5 s of sprint onset; decel profile lands ego ≥2 m behind his path with ≤5.5 m/s² peak and no lane-change into adjacent traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Goal-object-driven maximum-urgency crossings define the upper bound of pedestrian speed distributions and pure-ego responsibility splits.

scenarios.name: queue-filter-cyclist-light-change
scenarios.description: Cyclist filters forward between two lanes of cars stopped at a red light, then cuts diagonally into the crosswalk/bike lane the moment the light turns green.
scenarios.mechanism: Queue filtering puts the cyclist beside ego's front fender where mirrors and cameras lose track; the signal change triggers a sudden diagonal move into ego's launch path with under 1m lateral clearance.
actors: cyclist filtering between queued cars at 10-15 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego tracks cyclist through occlusion and yields launch by >=1.5s or holds >=1.0m lateral gap while cyclist clears.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers the highest-severity cyclist conflict: occlusion during queue filtering plus signal-timed emergence.

scenarios.name: dooring-passenger-side-bike-lane
scenarios.description: Passenger in a rideshare parked in a bike lane swings the door open as ego overtakes, directly into the cyclist's and ego's path.
scenarios.mechanism: Door sweep occupies the entire bike lane within ~0.8s; an overtaking ego at 40 km/h has ~2s from door-crack visibility to impact, demanding immediate brake-and-steer-out decision.
environment: urban street with bike lane adjacent to parking
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates to <=15 km/h or achieves >=1.2m clearance from door sweep zone; no contact with door or cyclist.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dooring is a top-5 urban cyclist fatality mechanism and forces joint ego-cyclist avoidance reasoning.

scenarios.name: dooring-chain-cyclist-deflect
scenarios.description: A parked car door opens into the bike lane ahead of a cyclist, who swerves left to avoid it and enters ego's travel lane at closing speed.
scenarios.mechanism: The door strike forces the cyclist's evasive swerve; ego's demand is not the door but the cyclist's unplanned 1.5m lateral excursion at ~20 km/h with 10m gap.
actors: cyclist in bike lane at 20 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to keep TTC >=1.5s as cyclist enters lane; lateral clearance >=0.8m at pass.
scenarios.trainingValue: Second-order hazard: AV must anticipate cyclist reaction to a door, not just track the door itself.

scenarios.name: bike-lane-ends-forced-merge
scenarios.description: Painted bike lane terminates 30m before an intersection, forcing the cyclist to merge into ego's 50 km/h lane with a shoulder check and hand signal.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane drop converts a separated cyclist into a same-lane vehicle; the merge happens over ~2s while ego approaches from behind at 25 km/h relative speed.
actors: cyclist merging from ended bike lane at 22 km/h
environment: bike lane ending at intersection approach
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields gap >=15m or decelerates >=2 m/s^2 to open >=1.5m passing clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests yielding to vulnerable road users during lane-drop merges where right-of-way is ambiguous.

scenarios.name: escooter-wrongway-sidewalk-curb-cut
scenarios.description: E-scooter rider travels against traffic on the sidewalk at 20 km/h, then drops off a curb cut diagonally into ego's lane mid-block.
scenarios.mechanism: Wrong-way sidewalk travel defeats direction-based prediction; the curb-cut descent produces a sudden 3m lateral + 2m longitudinal entry into ego's path with zero warning signals.
actors: e-scooter on sidewalk moving against traffic at 20 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves required decel <=4 m/s^2 with TTC >=1.5s at curb-drop detection; no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Counter-flow micromobility is a leading cause of mid-block urban collisions; tests non-canonical approach vectors.

scenarios.name: cyclist-left-hook-from-right
scenarios.description: Cyclist riding to the right of ego in the same lane suddenly turns left across ego's front, executing a vehicular-style left turn from the rightmost position.
scenarios.mechanism: The left turn from the right edge crosses ego's entire lane width (~3.5m) in ~2.5s while ego travels 35 km/h; no signal is given until the turn starts.
actors: cyclist at 18 km/h turning left from right edge
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to <=12 km/h before cyclist crosses ego's centerline path; lateral miss >=0.5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Classic 'left hook' fatality pattern; tests prediction of crossing-intent from edge-position riders.

scenarios.name: moto-lanesplit-queue-delta
scenarios.description: Motorcycle splits between ego's lane and the adjacent lane through stopped traffic at 55 km/h while cars move at 10 km/h, closing at 45 km/h differential.
scenarios.mechanism: The 45 km/h speed differential in a 1.2m gap leaves <1s from first detection to pass; any queue surge or mirror-stick-out shrinks the gap below motorcycle width.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds lane position (no drift toward gap) and does not accelerate while motorcycle is within 2m lateral.
scenarios.trainingValue: Distinct from highway high-speed splitting: queue environment tests micro-gap maintenance and non-drift policy.

scenarios.name: child-cyclist-wobble-stop
scenarios.description: A child cyclist ahead wobbles with 0.5m lateral oscillation at 12 km/h, then stops abruptly without warning to look at something on the sidewalk.
scenarios.mechanism: Child steering instability produces unpredictable lateral variance while the sudden stop collapses ego's closing distance from 15m to near-zero in 2.7s at 30 km/h.
actors: child cyclist ~8 years old at 12 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=1.0m lateral offset through wobble and stops with >=1.5m gap at the sudden halt.
scenarios.trainingValue: Child riders combine high lateral variance with zero signaling; a distinct instability model from adult cyclists.

scenarios.name: group-ride-abreast-narrow-rural
scenarios.description: Six cyclists ride two-abreast occupying the full 3m rural lane at 25 km/h; ego approaches at 70 km/h with oncoming traffic preventing a full-lane pass.
scenarios.mechanism: The abreast group blocks the only passing gap; ego must decelerate from 70 to ~25 km/h and trail the group until the oncoming lane clears, ~8s of constrained following.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates to match group speed with >=1.5s headway and passes only with full opposing-lane clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Rural group rides create long-duration passing constraints; tests patience policy vs risky partial-lane pass.

scenarios.name: cyclist-occluded-parked-van-intersection
scenarios.description: A cyclist riding between parked cars is fully occluded by a delivery van, then appears 5m before the intersection crossing ego's path with right-of-way.
scenarios.mechanism: The van blocks ego's view of the bike lane for ~40m; the cyclist emerges into the intersection at 20 km/h exactly when ego's green light begins, giving <1.5s TTC.
actors: cyclist occluded by parked van at 20 km/h
environment: parking lane adjacent to bike lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays launch >=1.0s after green or creeps at <=8 km/h until intersection is confirmed clear.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion-then-emergence at signalized intersections is the deadliest right-hook geometry for cyclists.

scenarios.name: cargo-bike-lane-blocking
scenarios.description: A 1.2m-wide loaded cargo bike travels at 15 km/h occupying the entire narrow lane, with parked cars preventing ego from achieving a legal 1.5m pass.
scenarios.mechanism: Cargo-bike width plus parked-car buffer leaves <0.5m passing gap; ego must follow at 15 km/h for 200m until a passing bay appears, resisting the urge to squeeze.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego trails at >=1.5s headway and passes only where lateral clearance >=1.5m is achievable.
scenarios.trainingValue: Width-variant VRU: same cyclist class, different geometry envelope; tests pass/no-pass threshold policy.

scenarios.name: delivery-rider-abrupt-stop
scenarios.description: A food-delivery rider in the bike lane brakes from 25 km/h to zero in 1.5s to check a phone order notification, mid-block with ego following at 40 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Delivery economics cause unpredictable mid-block stops; ego closes from 15m gap to 3m in ~1.4s, requiring emergency decel >=6 m/s^2 if detection is late.
actors: delivery cyclist with insulated backpack at 25 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects decel within 0.5s onset and stops with >=1.0m gap; required decel <=5 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gig-economy stop behavior is now a dominant urban cyclist pattern with distinctive backpack appearance cues.

scenarios.name: cyclist-pothole-swerve-into-lane
scenarios.description: Cyclist in the bike lane swerves sharply left to avoid a pothole, entering ego's lane 8m ahead as ego closes at 45 km/h in light rain.
scenarios.mechanism: Road-surface defect causes a 1.5m lateral excursion with ~0.4s of steer-in; wet pavement extends ego's stopping distance, compressing TTC to ~0.9s.
actors: cyclist at 22 km/h swerving around pothole
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves TTC >=1.5s via combined brake and lateral offset; pothole location correctly attributed as cause.
scenarios.trainingValue: Couples infrastructure defects with cyclist kinematics; tests causal anticipation from road-surface perception.

scenarios.name: moto-dark-clothing-night-rural
scenarios.description: Motorcyclist in all-black gear with no headlight on an unlit rural road is detected only by faint retroreflection at 120m as ego closes at 80 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Near-zero visual signature delays first detection until ~5.4s to impact; the motorcycle's small frontal area and absent illumination give no early cue.
actors: motorcycle at 45 km/h in black gear, headlight off
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects and initiates decel by 100m range; passes with >=1.5m clearance at <=50 km/h differential.
scenarios.trainingValue: Nighttime low-conspicuity motorcycles stress long-range perception fusion beyond camera-only limits.

scenarios.name: ebike-moped-speed-misjudgment
scenarios.description: Class-3 e-bike in the bike lane looks like a standard bicycle but travels at 45 km/h; ego turning right across the bike lane misjudges its arrival time.
scenarios.mechanism: Appearance-based speed priors fail: ego's turn gap computed for a 20 km/h bicycle is half the required gap, producing ~0.8s TTC as the e-bike arrives.
actors: class-3 e-bike at 45 km/h in bike lane
environment: urban intersection with protected bike lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields: turn aborted or delayed until e-bike passes with >=2.0s margin; no crossing conflict.
scenarios.trainingValue: Appearance-speed decoupling is a core micromobility perception challenge; e-bikes break bicycle speed priors.

scenarios.name: cyclist-no-lights-night-urban
scenarios.description: Unlit cyclist in dark clothing rides in the bike lane at 25 km/h at night; ego at 50 km/h detects only when headlights illuminate the bike at 60m.
scenarios.mechanism: Retroreflective-free cyclist gives 4.3s detection-to-impact; ego must rely on intermittent illumination between streetlights, causing detection flicker.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=1.5m lateral clearance and adjusts speed within 1s of first detection despite flicker.
scenarios.trainingValue: Unlit-cyclist night riding is a persistent real-world pattern; tests tracking under intermittent illumination.

scenarios.name: delivery-scooter-red-run-cross
scenarios.description: Delivery moped on the cross street runs a stale red at 50 km/h just after ego's light turns green, crossing ego's launch path.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal-phase timing exploits: the rider accelerates on the stale amber, arriving in the intersection 0.5s after ego's green, giving ego <1.2s to react at launch.
actors: delivery moped running red at 50 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds or creeps for >=1.5s after green until cross traffic is confirmed stopped.
scenarios.trainingValue: Green-light launch is the highest-exposure AV moment; delivery riders disproportionately run stale signals.

scenarios.name: salmon-cyclist-head-on-bike-lane
scenarios.description: Wrong-way cyclist rides head-on toward ego in the bike lane at 20 km/h while a parked car blocks any lateral escape for either party.
scenarios.mechanism: Contraflow cycling produces 65 km/h closing speed in a 1.5m bike lane; the parked car removes the cyclist's escape and ego's lane change is blocked by adjacent traffic.
actors: parked car adjacent to bike lane
environment: urban one-way street with contraflow bike riding
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to <=15 km/h and achieves >=0.8m clearance; no lane change into adjacent traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Head-on VRU closure in constrained geometry tests joint escape-reasoning, not just braking.

scenarios.name: cyclist-fall-wet-tram-track
scenarios.description: Cyclist's front wheel catches a wet tram track groove angled 20 degrees to travel, dumping the rider sideways into ego's lane 10m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: The track groove steers the wheel and causes a low-side fall in ~0.3s; the rider slides 2-3m across the lane boundary while ego closes at 40 km/h.
environment: urban street with embedded tram tracks
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops with >=2m gap to fallen rider; fall predicted from track-cyclist geometry >=0.5s before contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Falling-rider dynamics (slide, not steer) demand a different avoidance model than swerving riders.

scenarios.name: moto-hard-brake-ahead
scenarios.description: Motorcycle ahead in ego's lane brakes hard (8 m/s^2) to avoid a lane-change car; motorcycle decelerates twice as fast as ego comfortably can.
scenarios.mechanism: Motorcycle braking capability exceeds ego's, inverting normal following assumptions; ego's 25m gap closes to 8m in 1.5s despite immediate ego braking.
actors: car cutting in ahead of motorcycle
scenarios.successSignature: Ego matches decel within 0.3s of motorcycle brake-light onset; gap >=3m at resolution.
scenarios.trainingValue: Heterogeneous braking envelopes in platoons; motorcycle-specific decel priors must not be car-tuned.

scenarios.name: skateboarder-low-profile-crossing
scenarios.description: Teenager sits on a skateboard and rolls across a mid-block crosswalk at 12 km/h; seated posture gives a sub-0.8m silhouette partially hidden by a parked SUV.
scenarios.mechanism: Seated skateboarder combines pedestrian crossing behavior with vehicle-like speed; low profile plus SUV occlusion delays detection to ~2s before crossing ego's path.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields with TTC >=1.5s at emergence; classifies skateboarder as yielding-obligation VRU.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-profile seated micromobility blurs pedestrian/vehicle classification with direct right-of-way consequences.

scenarios.name: bike-trailer-wide-sweep
scenarios.description: Cyclist towing a child trailer sweeps 0.9m into the adjacent lane while rounding a corner, crossing ego's oncoming path at the apex.
scenarios.mechanism: Trailer off-tracking widens the cyclist's effective turn radius; the trailer's outer wheel crosses the centerline exactly where ego's corner-cutting trajectory peaks.
actors: cyclist with child trailer at 12 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds outside line with >=1.0m clearance from trailer sweep envelope.
scenarios.trainingValue: Articulated VRU width dynamics; trailer off-tracking is invisible to width-based pass planners.

scenarios.name: courier-gap-thread-parked-trucks
scenarios.description: Bike courier rides the 1m gap between double-parked box trucks and ego's moving lane at 25 km/h, appearing and disappearing between vehicles.
scenarios.mechanism: Intermittent occlusion between trucks breaks tracking; the courier's line weaves 0.8m laterally with each truck gap, ending with a sudden emergence into ego's lane edge.
actors: courier threading truck gap at 25 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=0.8m clearance at every emergence; tracking persists through >=3 occlusion events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intermittent-occlusion tracking through urban canyons is a persistent perception-continuity failure mode.

scenarios.name: abandoned-escooter-forces-detour
scenarios.description: Shared e-scooters dumped across the bike lane force the cyclist to merge around them into ego's 45 km/h lane at a blind spot created by a bus stop.
scenarios.mechanism: The scooter obstacle displaces the cyclist exactly where the bus shelter blocks ego's sightline; the merge occurs with <1.5s TTC from ego's approach.
actors: cyclist at 20 km/h detouring around fallen scooters
environment: urban bike lane near transit stop
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields or offsets laterally with TTC >=1.5s; correctly attributes causation to scooter obstacle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Static micromobility obstacles create dynamic cyclist displacements; chained-causation reasoning.

scenarios.name: cyclist-stop-sign-blowout-blind
scenarios.description: Cyclist on the cross street rolls through a stop sign at 25 km/h at a sight-line-limited intersection just as ego enters at 40 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Cyclist stop compliance is statistically low; the building-corner sightline gives ego only ~1.8s of pre-entry visibility of the cross-street bike approach.
actors: cyclist crossing at 25 km/h without stopping
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects cyclist pre-entry and delays or brakes to achieve >=1.5s TTC margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low cyclist stop compliance must be encoded in intersection-entry priors, not assumed law-abiding.

scenarios.name: moto-wheelie-adjacent-lane
scenarios.description: Motorcyclist pops a wheelie in the adjacent lane at 60 km/h; the raised front end eliminates headlight aim and adds 0.5m of vertical profile variance.
scenarios.mechanism: The stunt changes the motorcycle's detection signature (headlight pitches up, profile elongates) exactly when ego attempts a lane change into that lane.
actors: ego attempting lane change at 60 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts lane change; no lateral closure within 1.0m of motorcycle envelope.
scenarios.trainingValue: Non-canonical vehicle postures break template-based motorcycle detection at lane-change decision points.

scenarios.name: school-kids-bike-scatter
scenarios.description: Five children on bicycles exit a school gate and scatter across the road in diverging directions at 10-15 km/h as ego approaches at 30 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Diverging trajectories from a single emergence point defeat single-threat modeling; each child's path has independent lateral variance while ego must clear the whole swarm.
actors: five child cyclists diverging at 10-15 km/h
environment: suburban school gate on residential street
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops before the first child's path and holds until all five clear; no creep through the swarm.
