scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-actor diverging VRU swarms require set-based safety, not per-actor tracking.

scenarios.name: cyclist-drafting-bus-overtake
scenarios.description: Cyclist drafts 1m behind a moving city bus, fully hidden, then pulls out to overtake the bus as it decelerates toward a stop, entering ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The bus body occludes the cyclist for ~50m; bus deceleration triggers the overtake exactly when ego's passing gap is minimal, yielding ~1.2s TTC.
actors: cyclist at 28 km/h drafting then overtaking bus
environment: bike lane ending at bus zone
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates overtake from bus decel and opens >=1.5m clearance or decelerates >=3 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Drafting-then-overtake is a common cyclist pattern around transit; occlusion plus triggered emergence.

scenarios.name: sidewalk-rideout-between-cars
scenarios.description: Cyclist rides on the sidewalk and shoots out from between two parked cars across a driveway-adjacent sidewalk, crossing ego's lane at 18 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Parked cars create a 2m visibility slot; the cyclist's emergence speed gives ego at 35 km/h ~1.6s from first visibility to path conflict.
actors: two parked cars framing the gap
environment: urban residential street with sidewalk ride-out point
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves >=1.5s TTC via pre-brake at the known ride-out geometry; clearance >=0.8m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Ride-out geometry is a top urban child-cyclist fatality pattern; tests gap-scanning at occlusion slots.

scenarios.name: moto-filter-green-launch
scenarios.description: Motorcycle filters to the front between lanes at a red light; when the light turns green it launches at 2x ego's acceleration, cutting across ego's front from the gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Filtering position puts the motorcycle 0.5m ahead of ego's front bumper in the inter-lane gap; its superior launch crosses ego's lane within 1.5s of green.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays full-throttle launch >=1.5s and tracks the motorcycle's cross-lane path to clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Front-filtered motorcycles invert launch priority; ego must yield its own green to the gap occupant.

scenarios.name: cyclist-downhill-overspeed-intersection
scenarios.description: Cyclist descends an 8% grade reaching 55 km/h in a 30 km/h zone and cannot brake in time at the blind intersection at the bottom, entering on red.
scenarios.mechanism: Grade-driven overspeed exceeds the cyclist's braking envelope; entry speed at the intersection is 20 km/h above ego's approach assumption, halving available gap.
actors: cyclist descending at 55 km/h unable to stop
environment: urban hill with 8% descent into signalized intersection
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects high-speed approach and clears or brakes to achieve >=2.0s margin; grade correctly weighted in prediction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grade-corrupted speed priors: same-looking cyclist, radically different arrival kinematics.

scenarios.name: recumbent-handcycle-low-profile
scenarios.description: A recumbent hand-cycle rider travels in the bike lane at 25 km/h with a 0.9m-tall silhouette that ego's detector initially classifies as debris or shadow.
scenarios.mechanism: Sub-meter profile defeats cyclist height priors; misclassification delays yielding until ego is within 20m at 45 km/h closing speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct VRU classification by 60m range; pass with >=1.5m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Rare low-profile human-powered vehicles test classification robustness with legal road rights.

scenarios.name: escooter-two-riders-unstable
scenarios.description: Two riders share one e-scooter at 22 km/h; the rear passenger's shifting weight produces 0.7m lateral oscillation and a sudden foot-down wobble into ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Overloading doubles the scooter's instability variance; the foot-down recovery event is an unplanned 1m lateral excursion with 0.3s onset at 10m ahead of ego.
actors: doubled e-scooter at 22 km/h with two riders
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=1.2m clearance through oscillation; emergency decel <=5 m/s^2 at foot-down event.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-occupant micromobility is illegal but common; instability variance exceeds single-rider models.

scenarios.name: cyclist-oversized-load-ladder
scenarios.description: Cyclist carries a 4m ladder horizontally, extending 1.5m past the rear into ego's lane edge while riding at 18 km/h in a narrow street.
scenarios.mechanism: The load projects a rigid 1.5m overhang that sweeps with every steering correction; ego's passing envelope computed from rider width alone under-clears the overhang by 0.7m.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pass envelope includes load projection; clearance >=0.8m from ladder tip.
scenarios.trainingValue: Carried-load geometry extends VRU collision envelopes beyond body width; visible but easy to mis-model.

scenarios.name: moto-stalled-night-lane
scenarios.description: Motorcycle stalls mid-lane at night with no lights (dead battery) on a 60 km/h road; rider stands beside it waving, both nearly invisible until 50m.
scenarios.mechanism: Dead electricals remove tail light and headlight; the combination of stalled vehicle plus standing rider presents a 0.5m-wide double obstacle detected at ~3s to impact.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects by 80m (radar/lidar fusion) and achieves lane change or stop with >=2s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dark stalled two-wheelers are the hardest night obstacle class; tests sensor-modality fusion beyond headlights.

scenarios.name: door-strike-fall-chain
scenarios.description: A car door opens 15m ahead of a cyclist who cannot swerve due to adjacent traffic; the door clips the rider who falls across the lane boundary into ego's path at 35 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Constrained cyclist has no escape, so the door contact converts to a lateral fall; the sliding rider crosses into ego's lane 0.5s after door opening, with ego 12m out.
actors: cyclist struck by door falling left
environment: urban street with bike lane and dense parking
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to stop >=2m before fallen rider; door-cyclist conflict predicted >=0.4s before contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Full causal chain: door causes strike causes fall causes ego threat; tests multi-event anticipation.

scenarios.name: truck-buffered-bike-merge-blind
scenarios.description: Cyclist merges around a stopped delivery truck blocking the bike lane at the exact point ego passes in the adjacent lane, hidden by the truck's 3m box until 6m.
scenarios.mechanism: The truck occludes the merge point from both parties; cyclist emerges mid-merge into ego's lane edge with ~1.0s TTC at ego's 40 km/h.
actors: ego at 40 km/h in adjacent lane
cyclist merging around truck at 18 km/h
stopped delivery truck in bike lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pre-brakes at truck-blocked bike lanes and achieves >=1.5s TTC or >=1.0m clearance at emergence.
scenarios.trainingValue: Truck-blocked bike lanes are the standard urban merge-conflict geometry; occlusion symmetry fools both actors.

scenarios.name: roundabout-cyclist-diagonal-exit
scenarios.description: Cyclist in a roundabout's bike lane exits diagonally across ego's entry path at the yield line while ego commits to entry at 30 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Roundabout exits force cyclists to cross vehicle entry paths at 30-45 degree angles; the diagonal crossing extends conflict duration to ~2s while ego's entry commitment blocks braking geometry.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields at entry until cyclist's exit path clears; entry aborted or delayed with >=1.5s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Roundabout-cyclist geometry is underrepresented and has unique diagonal conflict vectors.

scenarios.name: moto-split-merge-zone-conflict
scenarios.description: Motorcycle lane-splits through a freeway merge zone exactly as a car merges into the gap the motorcycle occupies, forcing the moto into ego's lane at 100 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: The merging car compresses the split gap; the motorcycle's emergency lateral escape lands 0.5m inside ego's lane at 40 km/h relative speed with 1.2s TTC.
actors: motorcycle splitting at 120 km/h forced left
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects moto lateral displacement and opens >=0.8m within 0.5s; no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound interaction (split + merge) produces escape vectors no single-actor model predicts.

scenarios.name: rural-cyclist-no-shoulder-truck-push
scenarios.description: Cyclist rides on a 0.3m rural shoulder as an oncoming logging truck's mirror sweep forces the cyclist to veer into ego's 80 km/h lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Oncoming wide-vehicle aerodynamics and mirror projection remove the shoulder margin; the cyclist's forced veer enters ego's lane 12m ahead with ~1.3s TTC.
actors: cyclist on narrow shoulder at 25 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to <=45 km/h and passes with >=1.2m clearance after truck clears; anticipates veer from oncoming width.
scenarios.trainingValue: Rural VRU squeeze: the threat is created by a third party's geometry, requiring two-vehicle anticipation.

scenarios.name: electric-unicycle-silent-wrongway
scenarios.description: Rider on an electric unicycle travels 35 km/h against traffic in the bike lane at night; silent, narrow, and with a single point light source.
scenarios.mechanism: Single-point light at 35 km/h contraflow gives a closing speed of 75 km/h with an ambiguous signature; ego's classifier has no unicycle prior and delays response 0.8s.
scenarios.successSignature: Detection by 70m; ego achieves >=1.5s TTC and >=1.0m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Novel micromobility classes with no training prior; tests open-set classification under time pressure.

scenarios.name: cyclist-right-turn-conflict-oncoming
scenarios.description: Cyclist ahead of ego turns right across the path of oncoming traffic, hesitates mid-turn, and stops in ego's lane as ego approaches at 40 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Mid-turn hesitation from gap misjudgment parks the cyclist in ego's travel lane; ego's 40 m/s-to-stop distance from 40m gap leaves ~2.2s to resolve.
actors: oncoming car the cyclist yields to
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops with >=1.5m gap; hesitation recognized as stop-intent within 0.5s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mid-maneuver hesitation creates hybrid stationary/moving threat states rarely covered in cyclist models.

scenarios.name: bike-path-driveway-backing-suv
scenarios.description: On a shared-use path crossing a commercial driveway, an SUV backs out across the path just as ego drives past on the adjacent road, pushing a cyclist into ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The backing SUV compresses the path; the cyclist's emergency stop-and-swerve displaces them 1.5m into the roadway where ego passes at 40 km/h.
actors: cyclist on path at 20 km/h displaced by SUV
environment: road adjacent to shared-use path crossing a commercial driveway
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates cyclist displacement from backing vehicle; clearance >=1.0m or decel to <=20 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Three-actor chained displacement across path-road boundary; driveway crossings couple two road users' fates.

scenarios.name: moto-group-stagger-compression
scenarios.description: Five motorcycles in staggered formation at 90 km/h compress abruptly when the leader brakes for debris; the last bike swerves into ego's adjacent lane 8m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: Staggered formations have 2m inter-bike gaps that collapse in chain-reaction braking; the tail bike's swerve crosses the lane line at 30 km/h relative to ego.
environment: rural highway two lanes same direction
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects formation compression and opens >=1.0m lateral within 0.6s of leader brake onset.
scenarios.trainingValue: Group braking dynamics propagate threat backward; formation-aware prediction beats per-bike tracking.

scenarios.name: cyclist-dusk-reflective-void
scenarios.description: Cyclist at dusk wears clothing with reflective strips only on the back; viewed from ego's side angle during a pass, the rider disappears into background clutter for 1.5s.
scenarios.mechanism: Directional retroreflectivity creates angle-dependent visibility; the lateral pass geometry hits the reflective void exactly when ego's lane-change decision is pending.
actors: cyclist with rear-only reflectives at 22 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Tracking persists through the low-visibility window; no lane change within 2m of cyclist during pass.
scenarios.trainingValue: View-angle-dependent conspicuity breaks static appearance models; temporal tracking must bridge dropouts.

scenarios.name: ebike-crosswalk-speed-conflict
scenarios.description: E-bike rider uses the pedestrian crosswalk at 30 km/h, arriving at ego's turning path 3x faster than pedestrian walk models predict, from behind a waiting truck.
scenarios.mechanism: Crosswalk-position priors assume 1.2-1.8 m/s; the e-bike's 8 m/s from truck occlusion compresses ego's turning gap from a comfortable 4s to 0.9s TTC.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats crosswalk occupants speed-agnostically; yields with >=2.0s margin regardless of assumed mode.
scenarios.trainingValue: Crosswalk speed-prior violation is a growing e-bike injury pattern; mode-agnostic yielding is the safe policy.

scenarios.name: cyclist-track-stand-intersection
scenarios.description: Cyclist arrives at a busy intersection, track-stands (balancing stationary) in ego's lane edge for 6 seconds, then darts forward through a gap ego was also committing to.
scenarios.mechanism: Track-stand state is ambiguous between yielding and preparing to go; the dart occurs within 0.3s and crosses ego's path 5m ahead at 35 km/h closing speed.
actors: track-standing cyclist then darting at 15 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego does not commit to the gap while cyclist is within 3m laterally; yields with >=1.5s margin at dart.
scenarios.trainingValue: Ambiguous stationary-intent states require intent inference, not just trajectory extrapolation.

scenarios.name: moped-parking-lane-pullout-gap
scenarios.description: Moped parked in a parking lane pulls into a 12m gap in traffic at full acceleration just as ego closes the same gap at 45 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Moped acceleration (~3 m/s^2) fills the gap in 2.5s while ego covers 12m in 1s; the shared-gap conflict yields ~1.1s TTC unless ego anticipates the pullout.
actors: moped pulling from parking lane at accelerating speed
scenarios.successSignature: Ego covers the gap or brakes to achieve >=1.5s TTC; pullout anticipated from moped indicator/wheel angle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Parking-lane pullouts by powered two-wheelers close gaps faster than bicycle models allow.

scenarios.name: cyclist-gravel-corner-lowside-slide
scenarios.description: Cyclist descending a rural gravel corner at 35 km/h low-sides on loose gravel, sliding 4m across the centerline into ego's ascending path at 50 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Loose-surface cornering exceeds tire grip and produces an uncontrolled slide; the slide vector crosses the centerline 15m ahead of ego with ~1.5s to conflict.
actors: cyclist sliding from gravel corner at 35 km/h
environment: rural gravel descent with blind corner
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes and steers to achieve >=1.5m miss distance from slide path; corner flagged as high-risk pre-encounter.
scenarios.trainingValue: Falling-then-sliding dynamics on loose surfaces extend cyclist threat models beyond the bike's footprint.

scenarios.name: bikeshare-novice-umbrella-crosswind
scenarios.description: First-time bike-share rider holds an umbrella in one hand in 30 km/h crosswind gusts, producing 1m lateral excursions and a gust-driven veer into ego's lane edge.
scenarios.mechanism: One-handed control plus gust loading makes steering corrections late and overshooting; a gust at 8m ahead veers the rider 1m into ego's lane with 0.4s onset.
actors: novice bike-share rider with umbrella at 15 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=1.5m clearance or decelerates >=3 m/s^2 during gust veer; rider instability recognized within 2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Weather-compounded rider instability couples meteorology with VRU dynamics; rare high-variance combination.

scenarios.name: late-merger-full-length-run
scenarios.description: On a two-to-one lane-drop, a sedan runs the closed lane at 90 km/h past 400 m of 25 km/h queued traffic and demands a slot at the cone taper tip.
scenarios.mechanism: The late runner's 65 km/h speed differential consumes every legal gap; only ego, positioned last among cooperative queuers, can physically supply the forced slot, so the runner's speed choice itself creates an emergency merge demand at the taper apex.
environment: two-to-one freeway lane drop with 300 m cone taper
scenarios.successSignature: Ego supplies or denies the slot with bounded deceleration never exceeding 4 m/s^2 and maintains >=1.0 s TTC at the taper; no contact and no secondary braking wave behind ego.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches gap metering under social pressure where the naive behaviors (full block, panic yield) both cause crashes behind ego.

scenarios.name: early-merger-speed-mismatch-shockwave
scenarios.description: A minivan merges 800 m before the actual closure point, then slows to 15 km/h in the through lane waiting to be let into the faster adjacent flow, spawning a standing shockwave.
scenarios.mechanism: The premature merge at half the prevailing speed forces every follower to brake, and the resulting compression wave propagates backward into ego's platoon, converting one driver's over-politeness into a multi-vehicle rear-end risk field.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects the 40+ km/h speed discontinuity within 150 m, achieves >=2 s headway before the wave crest, and its own braking contributes <1 m/s^2 amplification to the follower behind.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shockwave damping is measurable; AVs that copy human brake-late behavior amplify jams, so this trains anticipatory speed harmonization.

scenarios.name: zipper-alternation-bus-refusal
scenarios.description: At an established zipper point, a city bus that has right-of-way under the alternating pattern arrives simultaneously with a car that refuses its yielding turn, and both expect ego's adjacent lane to resolve it.
scenarios.mechanism: Two non-ego actors break the implicit alternation contract at the merge point; the deadlock resolves only if someone yields off-contract, and ego's lane position makes it the default sacrificer unless it claims its contractual slot.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds its contracted slot without collision, achieving >=0.8 m lateral clearance to whichever vehicle intrudes, and total stop time in the bottleneck does not increase versus baseline alternation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests whether the AV understands emergent queueing conventions (turn-taking) rather than statutory right-of-way alone.

scenarios.name: staggered-ramp-pair-hidden-second
scenarios.description: Two cars accelerate up an on-ramp staggered nose-to-tail; ego accepts a gap sized for the lead car, and the trailing car uses the lead as cover to cut into the same gap at the last second.
scenarios.mechanism: Occlusion by the lead ramp vehicle hides the second accelerator until it emerges 30 m from the gore, converting ego's valid single-gap acceptance into a two-body conflict with under 1 s TTC.
actors: trailing ramp SUV hidden in lead's shadow
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either re-opens headway to fit both (>=2.5 s combined) or executes a single decisive decel to fall behind the pair, with minimum TTC >=1.2 s and no evasive steering beyond one lane correction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-actor occluded intent is a top crash mechanism at ramps; trains sensor fusion persistence plus game-theoretic gap sizing.

scenarios.name: blind-spot-drift-hostile-merge
scenarios.description: On open highway with no construction, a coupe drifts at a shallow angle from ego's blind spot into a 12 m gap at matched speed with no turn signal, compressing ego's space until braking is forced.
scenarios.mechanism: The unsignaled 5-degree lateral drift at constant longitudinal speed means the intrusion is invisible to lane-based prediction until the gap halves; the absence of signal removes the usual cue, so only continuous lateral tracking triggers the defensive response.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego initiates response within 0.5 s of lateral velocity detection, limiting required decel to <=3 m/s^2 and maintaining >=0.9 s TTC throughout the intrusion.
scenarios.trainingValue: Unsignaled hostile drift differs from the cataloged zipper case by having zero contextual warning; tests pure kinematic vigilance.

scenarios.name: brake-check-retaliation-after-declined-slot
scenarios.description: After ego declines to slow for an entitled merger, the rebuffed driver completes the merge anyway, then brake-checks ego twice within 500 m.
scenarios.mechanism: Social retaliation converts a routine merge dispute into a deliberate deceleration trap; the second check comes immediately after ego resumes spacing, exploiting the expected recovery-acceleration window.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >=2 s headway through both checks with max decel 5 m/s^2, never re-engages the antagonist, and logs consistent spacing behavior a reviewer can verify frame-by-frame.
scenarios.trainingValue: Distinguishes threat-responsive braking from panic braking and trains de-escalation: the correct policy sacrifices time, not safety margin.

scenarios.name: shoulder-run-merge-demand
scenarios.description: During stop-and-go congestion, a pickup drives 200 m along the right shoulder and then angles into the travel lane directly ahead of ego, which is the last vehicle before an entrance ramp.
scenarios.mechanism: The shoulder-runner arrives with closing speed while ego simultaneously faces a ramp vehicle legally demanding space, creating a three-way squeeze where granting one demand necessarily revokes the other.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego resolves with priority to the legal ramp user: pickup receives <=1 m clearance or is fully denied, ego never leaves its lane, and minimum TTC to either actor >=1.0 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Illegal-but-common behavior tests rule hierarchy: the AV must rank statutory right-of-way over positional aggression.

scenarios.name: merge-slot-theft-third-vehicle
scenarios.description: Ego slows to courteously open a slot for a signaling merger, but a faster third car from further back accelerates through the opened gap first, stealing the slot and stranding the courteous merger beside ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Courtesy creates a resource race: the yielded space is unowned, and the thief's higher speed lets it claim the gap ego sized for another vehicle, instantly converting ego's politeness into a blocking obstruction for the original merger now alongside.
scenarios.successSignature: Slot theft detected via relative speed within 1.5 s; ego closes or re-opens the gap decisively such that neither the stranded van nor thief ends up in a <0.5 s TTC overlap, and ego's follower never decels harder than 3 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains reasoning about unowned intermediate states created by courtesy — the gap between intention and completion is exploitable.

scenarios.name: double-park-oncoming-platoon-timing
scenarios.description: A delivery van double-parks in ego's lane; three oncoming cars are tightly bunched so ego cannot use the opposing lane, and the van's hazard lights suggest a departure that does not come for 40 seconds.
scenarios.mechanism: The oncoming platoon's length defines exactly when opposing-lane use becomes safe; the double-parker's hazard lights falsely predict departure, so ego must plan around the platoon's arrival geometry, not the decoy cue.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego waits out the platoon (total delay <45 s), then transits the gap at <=25 km/h with >=1 m clearance to the van and zero opposing-lane occupancy when platoon headway <3 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporal gap arithmetic against oncoming platoons is the core skill of all informal lane sharing; this isolates it cleanly.

scenarios.name: double-park-chain-staggered-slalom
scenarios.description: Vehicles are double-parked on both sides of a narrow street, offset so the free path zigzags; ego meets an oncoming car mid-slalom and both must perform a coordinated multi-step yielding dance.
scenarios.mechanism: Offset obstacles convert a simple pass into a sequential game with no simultaneous solution: whoever reaches the widest pocket first claims it, and the pocket assignment propagates backward to queued followers on both sides.
scenarios.successSignature: Coordination resolved via explicit deceleration-to-yield within 2 vehicle lengths of meeting; ego completes slalom with >=0.5 m clearance per obstacle and followers resume within 5 s of clearing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-step sequential negotiation with propagated commitments — far richer than single-pass cases and common in dense cities.

scenarios.name: double-park-door-open-during-negotiation
scenarios.description: While ego negotiates around a double-parked rideshare, the driver's door swings open into the remaining gap exactly when ego commits to the pass.
scenarios.mechanism: Door opening mid-negotiation invalidates the clearance ego just verified, forcing a split-second choice between lateral return (into oncoming) and braking; the causal trigger is ego's own commitment signaling the occupant to move.
scenarios.successSignature: Door motion detected >=0.6 s before maximum encroachment; ego aborts with decel <=6 m/s^2 and final clearance to door edge >=0.3 m, or delays commitment 2 s and passes after closure.
scenarios.trainingValue: Negotiations are dynamic contracts — the counterparty can revise terms mid-execution; trains continuous re-validation instead of commit-and-forget.

scenarios.name: waved-through-simultaneous-proceed
scenarios.description: At an uncontrolled four-way junction, an oncoming driver makes an explicit waving 'go' gesture toward ego, then begins accelerating through the intersection himself at the same moment ego accepts the invitation.
scenarios.mechanism: The gesture establishes a temporary right-of-way transfer, but the waver's own subsequent action violates the transfer he authored; ego's acceptance of the gesture is precisely what the waver treats as his cue to go, a classic dual-meaning deadlock.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego verifies waver wheel-angle and creep behavior for >=1 s before accepting, aborts with <=4 m/s^2 decel on contradiction, and keeps TTC to the waver >=1.5 s throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gestures are speech acts whose author may violate them; AVs must treat human communication as probabilistic priors, not commitments.

scenarios.name: wave-through-left-turn-retraction
scenarios.description: An oncoming driver waves ego through an unprotected left turn against traffic, then changes his mind mid-offer and proceeds straight while ego is already committed into the turn.
scenarios.mechanism: The offer's retraction occurs after ego's turning trajectory is kinematically locked (steered, rolling at 8 km/h), so the retraction converts a courtesy into a head-on crossing conflict requiring immediate abort dynamics.
actors: second oncoming car hidden behind waver
environment: four-lane arterial with center turn zone
scenarios.successSignature: Hidden second vehicle revealed via occlusion-aware prediction; ego aborts turn with heading rate <=20 deg/s returning to lane origin, or completes with >=1.2 s TTC if geometry allows, chosen within 0.8 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Wave-through offers occlude the waver's lane; accepting one without checking the shadowed lane is a fatal AV error pattern worth dedicated training data.

scenarios.name: waved-forward-then-crosses-from-side
scenarios.description: A driver stopped at a stop-sign side street waves ego straight through, then launches into a left turn across ego's path after ego is alongside his bumper.
scenarios.mechanism: The wave discharges only the straight-through conflict in the waver's mind; his planned left turn remains live, and ego's proximity masks his turn signal, so the residual conflict activates at point-of-no-return geometry.
actors: stop-sign driver waving then turning left
environment: two-lane road with stop-controlled side street
scenarios.successSignature: Ego tracks waver's front wheel rotation continuously through the entire pass, achieving >=1.0 s TTC response margin and lateral separation >=1.5 m at the moment of any launch.
scenarios.trainingValue: Scope of a courtesy waiver is ambiguous; training must teach that a wave clears the immediate head-on vector only, never the waver's full plan.

scenarios.name: exit-approach-tailgate-pressure
scenarios.description: A lifted truck tailgates at 0.8 s headway at 95 km/h for 2 km while ego approaches its own off-ramp, pressuring ego to speed up or change lanes away from the exit.
scenarios.mechanism: Tailgating pressure peaks exactly when ego needs stable longitudinal control for the ramp deceleration curve; capitulating to pressure corrupts exit geometry, while holding pace risks the tailgater attempting an unsafe right-side pass at the ramp gore.
environment: downstream exit with 250 m decel lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds target speed +/-3 km/h and lane center through pressure, exits with decel matching ramp geometry (<=2.5 m/s^2), and records tailgater headway violation without any ego-initiated erratic response.
scenarios.trainingValue: Social pressure applied at a geometric decision point tests whether the planner optimizes for comfort-of-others versus trajectory validity.

scenarios.name: tailgater-forcing-premature-green-commitment
scenarios.description: A tailgater riding ego's bumper at a red light creeps forward repeatedly; when the light turns green but the box ahead is full, the pressure tempts a premature entry that would trap ego mid-intersection.
scenarios.mechanism: Harassment-by-creeping raises the cost of waiting socially while the downstream queue makes entry physically illegal, weaponizing don't-block-the-box compliance against ego.
actors: queued traffic filling the far side
scenarios.successSignature: Ego enters only when exit-side storage >= ego's crossing distance +2 m, tolerates >=15 s of horn/creep pressure, and never occupies the crosswalk or box; measurable as zero box dwell time.
scenarios.trainingValue: Isolates robustness to manufactured urgency: the physical state says wait, the social state says go.

scenarios.name: tailgater-right-shoulder-pass-denial
scenarios.description: As ego decelerates for a visible 20 km/h queue, the tailgater behind swings onto the paved right shoulder to pass, converging on ego's lane just as the queue's last free gap closes.
scenarios.mechanism: The shoulder pass exists only because ego's lawful decel created the opportunity; the passer's re-entry timing collides with the queue closure, so ego's gap-search and the passer's cut-in converge on the same shrinking space.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego protects the queue transition (final headway to queue leader >=2 s) and denies the shoulder re-entry with >=0.5 m lateral buffer maintained, no contact, TTC >=1.0 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shoulder-passing punishes compliant deceleration; the AV must defend its trajectory without abandoning legality.

scenarios.name: tailgate-pressure-exit-miss-cascade
scenarios.description: A tailgating hatchback pressures ego past its intended exit; ego correctly continues to the next exit, but the tailgater also misses it, brakes violently realizing his error, and forces an emergency situation behind ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Ego's refusal to be rushed causes the aggressor to suffer his own navigation error; his panic braking at 95 km/h 60 m behind ego transfers the consequence of his aggression back onto ego as a rear-end threat.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains or increases headway via controlled accel to >=3 s during the antagonist's panic, absorbing the event with decel <=4 m/s^2 if the space closes, and no lane change into adjacent traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Aggressors create their own emergencies; ego must forecast the aggressor's error cascade, not just the current pressure.

scenarios.name: queue-jump-turn-lane-forced-reentry
scenarios.description: A sedan uses a 300 m right-turn-only lane to bypass a 400 m queue, then at the lane's end demands re-entry into through traffic at walking speed with blinker on, beside ego.
scenarios.mechanism: The jumper's illegal position gain converts into a forced merge demand exactly where the turn lane narrows; denying him risks a sideswipe as the lane expires, granting him rewards the violation and delays the lawful follower behind ego.
environment: arterial with 300 m right-turn lane feeding a cross street
scenarios.successSignature: Policy-consistent resolution: either firm denial maintained until the jumper fully stops (then admitted at zero speed advantage) or admission with >=2 s headway sacrifice documented; never a mid-lane-expiry panic yield.
scenarios.trainingValue: Enforcement-versus-pragmatism tradeoff at expiring lanes is a genuine AV policy question with measurable fairness outcomes.

scenarios.name: queue-jump-bike-lane-suv-cyclist-conflict
scenarios.description: An SUV noses into the bike lane to bypass a red-light queue, then must force re-entry across ego's lane while a cyclist approaches in the very bike lane being used as a shortcut.
scenarios.mechanism: The shortcut route itself generates the emergency: re-entry demand rises as the bike lane delivers the cyclist into the SUV's flank, so the SUV's cut-back accelerates precisely when ego is closing from behind.
actors: cyclist in bike lane at 25 km/h
environment: arterial with painted bike lane 1.8 m
scenarios.successSignature: SUV re-entry absorbed with ego TTC >=1.2 s AND cyclist never within 1 m of the SUV's path; ego's response prioritizes protecting the vulnerable road user over denying the jumper.
scenarios.trainingValue: Forces triage between punishing a violator and shielding a third party endangered by the violation.

scenarios.name: cascade-queue-jump-pair
scenarios.description: Two cars queue-jump the shoulder in succession; the second follows the first blindly and both arrive at the merge point together, doubling the forced re-entry demand on ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Herd dynamics mean the second jumper never independently assessed the merge point; the paired arrival presents ego with a two-vehicle demand spike at a gap sized for zero or one, with the pair's internal following distance under 1 s.
environment: congested freeway with 400 m usable shoulder
scenarios.successSignature: Pair treated as a unit: ego either admits both with combined >=3.5 s headway cost capped at 4 m/s^2 decel, or denies with sustained closure preventing either entry; no split decision leaving one jumper stranded across the line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Violations cluster; single-violator policies fail on herds. Trains demand estimation from follower behavior, not just leaders.

scenarios.name: denied-queue-jumper-diagonal-block
scenarios.description: When ego and the queue refuse re-entry to a turn-lane jumper, he stops diagonally across both the turn lane and through lane, freezing traffic rather than retreating.
scenarios.mechanism: Denial escalates the jumper from competitor to static obstacle spanning two lanes; the blockage converts ego's earlier tactical win into a strategic loss requiring a new plan (squeeze past his nose or wait him out) while cross-traffic conflicts build.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego selects and executes one coherent strategy within 10 s: hold position >=60 s if waiting, or pass with >=0.8 m clearance at <=10 km/h; no oscillation between strategies and no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Escalation outcomes of denial are rarely trained; the AV needs a contingency tree for when punishment of bad behavior fails.

scenarios.name: box-trap-green-entry-downstream-queue
scenarios.description: Ego enters on green because the far-side queue looks passable, but the queue advances slower than ego crosses, and the light turns red with ego fully inside the box as cross traffic releases.
scenarios.mechanism: Entry-time storage estimation error is the root cause: ego's crossing time exceeded the available far-side absorption, so the trap is sprung by the mismatch of two speeds, not by any single actor's aggression.
actors: leader car that entered alongside ego
scenarios.successSignature: Ego enters only with measured far-side storage > crossing distance x 1.3 margin; if trapped despite margin, clears the box within the first 2 s of cross-green with heading never perpendicular to cross flow.
scenarios.trainingValue: Storage-margin arithmetic under queue uncertainty is a foundational city-driving skill with crisp pass/fail geometry.

scenarios.name: box-trap-perpendicular-freeze-cross-flow
scenarios.description: Ego is legitimately mid-box when cross traffic launches early and stops perpendicular to ego, nose-to-nose, sealing both escape vectors while ego's own light is red.
scenarios.mechanism: Mutual entrapment: neither ego nor the cross vehicle can move without the other's cooperation, and both face rear-enders from behind; resolution requires negotiated inching governed by who has reverse room, a protocol with no codified rules.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego communicates via creep-and-hold micro-motions, achieving >=0.5 m incremental clearance per exchange, and never reverses into its follower; full extraction within one signal cycle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Deadlock protocols (creep, yield, signal-by-motion) are unwritten social conventions that must be learned, not programmed from traffic law.

scenarios.name: deceptive-gap-leader-stops-mid-box
scenarios.description: Ego trails a leader into an intersection on a stale green with adequate-looking far-side gap, but the leader stops mid-box for a late pedestrian, converting ego's valid entry into a trap.
scenarios.mechanism: The leader's discretionary mid-box stop severs ego's assumed continuity; ego's entry decision inherited the leader's implied promise of through-motion, so a third party (the pedestrian) collapses the shared assumption.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds entry when leader shows any pre-crossing decel >=1 m/s^2; if entered, stops behind leader fully clear of the box's critical cross-path and resumes within 1 s of leader clearing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Leaders' behavior is information about hidden road state; conditioning entry on leader momentum teaches inference from proxies.

scenarios.name: rail-crossing-queue-hold-under-tailgate-pressure
scenarios.description: Traffic queues across a grade crossing; ego correctly holds short of the tracks while a tailgater sounds horn and flashes lights demanding ego advance onto the rails as a train approaches in the distance.
scenarios.mechanism: The queue's far side is stationary so advancing feels harmless socially, but track occupancy is binary and train arrival uncertainty is real; the tailgater's pressure exploits the asymmetry that a collision costs ego everything and him little.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains stand-off with bumper >=6 m from nearest rail regardless of pressure duration; measurable as zero track occupancy while gates activate, plus logged pressure timeline.
scenarios.trainingValue: Absolute-rule defense against social coercion — some spaces are never tradable, and the corpus must include losing-socially-winning-physically outcomes.

scenarios.name: emergency-corridor-creation-queued-freeway
scenarios.description: An ambulance approaches from behind at speed through 15 km/h congested freeway lanes; ego and the adjacent lane must synchronously shift laterally to form a corridor where lanes are only 3.2 m wide.
scenarios.mechanism: Corridor formation is a distributed consensus problem: each vehicle's shift depends on neighbors shifting, and any single refuser breaks the channel; ego's move is useful only if sequenced with the truck beside it whose mirror clearance is marginal.
actors: passenger cars ahead forming partial corridor
scenarios.successSignature: Ego shifts >=0.8 m within 4 s of siren confirmation, achieving >=3.5 m total corridor width with truck coordination; ambulance passes with zero braking by responders and ego returns smoothly within 10 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-agent spontaneous cooperation is nearly untrainable from scripted data; this measures synchronization quality against imperfect humans.

scenarios.name: oncoming-emergency-divided-road-stop-ambiguity
scenarios.description: A fire engine approaches head-on on the far side of a 2 m painted median; some oncoming cars stop, others continue, and ego must decide whether the median exempts it while a following car misreads ego's hesitation as weakness and pushes past.
scenarios.mechanism: Legal ambiguity (median-width exemption varies by jurisdiction) produces heterogeneous crowd behavior, and ego's own choice is interpreted by the follower as a signal, coupling the decisions; wrong continuation endangers nothing physically but models bad precedent, wrong stopping invites a rear-end threat.
environment: divided arterial with 2 m raised/painted median
scenarios.successSignature: Jurisdiction-consistent choice executed within 3 s of siren detection, followed by stable behavior (no oscillation); if stopping, decel <=3 m/s^2 with follower managed via earlier gradual slowdown.
scenarios.trainingValue: Crowd-consensus scenarios teach the AV to behave legibly: its motion instructs other drivers, so indecision itself is hazardous.

scenarios.name: emergency-stuck-behind-refusing-jumper
scenarios.description: A paramedic van responding code-3 is trapped behind a queue-jumper occupying the only gap; the jumper refuses to yield, and ego beside him must unilaterally widen the corridor enough for the van to pass around the refuser.
scenarios.mechanism: One defector breaks corridor consensus, so the rescue falls on ego's side: ego must compress toward a parked car with sub-meter margins to compensate for the refuser's stolen width, converting another's violation into ego's physical risk budget.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields >=0.9 m additional corridor width within 5 s with >=0.3 m clearance to the parked car; van passes without stopping, and total rescue delay attributable to ego = 0 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compensation for defectors tests whether cooperation models degrade gracefully when the crowd's contract fails.

scenarios.name: ambulance-vs-mid-left-turn-completion
scenarios.description: Ego is halfway through a protected left turn when an ambulance appears through the intersection against the red; completing the turn crosses its path, reversing back blocks the platoon behind, and a car beside ego chooses the opposite.
scenarios.mechanism: Code-3 priority retroactively voids ego's lawful right-of-way mid-maneuver, and the physically optimal action (complete quickly) contradicts the legally canonical action (yield immediately), while a nearby human demonstrating the wrong choice adds social pressure.
environment: signalized intersection with protected left phase
ambulance on cross street 150 m out
scenarios.successSignature: Decision made within 100 ms of siren/light detection: complete turn raising exit speed to clear the path >=2 s before ambulance arrival, or freeze with nose clear of its lane; TTC to ambulance never <1.5 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mid-maneuver priority inversion is one of the hardest real AV cases: the correct answer is kinetic, not legal.

scenarios.name: procession-flag-car-stale-yellow
scenarios.description: A funeral procession led by a flag car crosses on a yellow-about-to-red signal; the flag car makes it but a gap opens mid-procession exactly as ego's cross-street green appears, tempting entry before trailing mourners sprint the light.
scenarios.mechanism: Procession convention (members follow the leader through regardless of signals) collides with signal logic that grants ego a legal green mid-procession; the variable inter-car gaps make it impossible to know from the flag car alone when the stream ends.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego counts the procession stream and enters only after >=3 s of confirmed stream end (last car cleared plus margin); measurable as zero conflict with any procession member and delay <30 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Convention-over-signal precedence plus gap-counting under uncertainty; processions are legally protected in many states yet visually ambiguous.

scenarios.name: procession-gap-cutin-break
scenarios.description: A commuter impatient with a slow procession cuts into a gap between mourning cars; the severed rear half of the procession accelerates to reconnect, and one mourner swerves across ego's lane trying to rejoin.
scenarios.mechanism: The cut-in breaks the procession's single-file contract, and the rear segment's reunion maneuver happens in ego's lane at 20 km/h deltas; the commuter's selfishness thus manufactures a sudden lateral conflict for an uninvolved ego.
environment: two-lane road with procession at 30 km/h
oncoming lane blocked by procession length
scenarios.successSignature: Swerving mourner tracked from deviation onset with ego decel <=4 m/s^2 and TTC >=1.2 s; ego never attempts to overtake the commuter through the broken procession.
scenarios.trainingValue: Second-order effects: violations propagate into new conflicts for bystanders; trains causal chaining beyond the initial actor.

scenarios.name: procession-escort-holds-ego-midblock
scenarios.description: A police escort motorcycle halts ego mid-block with a hand signal so the oncoming procession can cross through a gap in ego's direction flow, then waves ego on before the full procession has passed, contradicting the still-crossing tail.
scenarios.mechanism: Authority override creates a temporary rule regime, then the escort's early release signal conflicts with ground truth (procession tail still crossing), forcing ego to arbitrate between officer gesture and observed reality.
actors: police escort motorcycle with hand signals
scenarios.successSignature: Ego obeys the officer's stop instantly (<1 s), then on release verifies procession tail clearance >=5 s before moving; officer-gesture compliance logged alongside independent safety verification.
scenarios.trainingValue: Authority signals outrank signs but not physics; the AV must layer obedience with verification, measurable per frame.

scenarios.name: bus-pullout-flash-yield-ambiguity
scenarios.description: A transit bus at a curb stop activates its merge-flashers and re-enters traffic beside ego at matched speed; state law says ego must yield, but the bus driver hesitates half-committed, wobbling across the line twice.
scenarios.mechanism: Statutory duty (yield to buses) conflicts with the bus's own indecisive kinematics; a strict yield makes ego brake erratically for a bus that retreats, a strict claim causes a sideswipe if the bus finally commits — the wobble is the hazard.
environment: curbside stop with bus bay partially blocked by parked car
scenarios.successSignature: Ego classifies commitment (lateral velocity threshold) within 0.7 s, then executes one clean policy: full yield (decel to open >=4 s gap) or full claim (accel to clear), never matching the bus's oscillation; TTC >=1.5 s throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Half-enforced laws (bus yield rules) plus hesitant executors create oscillation traps; AVs must be the decisive party.

scenarios.name: bus-pullout-abort-cyclist-blindspot
scenarios.description: A bus begins pulling out, sees a cyclist in its mirror at the last instant, aborts back into the stop, then restarts the pull-out 3 seconds later just as ego had accelerated into the vacated space.
scenarios.mechanism: Abort-restart cycles mean the bus's apparent retreat is not a release of the lane; ego's exploitation of the aborted gap is punished by the restart, with the cyclist's presence as the hidden cause of both the abort and the timing.
environment: no bike lane, cyclist in travel lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats aborted pull-outs as suspended, not terminated: holds >=1.5 s observation before claiming space, and absorbs the restart with TTC >=1.5 s, decel <=4 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Aborted maneuvers leave intention-state residue; the corpus needs restart dynamics so planners don't reset beliefs on retreat.

scenarios.name: bus-travel-lane-pass-oncoming-truck-squeeze
scenarios.description: A bus boards passengers while stopped dead in the travel lane (no bay); ego edges left to pass just as an oncoming flatbed does the same from the opposite side, squeezing the gap over the bus's hood area to under 3 m total.
scenarios.mechanism: Two independent pass decisions around the same obstacle converge because each driver sees the other too late over the bus's bulk; the bus's boarding dwell time guarantees both arrivals coincide, and neither can see the pinch forming.
environment: two-lane road, bus unable to use destroyed bay
scenarios.successSignature: Pinch detected via oncoming lateral shift >=2 s before minimum gap; ego retreats to behind-bus position with >=1 m clearance, or times pass so total gap >=3.5 m; pedestrians at door given >=1 m berth.
scenarios.trainingValue: Symmetric obstacle-passing with hidden mutual visibility failures — classic squeeze generation that top-down renders show clearly.

scenarios.name: articulated-bus-sled-cutout-sweep
scenarios.description: An articulated bus departing a mid-block stop pivots sharply; its rear artic joint sleds the back section 1.2 m into ego's lane even though the front stayed in the bus zone.
scenarios.mechanism: Off-tracking geometry means the rear body follows a tighter radius than the front axle, so lane-keeping by the front section is misleading — the rear sweeps into adjacent space with no frontal cue, punishing ego for trusting the bus's nose position.
environment: mid-block bus stop on 50 km/h arterial
tight 90-degree turn 20 m past the stop
scenarios.successSignature: Rear-body sweep predicted from front-wheel angle (not body pose); ego drops back >=6 m from the rear door zone before the turn, achieving zero proximity events to the swept envelope.
scenarios.trainingValue: Articulated off-tracking is systematically mispredicted by models trained on rigid bodies; dedicated coverage fixes a real perception-planning gap.

scenarios.name: truck-wide-right-turn-inside-squeeze
scenarios.description: A semi signals a wide right turn from the left lane; a compact car tries to slip through on the truck's right into the turning radius, and the trailer sweeps across the compact's path while ego follows the compact.
scenarios.mechanism: Wide-turn right-of-way is signaled but widely ignored; the slipper's gamble puts two vehicles (compact, then ego) inside a closing trailer arc whose boundary moves at the trailer's yaw rate — the danger is the arc, not the cab.
environment: intersection with tight 12 m corner radius
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies trailer arc from tractor steering >=1.5 s early, holds outside the swept envelope (>=0.5 m from trailer path), and does not follow the compact into the kill zone; compact's outcome recorded but ego's isolation verified.
scenarios.trainingValue: Swept-path reasoning plus resisting follow-the-leader into known-dangerous geometry; trailer arcs are measurable ground truth.

scenarios.name: truck-turn-stall-two-lane-block-cross-negotiation
scenarios.description: A box truck misjudges a wide turn, mounts the curb corner, and stalls straddling both travel lanes; cross-traffic and ego's direction must self-organize alternating passage around the stalled truck with no signal authority.
scenarios.mechanism: The stall deletes the intersection's normal priority structure; passage order must emerge from eye contact, creep assertions, and gap-taking among strangers, with each vehicle's move changing what the next one can do.
scenarios.successSignature: Self-organized alternation achieved with ego taking no more than its fair share of slots when contested; per-move clearance >=0.6 m, deadlock duration <45 s, zero contact events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Emergent traffic governance without signals or police is a pure negotiation benchmark with countable throughput metrics.

scenarios.name: reverse-parking-midblock-lane-block-negotiation
scenarios.description: A driver performs a back-in parallel park mid-block on a busy street, taking 25 seconds and multiple corrections while fully blocking the lane; ego and oncoming traffic must orchestrate around the repeated reversals of direction.
scenarios.mechanism: Reverse maneuvers alternate the blocker's threat vector every few seconds (nose in lane, then tail), so any pass attempt must be re-validated at each reversal; the oncoming queue's willingness to hold determines whether ego can stage in the opposing lane at all.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stages in the opposing lane only during confirmed reversal windows (blocker stationary >3 s), transits with >=1 m clearance, total added delay <35 s, and zero aborts caused by ego's own indecision.
scenarios.trainingValue: Time-sharing a lane with a multi-phase maneuver requires phase tracking, not just object detection — a rich temporal reasoning target.

scenarios.name: abandoned-reverse-park-resume-bait
scenarios.description: A driver halfway through a reverse park pulls forward as if abandoning the attempt; ego accelerates through the opening, and the driver immediately resumes reversing into exactly the space ego is entering.
scenarios.mechanism: The feint (or genuine change of mind) resets ego's belief about lane availability; resumption timing targets the space while ego occupies its approach, making ego's acceleration itself the input that springs the conflict.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego requires >=2 s of sustained forward motion plus driver gaze/wheel cues before committing; if bait taken, aborts with TTC >=1.2 s and reverses <=2 m without striking the follower.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intent revision detection (feints, second thoughts) is undertrained everywhere; this isolates belief-reset dynamics in a compact scene.

scenarios.name: three-point-turn-oncoming-queue
scenarios.description: A lost driver executes a three-point turn mid-block on a narrow street just as ego and a 5-car oncoming queue converge on him from both directions.
scenarios.mechanism: The turn's three phases each block differently (forward sweep blocks one side, reverse blocks the other), and the converging queues from both ends compete to exploit whichever half-lane is momentarily free, with no one controlling sequence.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego claims the free half-lane only when the turner's phase matches (verified via wheel/tail direction), yields phase-changes gracefully, and total scene resolution <60 s with zero horn-induced rushed entries.
scenarios.trainingValue: Phase-locked opportunism: exploiting a moving blocker safely requires modeling his maneuver state machine — a step beyond static gap acceptance.

scenarios.name: phantom-jam-wave-damping-duty
scenarios.description: In dense 60 km/h traffic, a phantom jam wave approaches ego from 300 m ahead, propagating backward; ego's braking style will either amplify or damp the wave for the 40 cars behind it.
scenarios.mechanism: Stop-and-go waves persist because each driver brakes harder than necessary and accelerates late; ego sits at a node where its decel profile mathematically determines wave amplitude growth, making courtesy toward unseen followers a physical quantity.
environment: dense freeway 60 km/h, 1.2 s average headways
scenarios.successSignature: Ego caps decel at <=2.5 m/s^2 and maintains >=1.8 s headway through the crest; wave amplitude behind ego measurably smaller than ahead (speed variance reduction >=15%), computed from follower trajectories.
scenarios.trainingValue: Phantom jams are the canonical case where individual rationality harms the collective; AVs can measurably damp them and this quantifies it.

scenarios.name: phantom-jam-motorcycle-filtering-toward-moving-ego
scenarios.description: Ego crawls at 15 km/h in a jam wave when a motorcycle filters between lanes toward ego's lane boundary at 40 km/h just as ego's lane lurches forward and the adjacent lane brakes.
scenarios.mechanism: Filtering exploits the differential between adjacent lanes' speeds; when the speed differential flips sign (ego accelerates, neighbor brakes), the filtering corridor collapses onto ego's fender line with the rider's arrival time coupled to both lanes' decisions.
scenarios.successSignature: Corridor collapse predicted from adjacent-lane decel onset >=1 s ahead; ego modulates to give the rider an exit (>=0.8 m lateral) or freezes longitudinal motion, TTC to rider >=1.0 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Filtering riders are legitimate but fragile actors whose fate couples to ego's throttle; trains joint lateral-longitudinal micro-management.

scenarios.name: phantom-jam-meets-offramp-spillback-merge
scenarios.description: A phantom jam wave arrives at exactly the point where an off-ramp queue has spilled back into the through lanes; slowing vehicles must both absorb the wave and let ramp-bound cars cross over to reach the exit.
scenarios.mechanism: Two queues intersect: the longitudinal jam wave and the lateral exit-crossing demand occupy the same 100 m of lane, so every braking decision simultaneously changes the weaving gap structure — damping the wave tears open the weave holes and vice versa.
environment: freeway right lanes near busy off-ramp
scenarios.successSignature: Ego sustains >=2 s headway through the weave zone (enabling crossovers) while capping decel <=3 m/s^2; crossover vehicles complete with ego TTC >=1.5 s and no wave amplification behind.
scenarios.trainingValue: Competing queue structures superposed on one lane stretch is realistic megacity driving; success requires optimizing two coupled objectives at once.

scenarios.name: tiny-gap-cutin-series-shrinking
scenarios.description: At 105 km/h, three successive vehicles cut in ahead of ego over 800 m, each taking a smaller gap (1.2 s, then 0.9 s, then 0.6 s) as followers learn ego brakes politely and exploit the margin.
scenarios.mechanism: Polite braking is observable and learnable by surrounding drivers; each successive cutter calibrates a tighter gap from watching ego's previous responses, so the series constitutes an adaptive adversarial probe ending below ego's comfortable braking limit.
scenarios.successSignature: Series handled with monotonically decreasing response margin but never below 0.8 s TTC; ego's decel <=3.5 m/s^2 each time, and after the third cut ego re-establishes >=2 s headway within 5 s without retaliatory blocking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Adaptive adversaries that learn from your responses require response randomization/robustness — measurable as bounded worst-case across a learned escalation ladder.

scenarios.name: cutin-cascade-braking-truck-platoon
scenarios.description: A car cuts into a 0.7 s gap ahead of a loaded semi; the semi brakes hard and long, and the deceleration cascade rolls back through three lanes with ego positioned two cars behind the semi.
scenarios.mechanism: One small-gap cut-in seeds a platoon-wide braking cascade whose amplitude grows with each following-distance error; ego's exposure is determined by the semi's 100 m stopping profile and the errors of two intermediate human drivers, none of whom ego controls.
environment: semi following distance 0.8 s (too tight for load)
scenarios.successSignature: Cascade arrival anticipated from the semi's brake-light plus load type; ego achieves >=2.5 s effective headway before impact of the wave, peak decel <=4 m/s^2, no lane change into the swerving adjacent traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Cut-ins matter less for the cutter than for the cascades they seed behind heavy vehicles; trains second-order consequence forecasting.

scenarios.name: leapfrog-alternating-cutins
scenarios.description: Two sedans leapfrog each other through congestion by alternating cut-ins — one cuts ahead of ego, accelerates, the partner fills ego's old spot behind, and they repeat the cycle to progress through the pack using ego as a rung.
scenarios.mechanism: Coordinated pairs convert polite ego spacing into free lane-progress currency; each cycle consumes 15 m of ego's buffer and repositions an antagonist both fore and aft, so the harm is structural (buffer erosion from two vectors) rather than any single acute event.
scenarios.successSignature: Buffer erosion capped: ego maintains >=1.2 s minimum headway to either pair member across >=3 cycles; pair's net progress via ego reduced >=50% versus unconstrained, without any blocking or brake-check provocation by ego.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-agent coordinated exploitation is qualitatively unlike single cut-ins; defenses must be spatially distributed (front and rear simultaneously).

scenarios.name: rolling-roadblock-pair-sudden-split
scenarios.description: Two cars drive side-by-side at identical 85 km/h blocking both lanes for 3 km (whether intentional or obliviously matched); the left car abruptly exits left at a drop-off ramp, releasing the pressure asymmetrically onto ego in the right lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Matched-speed pairing suppresses all passing options; the sudden unilateral split instantaneously converts a stable blockade into a localized demand spike as the pent-up queue funnels through the new hole with divergent acceleration, converging on ego's space.
scenarios.successSignature: Split anticipated from left car's ramp-relative positioning >=2 s early; ego manages the convergence of the fast follower and motorcycle with TTC >=1.3 s to both and zero lateral pinning against the remaining blocker.
scenarios.trainingValue: Long-duration social stalemates ending in abrupt release test temporal persistence plus surge handling — the aftermath matters more than the blockade.

scenarios.name: courtesy-chain-gridlock-release
scenarios.description: At a four-way intersection during a power outage affecting signals, a well-meaning driver waves three cars through out of order, destroying the rotation convention; ego arrives fourth facing two drivers who both believe it is their turn.
scenarios.mechanism: Individual generosity corrupts the shared turn-taking state; by ego's arrival, the implicit FIFO queue referenced by each driver's memory disagrees, producing a dual-claim deadlock that only explicit signaling or decisive assertion can break.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego resolves the dual claim within 5 s via unambiguous creep-or-hold signaling, never entering while two claimants are undecided; intersection throughput not degraded by ego's presence, zero contact, TTC >=1.5 s throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Corrupted conventions are harder than missing ones: the AV must detect that the shared state machine is inconsistent and re-anchor it — core multi-agent reasoning with measurable deadlock-time outcomes.

scenarios.name: Tire tread strip across both lanes
scenarios.description: A full truck-tire tread strip lies diagonally across two highway lanes after shedding from a box truck 200 m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: The truck's retread fails and the shed tread bounces once then settles diagonal across ego's lane; following vehicles brake or swerve into ego's lane, forcing simultaneous debris avoidance and cut-in response within ~1.5 s TTC.
scenarios.successSignature: Required decel <=3 m/s^2 with lateral clearance >=0.5 m from tread while tracking lane; no collision with swerving neighbor
scenarios.trainingValue: Debris straddling lanes removes the single-lane swerve option and couples object avoidance with cut-in prediction.

scenarios.name: Tire debris hidden by leading vehicle shadow
scenarios.description: A shredded tire chunk sits just beyond a large SUV's occlusion shadow so it appears only ~40 m ahead at 90 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: The lead SUV masks the debris until its own wheels pass over/near it; ego's effective perception range drops below comfortable stopping distance, demanding late but controlled braking instead of panic stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Brake initiation within 0.4 s of first detection; decel <=5 m/s^2; stop gap >=2 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests occlusion-aware speed selection: ego should have slowed behind tall leads anticipating hidden road hazards.

scenarios.name: Refrigerator sliding off flatbed ahead
scenarios.description: An unstrapped refrigerator tips off a flatbed at 70 km/h and slides/tumbles into ego's lane 30 m ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: Corner straps fail on a curve; the appliance leaves the bed laterally, strikes the guardrail, and ricochets into ego's lane, creating a tumbling obstacle with unpredictable bounce direction.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves >=6 m/s^2 decel or executes gap-accepting lane change with >=0.8 s TTC margin at contact point
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers high-mass tumbling cargo with post-impact trajectory uncertainty — worst-case cargo-loss dynamics.

scenarios.name: Ladder bouncing in adjacent lane toward ego
scenarios.description: A 6 m extension ladder falls off a pickup, lands upright-ish, and skitters laterally across lanes at an angle.
scenarios.mechanism: The ladder's asymmetric bounce makes it hop sideways one lane per ~2 s; predicting its next position requires modeling its rotation phase rather than treating it as static debris.
scenarios.successSignature: Predicted ladder crossing point avoided with >=1 s buffer; no hard brake (<4 m/s^2) unless ladder enters ego lane within 25 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Moving debris with periodic dynamics breaks the static-object assumption most planners hold for road debris.

scenarios.name: Mattress airborne off rooftop carrier
scenarios.description: A mattress lifts off a car's roof at highway speed and cartwheels through the air into the middle lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Wind loading peels the mattress free; it becomes airborne, briefly occluding sight lines as it passes between vehicles before landing 20 m ahead of ego with residual slide velocity.
scenarios.successSignature: Airborne-phase heading maintained; landing-point avoidance with required decel <=5 m/s^2 and no secondary contact with mattress after slide
scenarios.trainingValue: Rare projectile-class obstacle requiring air-phase prediction plus post-landing slide handling.

scenarios.name: Loose plywood sheets fanning across lanes
scenarios.description: Several unsecured plywood sheets slide off a flatbed on a downhill and fan out like cards across two lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Gravity accelerates sheets down grade while truck motion spreads them laterally; thin low-profile sheets evade radar but create loss-of-control risk if driven over at speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop or steer-through gap chosen with wet-pavement decel model; zero wheel contact with sheets above 30 km/h
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-profile wide-area debris forces sensor-modality fusion (camera-only detection) and surface-friction-coupled decisions.

scenarios.name: Runaway shopping cart into crosswalk path
scenarios.description: A wind-blown shopping cart exits a store lot, crosses a sidewalk, and rolls into the roadway exactly where a pedestrian queue is waiting.
scenarios.mechanism: Slope plus gusts accelerate the empty cart to ~8 km/h; pedestrians step back to dodge it and spill into the curb line, compressing the sidewalk buffer ego must respect.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral clearance to displaced pedestrians >=1 m maintained; cart tracked to intercept or yield with TTC >=2 s
scenarios.trainingValue: Cart acts as a pedestrian-displacer: the hazard is the induced human movement, not the cart itself.

scenarios.name: Shopping cart convoy pushed by two kids toward road
scenarios.description: Two children push three linked carts down a lot incline aimed at the street, losing control near the curb.
scenarios.mechanism: Linked carts exceed the kids' control authority on the grade; the train curves toward the roadway entrance while children chase it, producing dual moving hazards entering the road within 3 s.
scenarios.successSignature: Yield initiated when cart-train heading error predicts road entry; stop line held >=3 m from curb ramp
scenarios.trainingValue: Group-of-small-actors with child-chaser coupling tests joint prediction of objects plus supervising humans.

scenarios.name: Trash bin rolling downhill across intersection
scenarios.description: Collection-day trash bin breaks loose on a steep residential hill and rolls through the intersection ego is entering.
scenarios.mechanism: ~15% grade plus unlatched wheels let the bin reach jogging speed; it crosses ego's planned path on a fixed ballistic line, and a chasing resident follows it out.
scenarios.successSignature: Bin path predicted within 0.5 m; ego yields or threads with >=1.2 s margin; resident's emergence handled without harsh stop (>5 m/s^2)
scenarios.trainingValue: Ballistic rolling object with human pursuer — tests coupled prediction on grades where bins are common context clutter.

scenarios.name: Bins blocking half-lane force oncoming merge
scenarios.description: Collection-day bins line the right half of a narrow street, forcing oncoming traffic into ego's lane around them.
scenarios.mechanism: Bins reduce drivable width to under 3 m; each opposing vehicle must encroach, converting a static-obstacle street into a serial negotiation where ego must time yields against multiple oncomers.
scenarios.successSignature: Successful negotiation with zero encroachment conflicts; average negotiation delay <10 s per oncoming vehicle; no bin strike
scenarios.trainingValue: Static small obstacles induce dynamic conflicts — classic informal-right-of-way training signal.

scenarios.name: Garbage truck reversing toward bins with spotter hidden
scenarios.description: Garbage truck reverses 30 m along the curb to reach bins, spotter walking blind-side behind the trailer.
scenarios.mechanism: Reverse motion claims the travel lane while the spotter steps in/out of ego's path signaling; ego must infer the reverse maneuver intent from backup lights and spotter gestures rather than signals.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop >=5 m behind truck within 1 s of backup-light onset; spotter gesture compliance (advance/hold) followed correctly
scenarios.trainingValue: Human-directed reverse operations require reading gestured intent — rare non-signal communication channel.

scenarios.name: Loose dog weaving between queued cars
scenarios.description: A collarless dog runs along a congested arterial, darting between stopped cars at bumper level.
scenarios.mechanism: Dog uses car gaps as running lanes; its zigzag makes gaps alternately appear and close, and it may reverse direction unpredictably, invalidating single-trajectory prediction.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed capped such that any gap-entry by dog yields TTC >=1.5 s; creep speed <=5 km/h while dog within 5 m of lane
scenarios.trainingValue: Small erratic actor among occluding vehicles trains gap-aware low-speed tracking rather than binary stop/go.

scenarios.name: Deer crossing at dusk with fawn trailing
scenarios.description: A doe crosses a rural two-lane at dusk; a fawn freezes mid-road 3 s behind her.
scenarios.mechanism: Lead animal clears but follower hesitates in lane; headlights' glare cone reduces contrast so the fawn is detected late, and freezing behavior defeats motion-based detection.
scenarios.successSignature: Second-animal anticipation: ego maintains readiness (decel prep) after doe exits; fawn cleared with >=1.5 s margin or full stop before 15 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-animal staggered crossings punish clearing-on-first-animal logic; dusk contrast stresses detection.

scenarios.name: Cattle drive spilling around a bend
scenarios.description: A cattle drive rounds a blind rural bend, animals spread across both lanes with cowboys at the flanks.
scenarios.mechanism: Herd edge extends past sightline; individual cows mill laterally without pattern, and flank riders wave ego to a specific slow corridor that shifts as the herd moves.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed <=10 km/h inside herd boundary; corridor changes follow rider signals within 2 s; zero livestock proximity events <2 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Large-group amorphous actor with human-guided corridor — extreme case of cooperative slow passage.

scenarios.name: Starling flock bursting off roadside tree
scenarios.description: A starling flock erupts from a roadside tree as ego passes; dozens cross the windshield path at low height.
scenarios.mechanism: Flock startle response sends birds across the road in a dense cloud; individual trajectories are chaotic but the cloud has coherent drift, testing whether ego can reason about swarm-level rather than agent-level threat.
scenarios.successSignature: No evasive maneuver worse than moderate decel (<=3 m/s^2); forward sensors maintain tracking lock through flock passage
scenarios.trainingValue: Swarm occlusion burst degrades vision/radar simultaneously; correct behavior is usually hold-course, which naive planners violate.

scenarios.name: Canada goose family parading along lane centerline
scenarios.description: A goose pair with goslings walks down the middle of a quiet suburban lane, refusing to yield.
scenarios.mechanism: Goslings set pace (~1 km/h) and adults defend position; passing requires either full lane change into opposing traffic or a long slow escort at walking speed until they exit at a driveway.
scenarios.successSignature: Follow distance >=5 m sustained up to 120 s OR clean lane-change pass with opposing gap >=4 s; zero proximity <1.5 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Extremely slow protected actors test patience/escort behaviors and illegal-pass suppression near wildlife.

scenarios.name: Turkey vulture feeding on roadkill in lane
scenarios.description: Vultures feed on a carcass in the right lane and flush vertically at the last second as vehicles approach.
scenarios.mechanism: Birds hold position until vehicle is ~15 m out, then launch upward into the vehicle's path envelope; the carcass itself remains as a stationary obstacle beneath their flight lines.
scenarios.successSignature: Detection and slowdown initiated at >=60 m (pre-flush); carcass avoided laterally >=1 m; no swerve reaction to airborne birds
scenarios.trainingValue: Delayed-flush actors plus hidden static hazard teach anticipatory slowdown keyed to feeding-bird presence.

scenarios.name: Delivery robot stalled mid-crosswalk
scenarios.description: A sidewalk delivery robot stops dead in the middle of a crosswalk with flashing amber, blocking pedestrian flow.
scenarios.mechanism: Robot fault freezes it in the crosswalk; pedestrians funnel around it into the roadway just as ego gets green, converting an object blockage into human exposure in ego's path.
scenarios.successSignature: Green-light proceed delayed until detouring pedestrians clear; clearance envelope >=1 m around robot maintained; creep only after ped-zone empty
scenarios.trainingValue: Machine actor failure inducing human rule-breaking — green does not mean go when the crosswalk is occupied by an obstruction.

scenarios.name: Delivery robot descending curb cut into bike lane
scenarios.description: A delivery robot noses off a curb cut at 5 km/h directly across a bike lane where cyclists approach at 25 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Robot's descent blocks the bike lane; swerving cyclists veer left into ego's travel lane, creating a secondary cut-in chain triggered by the robot's slow entry.
environment: urban street with buffered bike lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates cyclist displacement: lateral shift or decel yielding >=1 m clearance to displaced rider; robot never struck
scenarios.trainingValue: Slow machine entry causes fast vulnerable-actor displacement — two-hop causal chain rarely covered by direct-interaction scenarios.

scenarios.name: Amish buggy at night with dim lantern
scenarios.description: A horse-drawn buggy travels at 8 km/h on a 90 km/h rural road at night, marked only by a small amber lantern and one reflector.
scenarios.mechanism: Closing speed exceeds 80 km/h against a nearly invisible target; buggy may make wide slow turns into a farm driveway, swinging its rear into ego's lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Detection at >=150 m; pass completed with lateral gap >=1.5 m and headlamps dipped; no horn use causing horse startle
scenarios.trainingValue: Extreme speed-differential plus low-signature target plus animal-startle constraint stacks three rarity axes.

scenarios.name: Buggy making wide left from right lane
scenarios.description: A horse-drawn wagon initiates a left turn by first angling right across ego's lane, standard horse-drawn practice.
scenarios.mechanism: Wagon swings opposite to intended turn to gain angle; its trajectory contradicts indicator-free expectations, so ego mispredicts a right turn and closes on the swing arc.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn-direction reclassification within 1 s of counter-swing onset; decel to <=20 km/h differential before wagon apex
scenarios.trainingValue: Vehicle class with inverted turn kinematics — trajectory priors learned from cars actively mislead here.

scenarios.name: Oversize load overhanging into ego lane
scenarios.description: A tractor hauling a wind-turbine blade overhangs 2 m into ego's adjacent lane on a curve, blade tip sweeping inward.
scenarios.mechanism: Blade pivot geometry means the overhang depth varies through the curve; at apex the intruding width peaks exactly where sightlines are shortest.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds >=0.5 m clearance from predicted max sweep envelope; speed matched to pilot-car pacing; no phantom-brake on legal pass sections
scenarios.trainingValue: Dynamic overhang envelope requires modeling articulated geometry over path curvature, not bounding-box logic.

scenarios.name: Oversize convoy requiring shoulder stop
scenarios.description: Escort vehicle flags ego to pull onto a narrow shoulder as the oversize module needs the full road at a bridge.
scenarios.mechanism: Escort waves ego down at a pinch point; ego must execute a complete shoulder stop and restart sequence timed to escort's release signal amid following traffic that hasn't yet seen the flag.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop fully on shoulder within 8 s of flag; restart only after escort release gesture; rear-end risk managed via early brake lights
scenarios.trainingValue: Hand-flagged full-stop choreography with rear-traffic management — cooperation scenario absent from normal driving data.

scenarios.name: Driverless roller creeping along work zone lane
scenarios.description: An asphalt roller operates semi-autonomously at 4 km/h occupying the left lane of a work zone with no visible operator.
scenarios.mechanism: Machine compacts in overlapping passes, drifting toward the lane edge periodically; its operator-less cab denies the usual human-eye-contact check, and it reverses direction at pass ends.
scenarios.successSignature: Pass executed with >=1 m clearance during drift phases; reversal at pass end anticipated (decel pre-positioned); zero entry onto fresh tack
