scenarios.trainingValue: Unmanned construction machinery with oscillating trajectory tests prediction of industrial duty cycles.

scenarios.name: Skid-steer loader crossing between stockpiles
scenarios.description: A skid-steer repeatedly shuttles perpendicular across the open lane between material piles, 5 s round trip.
scenarios.mechanism: Crossings are periodic but jittered; ego must find insertion windows between crossings while the loader's bucket raises and blocks its own visibility profile.
environment: road reconstruction site using live lane
scenarios.successSignature: Gap acceptance: crossings attempted only with >=3 s window; abort if bucket raised; zero conflict <2 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Periodic-but-jittered crossing pattern trains window-based negotiation with construction machinery.

scenarios.name: Street sweeper brushing debris into ego path
scenarios.description: A street sweeper works the curb lane spinning brushes that flick gravel and bottles laterally into the adjacent lane ego occupies.
scenarios.mechanism: Brush ejection throws small debris across ego's lane at intermittent intervals synchronized with sweeper progress; ego must tolerate impacts-risk vs. changing lanes into the sweeper's own turning envelope.
scenarios.successSignature: Following distance >=20 m behind sweeper's ejection zone; no emergency maneuvers for sub-5 cm debris; lane change only with full sweeper-envelope clearance
scenarios.trainingValue: Continuous low-energy hazard source with spatial gradient — teaches graded response rather than binary obstacle logic.

scenarios.name: Sweeper U-turn mid-block
scenarios.description: A sweeper completes a curb pass and executes a mid-block U-turn against traffic to start the opposite side.
scenarios.mechanism: Its slow wide U-turn sweeps across both lanes; approaching ego sees sweeper angled ambiguously (passing vs turning) because sweepers lack standard turn signals on all corners.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn-intent classification within 2 s of angle deviation >15 degrees; yield with >=4 m stopping gap; resume only after sweeper straightens
scenarios.trainingValue: Specialty vehicle with ambiguous pose and incomplete signaling — intent inference from geometry alone.

scenarios.name: Garbage truck lifting bin while ego squeezes past
scenarios.description: Garbage truck's arm lifts a bin just as ego arrives; the arm's arc extends over the adjacent lane ego must use.
scenarios.mechanism: Arm sweep creates a transient overhead/lateral obstruction; ego must decide whether to wait out the 6 s lift cycle or thread under/past the arm envelope while the truck's mirror sticks out.
scenarios.successSignature: Wait-or-thread decision consistent with measured arm envelope; if threading, clearance >=0.5 m from arm tip; following car informed via early decel
scenarios.trainingValue: Articulated mechanism extending beyond vehicle body — dynamic envelope estimation on familiar vehicles.

scenarios.name: Food truck queue spilling into travel lane
scenarios.description: A lunch queue at a food truck extends past the sidewalk onto the roadway shoulder, with people stepping back as orders are called.
scenarios.mechanism: Queue tail grows into the parking lane and periodically surges backward when names are called, injecting pedestrians into the roadway in bursts rather than steady flow.
environment: bike lane between queue and traffic
scenarios.successSignature: Speed reduced to <=15 km/h within influence zone; lateral buffer to nearest queue member >=1.2 m; surge responses within 0.5 s onset
scenarios.trainingValue: Bursty crowd dynamics tied to external audio cues — models crowd behavior beyond smooth flow assumptions.

scenarios.name: Food truck departing through its own queue
scenarios.description: A food truck pulls away from the curb, cutting through the remaining line of customers who scatter.
scenarios.mechanism: Truck departure scatters pedestrians into both the bike lane and travel lane simultaneously; ego faces multi-directional human influx with the truck itself merging into traffic ahead.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop within 1.5 s of departure cue; resume only after scattered peds clear; truck merge tracked without phantom-yield
scenarios.trainingValue: Vehicle-departure-triggered crowd dispersal — compound event chaining a commercial behavior to pedestrian safety.

scenarios.name: Disabled van angled across shoulder and lane
scenarios.description: A stalled minivan sits at 30 degrees, nose on shoulder, tail occupying half the travel lane with hazards on.
scenarios.mechanism: Partial-lane occupancy forces a merge decision at the exact point a tow truck arrives and opens its door into the same gap ego targeted.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane change executed with >=2 s gap before door-open event OR aborted cleanly; occupant clearance >=1.5 m throughout pass
scenarios.trainingValue: Static disable evolving into dynamic door/occupant hazard — timing-dependent threat transition.

scenarios.name: Stalled car hidden by crest then revealed rolling backward
scenarios.description: A stalled sedan just over a hillcrest begins rolling backward into ego's lane as its driver abandons it.
scenarios.mechanism: Crest hides the car until 60 m; simultaneously park-release sets it rolling downgrade across ego's path at increasing speed, so reveal and motion onset coincide.
scenarios.successSignature: Post-reveal reaction <=0.5 s; intercept solution computed for moving obstacle (not static brake); lateral miss or stop with >=1 m gap
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion reveal coincident with obstacle acquiring velocity — compounds two hard perception/planning problems at once.

scenarios.name: Flatbed with steel beams shifting on curve
scenarios.description: A flatbed's unsecured steel beam bundle visibly shifts and extends past the deck edge on a tight ramp curve.
scenarios.mechanism: Centrifugal load walks the bundle outward; by ramp exit beams overhang 1 m laterally into the passing space, converting a legal pass into an unsafe one progressively.
scenarios.successSignature: Pass attempt abandoned when overhang detected (>=0.5 m beyond deck); following gap reopened >=30 m; no overhang contact within 1 m margin
scenarios.trainingValue: Gradually worsening hazard rewards continuous re-evaluation of pass feasibility instead of snapshot decisions.

scenarios.name: Wide-load flatbed blocking both lanes at gate
scenarios.description: A flatbed carrying a prefabricated building section is 4.5 m wide and momentarily spans both lanes of a two-lane road at a rail crossing gate.
scenarios.mechanism: Its width pins ego behind it precisely where the gate arm descends; ego must stop short of tracks with the wide load crawling ahead, managing queue space behind.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop positioned >=6 m from outer rail regardless of flatbed pressure; queue-space maintained; resume only after flatbed clears gate zone
scenarios.trainingValue: Forced-follow into a constrained hazard zone — spatial trap requiring preemptive positioning.

scenarios.name: Watermelon rolling off produce truck at intersection
scenarios.description: Watermelons drop off a produce truck's tailgate as it accelerates from a light; several roll and split across the crosswalk.
scenarios.mechanism: Round fruit follows divergent rolling paths — some into ego's turn arc, one splitting into pulp that reduces friction where the crosswalk aligns with ego's acceleration zone.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn executed around rolling melons with >=0.8 m clearance; traction-aware acceleration through pulp zone (no wheelspin trigger >10% slip)
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-object scatter with soft-hazard residue combines dynamic avoidance and surface-state adaptation in one event.

scenarios.name: Cones cascading off road-construction truck
scenarios.description: A contractor truck's unsecured cone rack discharges cones one by one over 200 m of freeway, scattering across three lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Cones fall sequentially as truck hits expansion joints, creating a moving debris field whose density peaks mid-stream; drivers weave unpredictably around the cone trail.
scenarios.successSignature: Corridor through cone field chosen with >=1 s predicted neighbor-gap; cone strikes avoided entirely; speed reduction <=15 km/h delta from flow
scenarios.trainingValue: Sequential-debris field with correlated neighbor behavior — tests corridor planning under distributed small obstacles.

scenarios.name: Traffic barrel rolling between lanes on wind gust
scenarios.description: An empty construction barrel tips in a gust and rolls across two freeway lanes at ~15 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Lightweight barrel rolls predictably but rebounds off a car strike, reversing direction mid-crossing; its low mass tempts wrong 'drive through' choices at speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Post-bounce trajectory update within 300 ms; decision consistent with barrel mass model (avoid, not absorb); clearance >=0.5 m at final crossing
scenarios.trainingValue: Bounce-reversal dynamics break linear extrapolation; tests mid-event replanning on lightweight objects.

scenarios.name: Pallet shattered across lane by truck tail-swing
scenarios.description: A delivery truck's rear pallet drags off at a tight corner and shatters, spreading planks and shrink wrap across the intersection.
scenarios.mechanism: Tail-sweep during the truck's tight turn rips the pallet loose; planks lie at varied angles presenting sharp edges while wrap film adheres to the pavement as a traction trap.
scenarios.successSignature: Path avoiding plank edges with >=0.3 m margin; wrap-film segment crossed at <=20 km/h with straight steering; no debris displacement into other actors
scenarios.trainingValue: Mixed-rigidity debris (rigid planks + compliant film) demands heterogeneous avoidance strategies in one scene.

scenarios.name: Dump truck tailgate spill trailing gravel blast
scenarios.description: A dump truck with a fouled latch spills gravel in pulses; rocks bounce off the pavement into following lanes at head height for sedans.
scenarios.mechanism: Each pulse ejects stones that ricochet upward-and-backward into ego's windshield zone; safe response is distance opening, but the truck also slows for its turn, compressing the following gap decision.
scenarios.successSignature: Gap opened to >=50 m within 3 s of first spill pulse; lane change away from ejection cone; no windshield-strike exposure windows >1 s
scenarios.trainingValue: Projectile-emitting lead vehicle — protective spacing behavior with time pressure from the lead's turn plan.

scenarios.name: Escalating furniture: couch then dresser sequence
scenarios.description: An overloaded moving truck loses a couch at 80 km/h, then a dresser 400 m later as the driver brakes in surprise.
scenarios.mechanism: First loss forces ego to change lanes; the dresser drop occurs exactly in the lane ego just merged into, punishing commitment to the escape route without re-scanning.
scenarios.successSignature: Second obstacle detected during first avoidance; recovery maneuver executed with >=1 s TTC or controlled stop; no freeze/oscillation between targets
scenarios.trainingValue: Sequenced losses invalidate completed plans — tests persistent monitoring of the source vehicle after initial avoidance.

scenarios.name: Loose calf on livestock-truck ramp gap
scenarios.description: A calf escapes through a gap in a livestock truck's ramp at a fuel stop and bolts onto the highway shoulder then lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Calf exits from a stopped truck in an unexpected location (fuel stop frontage), entering the road at an angle trucks never do; its 30 km/h bolt crosses ego's lane in ~2 s from occlusion behind the truck.
scenarios.successSignature: Calf detected despite truck occlusion (motion/audio cues); brake initiated within 0.4 s of lane entry; stop gap >=3 m
scenarios.trainingValue: Animal entry from vehicle-mediated occlusion at non-roadway locations — generalizes animal handling off natural habitats.

scenarios.name: Wheelbarrow blown across bike lane into road
scenarios.description: An empty wheelbarrow left by a landscaper catches wind, rolls across the planting strip, bike lane, and into the travel lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Wheelbarrow's wheel alignment gives it a curved rolling path that arcs into the travel lane just as a cyclist swerves to avoid it, stacking two actors into ego's corridor.
scenarios.successSignature: Arc trajectory predicted to road-entry point; cyclist displacement yielded-to with >=1 m clearance; wheelbarrow intercepted path avoided with TTC >=1.5 s
scenarios.trainingValue: Curved-roll dynamics plus chaser-plus-swerver stack — three-actor causal chain from one unsecured tool.

scenarios.name: Inflatable tube man collapsing across lane
scenarios.description: A car dealership's inflatable tube man loses blower power mid-gust and flops down across the adjacent travel lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Deflation converts a vertical sign into a wide fabric banner lying across the lane; its prior constant motion caused classifiers to track it as background, so the sudden state change evades detection.
scenarios.successSignature: Collapse detected as new obstacle within 1 s of lane entry; fabric avoided or crossed per mass model without evasive swerve into adjacent traffic
scenarios.trainingValue: State-change camouflage: object transitions from ignored background to blocker, attacking tracker persistence assumptions.

scenarios.name: Hot-air balloon basket dragging on road
scenarios.description: A low balloon's drag rope and basket skim a rural road, the rope snapping taut across ego's lane as the balloon rises.
scenarios.mechanism: Rope lies slack across the lane invisible until lift tension snaps it upward; the rising basket then traverses the roadway at 10 m altitude dropping ballast water ahead of ego.
scenarios.successSignature: Rope snap-up treated as transient (no permanent obstacle assumption); ballast splash handled as friction event with traction-consistent decel; vertical clearance respected until basket exits
scenarios.trainingValue: Vertical-dimension actor with staged states (rope, basket, discharge) exercising rarely-used 3D reasoning.

scenarios.name: Kayak sliding off car roof into intersection
scenarios.description: A kayak slides forward off a sedan's roof racks under hard braking and spears into the intersection box ahead.
scenarios.mechanism: Brake-induced slide launches the kayak bow-first through the crosswalk while pedestrians jump back; its hollow hull spins slowly, sweeping a 3 m radius.
scenarios.successSignature: Spin radius respected with >=0.5 m margin; pedestrian scatter given priority; hull stop position mapped before resuming turn
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-friction elongated cargo with rotational dynamics — geometric sweep avoidance beyond point-object models.

scenarios.name: Trash bag burst scattering contents into lane
scenarios.description: A curb-side trash bag ruptures under a car tire, spraying cans and glass across the bike lane and travel lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Impact burst distributes debris radially; glass shards occupy the bike lane pushing cyclists into ego's lane seconds after the visual clutter of flying trash distracts classifiers.
scenarios.successSignature: Cyclist displacement anticipated from debris footprint; ego speed <=20 km/h through glass zone; lateral support of bike-lane closure communicated via positioning
scenarios.trainingValue: Explosive debris event with delayed secondary actor displacement — temporal staging within a single incident.

scenarios.name: Garden tractor towing trailer wobbling at 15 km/h
scenarios.description: A garden tractor towing an overloaded utility trailer wobbles (trailer sway) while holding up a line of cars on a no-passing rural road.
scenarios.mechanism: Trailer sway amplifies with speed and each sway cycle extends the combination's width past lane edges; impatient followers begin risky passes, and ego must handle both slow leader and illegal passer.
scenarios.successSignature: Following distance >=25 m accounting for sway envelope; illegal passer yielded to safely (positioned for escape); no pass attempt mirrored
scenarios.trainingValue: Oscillating-width slow leader plus rule-breaking third party — combined restraint and defensive positioning training.

scenarios.name: Porta-potty tipped by wind across bike path
scenarios.description: A gust topples a construction porta-potty from its pad across the adjacent bike lane and partially into the roadway.
scenarios.mechanism: Topple is preceded by rocking for ~2 s giving predictive cues; occupants' exit afterward places a person at the fallen unit's door which now opens into the roadway.
scenarios.successSignature: Rocking-phase prediction triggers pre-positioning; post-topple occupant given >=1.5 m clearance; blocked-path lane merge executed with work-zone traffic respect
scenarios.trainingValue: Pre-event physical cues reward anticipatory planning; aftermath includes human egress from unexpected container.

scenarios.name: Beach umbrella cart-wheeling down the roadway
scenarios.description: A closed beach umbrella blows from a sidewalk stand and cartwheels down the street end-over-end, tracking the lane center.
scenarios.mechanism: Umbrella's canopy catches gusts in rhythmic flips, advancing down the lane centerline faster than cyclists; its intermittent ground contact makes bounce points the key prediction targets.
scenarios.successSignature: Bounce-cycle prediction accurate to one bounce period (±0.5 s); cyclist pursuit yielded-to; interception avoided with >=1 s margin
scenarios.trainingValue: Aerodynamic periodic-motion object plus pursuing human — playful but rigorous dynamic-object benchmark.

scenarios.name: Hay bales rolling off trailer on grade
scenarios.description: Round hay bales roll off an unsecured flatbed on a slight grade, two cylinders rolling down the crowned road toward the shoulder ego uses to pass.
scenarios.mechanism: Road crown steers the rolling bales toward the south shoulder exactly where ego steers to pass the stopped trailer; bale speed builds with grade, converging paths.
scenarios.successSignature: Pass aborted or retimed so bale crossing point clears by >=2 s; bale positions continuously tracked; no shoulder entry into bale corridor
scenarios.trainingValue: Environment geometry (crown) actively shapes hazard trajectories — coupling road-model knowledge with object dynamics.

scenarios.name: Faded Stop Bar Ambiguity
scenarios.description: An intersection's stop bar and crosswalk paint have faded to near-invisibility, leaving the legal stopping point ambiguous; a pedestrian crosses where the crosswalk used to be.
scenarios.mechanism: The missing bar removes ego's yield anchor, so ego creeps forward past parked cars while the pedestrian treats the invisible crosswalk as valid and enters the creep path — a late-yield with shrinking TTC.
environment: stop bar and crosswalk worn to faint traces
scenarios.successSignature: Yield with TTC >= 3 s and stop within 2 m of the mapped stop line despite zero visible paint.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests map-based stop-line priors versus visual marking detection.

scenarios.name: Old Paint Under New Paint Turn-Lane Conflict
scenarios.description: A turn lane was re-striped 30 m upstream but the old channelization lines are still visible; a lead driver follows the old faded taper and swerves into ego's lane at the last moment.
scenarios.mechanism: The lead driver reads the old visible taper as the turn lane, decelerates late and drifts right across the new solid line into ego's path, forcing brake-or-evade where the new geometry says the lead is illegally crossing.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains >= 4 m lateral clearance or decel <= 4 m/s^2 without crossing the new solid line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers paint-on-paint contradictions that break lane-detection models calibrated on one crisp marking set.

scenarios.name: Temporary Centerline Tape Contradiction
scenarios.description: During trench restoration, temporary tape shifts the centerline 1 m left but the old centerline remains visible; an oncoming driver straddles the old line and occupies ego's lane through the narrowed section.
scenarios.mechanism: The oncoming driver trusts the familiar old centerline, closing ego's lane head-on; ego must slow and shade right within a corridor defined only by barricades.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego slows to <= 30 km/h before the conflict point and keeps >= 1.5 m net lateral gap from the oncoming pickup.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains robustness when both map and dominant visual marking are wrong and barricades define the true corridor.

scenarios.name: Ghost Left-Turn Pocket
scenarios.description: Faded markings and an old asphalt patch outline a left-turn pocket removed by a median retrofit; a driver ahead slows to swing into the nonexistent pocket directly in front of ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Ghost geometry invites the lead to decelerate and angle left where a solid median now stands; ego must absorb the surprise decel where the median eliminates any left escape path.
actors: lead SUV slowing for ghost pocket
environment: median retrofit over old turn lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves headway >= 1.2 s before the lead's speed drops below 40% of ego's.
scenarios.trainingValue: Punishes planners keying on lane-geometry appearance rather than authoritative current layout.

scenarios.name: Short-Cycle Temporary Signal Launch
scenarios.description: A one-lane work-zone alternation uses a temporary signal with a 20-second green; ego is released behind a slow loaded dump truck and cannot clear before opposing release.
scenarios.mechanism: The short cycle assumes fast clearance but the truck accelerates at half rate, so ego's green expires mid-section as opposing traffic releases — a head-on closure window.
environment: single-lane work zone on rural two-lane road
scenarios.successSignature: Clear >= 3 s before opposing release or stop fully within its half with >= 20 m gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Signal reasoning under nonstandard timings where cycle-length priors fail and clearance dynamics matter.

scenarios.name: Faulty Temporary Signal All-Red
scenarios.description: A temporary work-zone signal hangs in all-red due to a fault; drivers improvise gaps and one crosses on ego's tentative launch, creating a mid-zone conflict the signal was meant to prevent.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal failure dissolves the alternation protocol, making right-of-way negotiated; an improvising driver entering during ego's launch forces ego to re-derive right-of-way from behavior rather than signal state.
actors: improvising sedan entering on ego's move
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts launch with decel <= 3 m/s^2 upon detecting the intruder and yields until the zone is verifiably clear.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exercises degraded signal-state perception and negotiation behavior no fixed-timing planner handles by default.

scenarios.name: Desynced Temporary and Permanent Signals
scenarios.description: A temporary work-zone signal one block downstream of a permanent signal has uncoordinated timing; the permanent green releases a platoon that spills back and traps ego in the first intersection.
scenarios.mechanism: Platoon discharge fills the block across the temporary stop bar; when cross traffic later releases, ego is boxed in with flow passing close ahead.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop clear of the box (>= 2 m behind the far crosswalk) and hold with zero encroachment through the cross phase.
scenarios.trainingValue: Anticipating spillback from uncoordinated signals, a top cause of real intersection blockage.

scenarios.name: Flagger Paddle Mid-Approach Flip
scenarios.description: A flagger holding SLOW rotates the paddle to STOP when ego is 60 m out at 50 km/h, simultaneously waving an opposing truck out of the single-lane section toward ego.
scenarios.mechanism: The paddle flip revokes ego's right of way mid-approach while the released opposing truck closes head-on; ego must combine required decel with trusting the flagger's gesture over its momentum-based plan.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates <= 3.5 m/s^2 to a full stop >= 5 m before the flagger and holds until an explicit go gesture.
scenarios.trainingValue: Paddle semantics (SLOW advisory, STOP a revocable command) must gate the right-of-way state machine in real time.

scenarios.name: Unsynchronized Double-Flagger Zone
scenarios.description: On a long single-lane section the upstream flagger releases ego but the downstream flagger stops traffic mid-section for equipment; ego meets a stopped queue inside the single lane as oncoming release begins.
scenarios.mechanism: Desynchronized flaggers commit ego into a section occupied from both ends with no legal escape.
environment: 800 m single-lane zone on rural highway
scenarios.successSignature: Stop with >= 10 m gap and reach a pullout or hold with no opposing-lane encroachment > 5 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Coordination failure testing mid-route re-planning inside an inescapable corridor.

scenarios.name: AFAD Gate Ignored by Impatient Driver
scenarios.description: An automated flagger assistance device with a physical STOP gate controls the zone; a driver on the opposing approach drives around the lowered gate, entering ego's single lane head-on.
scenarios.mechanism: Gate-running breaks the alternation protocol; ego, freshly released, faces a wrong-way intruder in a corridor narrowed by concrete barrier with no shoulder.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego brakes to <= 15 km/h within the zone and keeps >= 1 m lateral clearance from the intruder without barrier contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers automation-assisted control points where one violator converts a protected phase into a head-on scenario.

scenarios.name: Pilot Car Alternation Handoff
scenarios.description: On an unpaved reconstruction stretch a pilot car leads alternating traffic; ego is released by the flagger but the pilot departs early, and an opposing vehicle appears before ego clears.
scenarios.mechanism: The flagger-to-pilot handoff has a timing hole; ego must detect that the pilot is not pacing it and that the opposing release window overlaps its remaining exposure.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego matches pilot speed within 5 km/h or aborts to the release point before the opposing vehicle closes within 5 s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Pilot-car ops exercise convoy-following plus protocol-trust under dust-degraded perception.

scenarios.name: Double Closure Shoulder Escape Conflict
scenarios.description: A freeway zone closes both right lane and shoulder; ego merges left as an ambulance uses the closed shoulder behind the barrier while a lead car brakes hard at the taper.
scenarios.mechanism: Closing the shoulder removes the escape space, so the ambulance coincides with taper braking that compresses the queue.
scenarios.successSignature: Merge with >= 3 s TTC to the ambulance path, decel <= 4 m/s^2, >= 2 m from barrier.
scenarios.trainingValue: Closure geometry and emergency privileges consuming the same space demand joint reasoning.

scenarios.name: Moveable Barrier Mid-Transition Width
scenarios.description: A zipper-barrier machine shifts configuration between setups; ego meets the half-transitioned state where lanes run 20 cm narrower than the HD map and a bus tracks the true edge.
scenarios.mechanism: Mid-shift positions give transient widths no static map holds; the bus overlaps ego's mapped lane, forcing observed-not-mapped positioning.
actors: city bus at true lane edge
scenarios.successSignature: Slow to <= 45 km/h and keep >= 30 cm clearance to the bus without crossing the barrier line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Moveable barriers make lane width time-varying; breaks map-equals-physics assumptions.

scenarios.name: Barrier-Narrowed Lane Cone Strike
scenarios.description: Temporary concrete barrier leaves a 3.0 m lane with no shoulder; a wide truck hogs the lane and clips the cone line, sending cones tumbling into ego's path at 80 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: The narrowed lane forces the truck onto the cones; displaced cones become moving obstacles in ego's lane with barrier on the right removing lateral escape, demanding a decelerating weave in a compressed corridor.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego avoids all cones with >= 0.5 m lateral offset and keeps >= 1.0 s headway to the truck, no barrier contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dynamic cone motion plus zero-shoulder geometry is distinct from the static cone fields common in training data.

scenarios.name: Worker Reach Into Lane Beside Cones
scenarios.description: Cones narrow the lane past a patching crew; a worker leans 0.5 m into ego's lane to reposition a knocked-over cone just as ego passes at the 40 km/h work-zone limit.
scenarios.mechanism: The worker's reach converts the cone line from boundary to incursion; ego must trade lateral clearance against oncoming traffic in the open lane with the demand created by the worker's motion, not static cones.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego slows to <= 25 km/h before passing the worker with >= 1.2 m clearance to the worker and >= 1.0 m to the oncoming car.
scenarios.trainingValue: Distinguishing a static cone line from an actively worked edge is a perception-plus-prediction gap behind real work-zone strikes.

scenarios.name: Displaced Cone Ambiguity
scenarios.description: Wind and traffic scattered part of a cone taper; two lanes appear partially open and the lead vehicle brakes hard mid-lane deciding, forcing ego to commit under uncertainty.
scenarios.mechanism: Scattered cones destroy the taper's legibility, so the lead's hesitation brake is caused by ambiguous channelization; ego inherits a hard-brake response at short headway with no legible open path itself.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego keeps >= 1.5 s headway through the brake event and selects a lane consistent with the true boundary without stopping.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains open-lane inference from partial channelization plus car-following through another agent's uncertainty-driven braking.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous SLOW Paddle Target
scenarios.description: A worker walks the cone line carrying a SLOW paddle, raising it intermittently; ego cannot tell whether the paddle addresses ego or the opposing queue while the worker drifts toward the lane edge distracted.
scenarios.mechanism: Intermittent paddle raises create alternating advisory states with no clear addressee; the worker's drift compounds instruction uncertainty with incursion risk.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds <= 30 km/h through the worker segment and never treats a paddle raise as a stop command unless paired with a STOP face.
scenarios.trainingValue: Instruction attribution is a real reasoning gap; correct response calibrates speed rather than binary stop/go.

scenarios.name: Surveyor Steps Back With Prism Pole
scenarios.description: A surveyor eyes on the total station walks backward carrying a 2 m prism pole that sweeps into ego's lane; a parked van occludes him until the last 15 m.
scenarios.mechanism: Backward walking while instrument-focused means no head checks; occlusion compresses detection so the pole arrives with < 1.5 s visibility.
scenarios.successSignature: Pass at <= 20 km/h with >= 1.0 m pole clearance, or stop with TTC >= 2 s if it enters earlier.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occlusion plus distracted actors near the travel lane maps to real strike incidents.

scenarios.name: Crawling Striping Convoy Overtake Decision
scenarios.description: A marking convoy paints the centerline at 10 km/h in a no-passing zone; an impatient driver ahead of ego pulls out just as a crest hides an oncoming truck.
scenarios.mechanism: Queue pressure from the crawl triggers the risky overtake; the crest-hidden truck turns it into a three-body conflict resolved by ego opening an escape gap.
scenarios.successSignature: Detect overtake initiation and drop >= 15 km/h within 2 s, giving the truck >= 4 s TTC to the lead.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mobile work zones induce third-party risk-taking; requires predicting driver frustration, not tracking the convoy.

scenarios.name: Cone Truck Brake-Check Placement
scenarios.description: A cone-laying truck advances the taper by braking hard to place each cone; ego closes at 60 km/h behind it while the chase vehicle blocks the only lateral gap and the truck stops at ego's projected passing point.
scenarios.mechanism: Cone placement cadence produces periodic full stops with no warning beyond brake lights; ego's closing geometry intersects the next placement stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates placement cadence, holding >= 2.5 s headway with no hard-brake response (< 4 m/s^2) across two placement stops.
scenarios.trainingValue: Periodic stop patterns of utility vehicles are learnable; rewards cadence prediction over pure reactive braking.

scenarios.name: Weaving Striping Escort Protection
scenarios.description: A striping escort with flashing arrow board weaves between lanes to protect the paint truck, alternately closing left and right lanes; ego's planned lane is closed, reopened, and closed again within 400 m.
scenarios.mechanism: The escort's protection flips open-lane state faster than signage communicates, invalidating ego's route plan mid-execution against adjacent platoons.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego completes lane changes with TTC >= 4 s to the adjacent platoon and never enters a lane while the arrow board protects it.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mobile protection flips exercise rapid plan invalidation and arrow-board semantics fixed signage never covers.

scenarios.name: Storm-Downed Speed Sign Curve Overbrake
scenarios.description: A storm knocked down the curve-warning and speed-limit signs at a sharp rural bend; the lead finds the curve late and over-brakes to 20 km/h while a trailing driver closes fast behind ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Missing signage delays every driver's curve detection, producing lead over-brake plus trailing closure; ego must infer safe speed from geometry alone.
scenarios.successSignature: Enter the curve at <= 40 km/h with >= 2 s headway to the lead and early brake lights for trailing drivers.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sign-absent speed inference plus two-sided surprise tests generalization beyond signage-driven expectations.

scenarios.name: Misplaced Work-Zone Sign Traps Lead Driver
scenarios.description: A ROAD WORK AHEAD sign was placed 200 m after the taper and a detour arrow points the wrong way; the lead driver brakes at the unwarned taper then follows the bad arrow across ego's path.
scenarios.mechanism: The placement error creates both an unwarned taper (lead hard brake) and a false route (lead turning across ego); both demands trace to the misplaced signs, not actor intent.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates the unwarned taper (decel <= 3 m/s^2) and predicts the detour turn early enough to hold >= 3 s TTC through the crossing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Infrastructure errors, not just actor errors, must be anticipated; trains reasoning from observed signage inconsistency.

scenarios.name: Occluded Signal-Ahead Sign Late Discovery
scenarios.description: Overgrown vegetation hides the SIGNAL AHEAD sign on a high-speed approach; the lead driver sees the red signal late and brakes from 80 km/h at 90 m, inside ego's comfortable following distance.
scenarios.mechanism: The occluded sign removes the lead's early cue, shifting its braking point 100 m closer; ego's demand is the lead's late hard decel, anticipatable only by noticing the same occlusion.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego opens headway to >= 2.5 s before the lead's brake onset and decelerates <= 3.5 m/s^2 to the red.
scenarios.trainingValue: Rewards proactive headway management from environmental cues rather than reactive brake-light following.

scenarios.name: Late-Revealed Ramp Closure Hard Stop
scenarios.description: An incident closed a freeway ramp but the DO NOT ENTER panel sits past the curve; the lead car stops mid-ramp on late discovery and the trailing SUV behind ego brakes even later.
scenarios.mechanism: Late sign revelation produces a braking cascade ordered by sight lines; ego is compressed between a stopped leader and a late-braking follower, both caused by the sign past the sight-line break.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops >= 3 m behind the lead with decel <= 5 m/s^2, zero collision, and mitigates rear risk (hazards, creep-forward if clear).
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains sandwiched-braking mitigation where ego must manage front and rear risk from one cause.

scenarios.name: Reversed Detour on One-Way Street
scenarios.description: A crash detour runs the wrong way up a normally one-way street with minimal signage; ego enters legally per the detour and meets an oncoming driver who never saw the sign.
scenarios.mechanism: Two contradictory direction beliefs share one street; ego must resolve the head-on meeting by yielding into narrow curb space rather than asserting right of way.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies the conflict at >= 40 m and executes a pull-in yield with >= 1 m clearance, no oscillation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Direction-of-travel must downgrade from map priors under temporary control; narrow reversed-flow negotiation is rare but critical.

scenarios.name: HD Map Shows Closed Lane Open
scenarios.description: A lane closure was installed after the last map update; the HD map still shows the lane open, so ego plans through it and the taper appears only 150 m ahead against a dense platoon.
scenarios.mechanism: Map-versus-world mismatch removes the early merge cue; the demand is the short taper plus platoon gaps, both from the stale belief.
scenarios.successSignature: Detect the closure within 200 m via perception and merge with TTC >= 3 s, decel <= 3 m/s^2, no shoulder use.
scenarios.trainingValue: Perception-over-map arbitration under closure is a highest-value stale-map failure.

scenarios.name: HD Map Missing New Bypass Lane
scenarios.description: A construction bypass opened this week, absent from the map; ego stays in the mapped lane, closed 300 m ahead, while local traffic uses the unmapped bypass at free flow.
scenarios.mechanism: The unmapped bypass drains traffic, isolating ego at the mapped lane's closure with a short taper onto sparse high-speed flow.
environment: highway construction with new bypass alignment
scenarios.successSignature: Identify the bypass as drivable from observed traffic, enter with TTC >= 4 s, never follow the mapped lane in.
scenarios.trainingValue: The inverse stale-map error — trusting a deprecated mapped lane — defeats pure map-following planners.

scenarios.name: Signal Converted to Temporary Four-Way Stop
scenarios.description: During reconstruction the permanent signal is bagged and a temporary four-way stop installed; the HD map still models signal phases, so ego arrives expecting a green wave.
scenarios.mechanism: The map predicts cross traffic held by a red, but stop control gives everyone equal claim; cross vehicles legitimately enter per the protocol ego's plan lacks.
scenarios.successSignature: Detect the stop control, stop completely at the line, proceed only after >= 2 s turn-order observation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Control-mode reclassification from perception differs from phase prediction.

scenarios.name: Unposted Temporary Speed Limit Mismatch
scenarios.description: A temporary 30 km/h limit covers a bridge-joint zone on a road mapped at 70; drivers brake hard at an enforcement point ego's map says does not exist while a tailgater expects the old speed.
scenarios.mechanism: The unmapped limit changes both directions: leaders brake for the camera, followers press ego; the cause is the temporary sign's behavioral effect, not ego's speed choice.
scenarios.successSignature: Adopt <= 30 km/h before the camera, keep >= 1.5 s headway both ways, no hard-brake event.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporary limits need sign-level speed arbitration over map priors plus managing the two-sided mismatch.

scenarios.name: Steel Plate Wobble Ahead of Ego
scenarios.description: Steel plates cover a trench under an advisory 30 km/h limit; a motorcycle ahead hits a shifted plate edge and wobbles violently, forcing emergency space creation by ego.
scenarios.mechanism: The displaced edge injects a lateral impulse into the motorcycle; ego must predict erratic trajectory within the plate field's own limit.
scenarios.successSignature: Drop >= 10 km/h below advisory on detecting plates and give the motorcycle >= 2.5 m lateral buffer.
scenarios.trainingValue: Couples surface-state perception to VRU trajectory uncertainty inflation.

scenarios.name: Off-Season School Flashers Active
scenarios.description: Summer school keeps the flashers running at 14:00 in July when habit expects them off; the lead ignores the flasher at 50 km/h just as children exit a program van near the curb.
scenarios.mechanism: The unexpected flasher splits traffic: the lead speeds through while a child's exit creates a curb-side incursion crossing the lead's wake.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds <= 30 km/h and yields >= 3 s TTC to any curb-side pedestrian despite the lead's noncompliance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Calendar-prior versus posted-control conflicts train obedience to physical signal state over expected schedule.

scenarios.name: School Flasher Stuck On, Guard Enforces
scenarios.description: The beacon is stuck flashing during a holiday when the zone is inactive; drivers ignore it, but a crossing guard still stops traffic for stragglers, splitting beacon state from human command.
scenarios.mechanism: The stuck beacon devalues the flasher, so cars fail to stop for the guard; ego faces the guard's command plus noncompliant vehicles passing through the space ego yields into.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops fully within 5 m of the crosswalk and holds until the guard's explicit release regardless of beacon state.
scenarios.trainingValue: Human authority must outrank degraded automated signals when the two disagree.

scenarios.name: School Flasher Failed Off During Hours
scenarios.description: The beacon fails dark during active morning hours; nobody slows, and children cross mid-block because a delivery truck blocks the crosswalk, landing them in a 50 km/h flow.
scenarios.mechanism: The dark beacon removes the collective slow-down suppressing mid-block risk; the children's improvised crossing meets traffic behaving as if no school zone exists.
scenarios.successSignature: Enter at <= 30 km/h from schedule knowledge, detect children by >= 2.5 s TTC, no braking above 4 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Failure-off controls demand knowledge-driven caution where visual cues invite speed.

scenarios.name: Drawbridge Gate Descent Timing
scenarios.description: Ego approaches a drawbridge at 50 km/h as bells start and gate arms descend; the barrier lands at ego's arrival point in 3 s while the lead accelerates to beat it.
scenarios.mechanism: Gate descent sets a hard deadline that the lead's gamble compresses further; demand comes from barrier kinematics intersecting the lead's acceleration.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop >= 2 m before the gate line, decel <= 4 m/s^2, never crossing below horizontal arm even with the lead's gap offer.
scenarios.trainingValue: Moving-barrier deadlines plus rule-breaking exercise kinematics fixed signals cannot produce.

scenarios.name: Drawbridge Gate Arm Failure
scenarios.description: Warning lights flash but both gate arms failed up; the bridge is rising, one sedan crosses anyway, and a queue builds behind ego unsure whether to follow.
scenarios.mechanism: Arm failure decouples warning from barrier, making crossing a judgment call for everyone; ego faces the crossing sedan plus queue hesitation from the barrier's absent authority.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop and hold >= 10 m from the span gap for the full opening; never follow anyone across.
scenarios.trainingValue: Control-authority reasoning when enforcement fails but hazard persists.

scenarios.name: Ferry Dock Reverse-Load Marshaling
scenarios.description: Ferry crew direct vehicles to back aboard in reverse load order while walk-on passengers thread between queued cars; gestures contradict the painted dock lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Load order commands last-in vehicles first, overriding lane paint; ego faces the adjacent vehicle's commanded reverse move plus passengers in the same space.
scenarios.successSignature: Follow crew commands over paint holding >= 2 m to the backing SUV and >= 1.5 m to passengers, zero ramp-edge encroachment.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dock marshaling overrides painted infrastructure by protocol — key special-site competence.

scenarios.name: Unmanned Toll Cash Lane Sudden Stop
scenarios.description: At a toll plaza the lead enters the cash lane, finds no attendant, and stops at the basket while the electronic lane beside ego has a barrier gate stuck down on a misread transponder.
scenarios.mechanism: Staffing absence causes the mid-plaza stop and the gate fault pins ego's lateral escape, turning routine passage into a compound stop-and-trap.
scenarios.successSignature: Stop >= 4 m behind the lead and merge with TTC >= 3 s, or reverse only after full rear verification.
scenarios.trainingValue: Per-lane control faults create trap states unavailable on open road; key for toll-road deployment.

scenarios.name: Rail Crossing Stuck Gates Second Train
scenarios.description: Crossing gates are down with no train (fault); they rise after 90 s, drivers launch instantly, and a second train appears at speed as the queue commits.
scenarios.mechanism: The fault cycle teaches drivers the gates are unreliable, so the rise triggers immediate launches; the second train converts conditioned impatience into a crossing conflict.
scenarios.successSignature: Hold until all tracks are verifiably clear (>= 10 s observation); never cross during any active warning.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gate-reliability conditioning is a real hazard; compliance must survive infrastructure that taught drivers otherwise.

scenarios.name: Lane-Control Gantry X Mid-Block
scenarios.description: An overhead gantry shows a red X over ego's lane 200 m ahead; opposing traffic enters through a median break as ego merges while a distracted driver stays in the doomed lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The X revokes the lane's direction and the median break makes it physical; ego faces both a merge against a platoon and a wrong-way incursion from the break.
actors: noncompliant driver staying in X lane
scenarios.successSignature: Merge with TTC >= 3.5 s to the platoon and >= 4 s to the incursion, not entering the X lane beyond the gantry.
scenarios.trainingValue: Direction-revoking signals with physical consequences exceed advisory overhead signs; tests gantry semantics under violation.

scenarios.name: Reversible Center Lane Flip Rush Hour
scenarios.description: At 15:30 a center two-way-left-turn lane converts to inbound through lane per overhead signs; a driver mid-turn into a driveway stalls across the new inbound flow ego joins.
scenarios.mechanism: The scheduled flip redefines the lane while legacy users are mid-maneuver; the stalled vehicle blocks ego's newly legal lane as an oncoming platoon forms.
environment: five-lane arterial with reversible center lane
scenarios.successSignature: Verify the flip from overhead signals, enter at <= 40 km/h, and yield >= 3 s TTC around the stalled vehicle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Time-indexed lanes require reasoning about transition-period legacy users, not just current legal state.

scenarios.name: Reversible Entry Gate Wrong-Way Release
scenarios.description: A reversible-lane entrance with gate arms releases the opposite direction first; an impatient driver swings through the open opposite gate and enters the reversible lane backward relative to ego's pending release.
scenarios.mechanism: Gate sequencing opens a window for wrong-way entry; the entrant meets ego head-on in a barrier-lined corridor.
scenarios.successSignature: Detect at >= 100 m, decelerate to <= 30 km/h, reach the crossover or hold >= 5 s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gated entries concentrate wrong-way risk; barrier-lined head-on avoidance is survival-critical.

scenarios.name: Temporary Mini-Roundabout Yield Chaos
scenarios.description: A signalized intersection under reconstruction becomes a temporary mini-roundabout marked in paint with a center planter; drivers habituated to the old signal enter without yielding as ego circulates.
scenarios.mechanism: Habituation hides the mode change, so entries ignore the yield rule; a non-yielding entry crosses ego's circulating path.
environment: intersection under reconstruction with temporary roundabout
scenarios.successSignature: Ego circulates at <= 25 km/h, yields left at every entry, avoids the non-yielder with TTC >= 2.5 s and no stop inside the circle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Control-mode conversions break driver priors; circulating under violation risk differs from normal roundabout negotiation.

scenarios.name: Banner-Obscured Signal Head
scenarios.description: A work-zone banner strapped across the mast arm partly covers the signal heads; drivers read the adjacent intersection or pedestrian display and one enters on a misread phase as ego starts on green.
scenarios.mechanism: Degraded legibility causes phase misreads; ego's demand is the misreading vehicle entering on its green, caused by the banner rather than any signal fault.
scenarios.successSignature: Proceed on verified green but cover the brake with >= 2.5 s TTC mitigation against the entry.
scenarios.trainingValue: Legibility degradation shifts risk to compliant ego; reward defensive verification of others' reads.

scenarios.name: Dark Head, Live Ped Countdown
scenarios.description: A power fault darkens vehicle signal heads but the pedestrian countdown still runs; drivers adopt it as authoritative and one launches on flashing don't-walk as a pedestrian finishes crossing.
scenarios.mechanism: The countdown becomes the only phase signal, causing early launches; the head fault cascades into a vehicle-pedestrian conflict in ego's path.
environment: urban intersection during signal power fault
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats the junction as uncontrolled, yields to the pedestrian with TTC >= 3 s, and proceeds only after cross traffic confirms the phase.
scenarios.trainingValue: Partial-signal faults force reasoning about which displays remain trustworthy — absent from blackout scenarios.

scenarios.name: Springy Temporary Stop Sign Blowthrough
scenarios.description: A portable spring-mounted STOP sign controls an intersection normally uncontrolled during water-main work; habituated drivers blow through and one crosses ego's path after ego has committed.
scenarios.mechanism: The temporary sign lacks salience and driver priors, so compliance is low; the blowthrough crossing stems from the sign's low-authority presentation.
environment: residential intersection with temporary stop control
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop at the sign, >= 2 s cross-check, >= 3 s TTC to the blowthrough.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporary devices get systematically lower compliance; ego must model drivers' priors about the normal state.

scenarios.name: Conflicting Detour Signs Mid-Lane Stop
scenarios.description: Two overlapping projects posted contradictory detour arrows; the lead stops in-lane to read them and a second driver swerves around him into ego's lane without signaling.
scenarios.mechanism: Contradictory signage causes both the hesitation stop and the unsignaled swerve; ego faces a compound stop-and-swerve within 3 s at 50 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Hold >= 2 s headway into the stop and absorb the swerve with >= 1 m clearance, decel <= 4 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Trains prediction of human confusion cascades when projects overlap and signage conflicts.

scenarios.name: Officer Directs Ego Into Oncoming Lane
scenarios.description: A police detail directs ego past a stalled truck via the oncoming lane, but an oncoming driver watching the officer drifts partially into that lane before correcting.
scenarios.mechanism: The wave-through creates legitimate wrong-lane occupancy while the oncoming driver's attention capture shrinks the borrowed corridor mid-passage, demanding lateral precision.
environment: urban two-lane street with police detail
scenarios.successSignature: Ego follows the direction at <= 25 km/h keeping >= 0.8 m from truck and sedan, aborting to the shoulder below 0.5 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Human-directed wrong-lane passage is legal but fragile; ego must track actors the officer cannot watch.

scenarios.name: Curb Build-Out Squeezes Cyclist Into Swerve
scenarios.description: A temporary curb extension of water-filled barriers pinches the right lane; a cyclist is pushed into the travel lane at the pinch and the car ahead swerves left around him into ego's lane at 45 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: The pinch removes the shoulder line, displacing the cyclist into traffic; the lead's swerve transmits the pinch into ego's path with barriers blocking any right escape.
environment: urban street with temporary curb extension
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pre-slows to <= 30 km/h at the pinch, letting the lead return with >= 1 m clearance and >= 1.5 m passing distance to the cyclist.
scenarios.trainingValue: Links geometry pinch through VRU displacement to multi-vehicle prediction.

scenarios.name: Unlit Night Flagger Discovery
scenarios.description: A rural night work zone's flagger paddle has lost its retroreflective facing; drivers see nothing until headlights sweep the worker at close range and the lead brakes very late.
scenarios.mechanism: Non-reflective paddle plus darkness removes the advance cue, shifting the lead's braking into ego's stopping distance; ego must infer the control point from cone lines and the lead's decel.
environment: rural two-lane work zone at night
scenarios.successSignature: Detect the control point by >= 150 m and stop >= 5 m before the flagger with decel <= 4 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Night-degraded human control points demand cue fusion beyond sign detection.

scenarios.name: highway-brake-check
scenarios.description: Aggressive driver whom ego just passed pulls within 3m at 100km/h and stomps the brakes twice.
scenarios.mechanism: Retaliation braking after a pass violates priors that lead vehicles maintain flow; prediction sees constant velocity while decel exceeds -8 m/s².
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥1.2s following time-to-collision and applies ≤ -6 m/s² controlled decel without lane departure.
scenarios.trainingValue: Covers hostile lead-vehicle decel spikes that break constant-velocity motion models.

scenarios.name: rolling-roadblock-boxin
scenarios.description: Two cooperating sedans pace side-by-side at 60km/h in both lanes ahead, then the left one drifts toward the median barrier squeezing ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Deliberate lateral compression closes the escape envelope faster than lane-change planners re-plan.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego executes a safe fall-back: ≥0.8m clearance maintained or complete stop ≥40m short without barrier contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests joint multi-actor adversarial prediction rarely seen in natural data.

scenarios.name: merge-brakecheck-chain
scenarios.description: On an on-ramp, a driver merges then brake-checks the follower; the follower swerves into ego's adjacent lane at 80km/h with <0.5s gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Brake-check cascades a swerve one lane over, spawning an unsignaled lateral threat ego must predict from the lead's brake lights.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects swerve onset within 200ms and keeps TTC ≥1.5s via speed dip of 5–10km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Second-order behavioral chains where one violation induces another.

scenarios.name: wrongway-ramp-headon
scenarios.description: An intoxicated driver enters a diamond off-ramp against flow and drives 300m up the ramp at 70km/h toward ego exiting at 90km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Head-on closure at 160km/h in a lane whose prior says all traffic moves away; heading classifier confidence collapses.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego initiates avoidance by TTC≤2.0s, achieving lateral offset ≥2m or full stop before 10m gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Highest-severity relative-velocity case; tests rejection of impossible-heading hypotheses.

scenarios.name: wrongway-one-way-downtown
scenarios.description: A tourist sedan drives toward ego against a one-way street at 25km/h hugging the wrong curb, forcing ego to thread between it and parked cars.
scenarios.mechanism: Counterflow in a mapped one-way breaks route-graph directionality priors while leaving <3m total corridor width.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego slows to ≤10km/h and passes with ≥0.5m clearance on each side, no contact.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-speed counterflow negotiation with tight lateral budget.

scenarios.name: wrongway-divided-shoulder
scenarios.description: Driver misses a divided-highway crossover and continues the wrong way along the outer shoulder at 60km/h, then cuts diagonally back across both lanes toward a distant turnaround.
scenarios.mechanism: Diagonal crossing path intersects ego's lane with a shallow ~20° angle, giving long ambiguous TTC from a region priors treat as empty.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego flags threat by 4s TTC, adjusts ±1 lane or decelerates to keep ≥3s gap through crossing point.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shallow-angle crossing geometry defeats simple closing-speed estimates.

scenarios.name: impaired-sinusoid-weave
scenarios.description: Drunk driver oscillates sinusoidally across a lane every 2–3s with 1.5m amplitude at 100km/h, occasionally clipping the adjacent lane where ego travels.
scenarios.mechanism: Periodic lateral excursions defeat constant-lane models; each trough penetrates ego's lane boundary unpredictably in phase.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego predicts next intrusion ≥1.5s ahead and holds ≥1m lateral buffer or drops back ≥2s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Oscillatory motion outside normal steering spectra; tests temporal extrapolation.

scenarios.name: impaired-random-fullstops
scenarios.description: Impaired driver at 3am performs random full stops in an active lane for 3–10s between 40–70km/h bursts, ego approaching from behind at 60km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Unsignaled stochastic decel-to-zero in a travel lane violates free-flow priors; stop timing unpredictable so ego cannot rely on lead intent cues.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥2.5s headway throughout, worst-case required decel ≤ -4 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Stochastic stop-go dynamics stress longitudinal planners under low visibility.

scenarios.name: impaired-frozen-at-green
scenarios.description: Vehicle sits motionless at a green light for 20s, then launches abruptly and stalls again 15m past the crosswalk as ego arrives on cross street.
scenarios.mechanism: Frozen-then-launch pattern makes occupancy of the box nonstationary; ego's crossing window appears open then closes mid-maneuver.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts or clears crossing keeping ≥1s margin to the launched vehicle's path.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dynamic occupancy reversal inside the conflict zone.

scenarios.name: freeze-unprotected-left
scenarios.description: Driver commits to an unprotected left, then freezes straddling the centerline in ego's oncoming lane as the light changes.
scenarios.mechanism: Half-committed turn leaves ego's lane blocked by a vehicle facing ego; priors expect either completion or retreat, not immobility.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥8m short or threads with ≥0.8m offset; no false assumption of turn completion.
scenarios.trainingValue: Intent inference failure on partially executed maneuvers.

scenarios.name: hypercautious-parked-shadows
scenarios.description: Over-cautious driver brakes to 15km/h below the 50km/h limit for every parked car and tree shadow, unpredictably, on a busy collector where ego follows at limit.
scenarios.mechanism: Sub-norm braking triggered by non-threat stimuli gives ego no predictive cue; decel events arrive at random intervals at -3 to -4 m/s².
scenarios.successSignature: Zero unsafe headway violations (<1s); mean speed loss ≤8km/h via early lane change.
scenarios.trainingValue: Random low-amplitude decel sources teach robustness to cue-less slowdowns.

scenarios.name: zero-gap-merger
scenarios.description: Hyper-cautious driver comes to a complete stop at every merge and turn even with 6s gaps, launching only when ego has committed to pass on the shoulder-side lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Stop-launch timing anti-correlates with ego's pass decision, converting a predicted-safe overtake into a sudden lateral conflict.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego aborts pass or completes with ≥1s TTC at all times.
scenarios.trainingValue: Interaction-coupled timing where the other agent reacts to ego's own plan.

scenarios.name: systematic-stop-runner
scenarios.description: Commuter rolls through a residential stop-sign corridor at 40km/h without any deceleration, hitting five consecutive stops while ego emerges from a stop-controlled side street.
scenarios.mechanism: Zero compliance with stop control removes the expected yield signature, so ego's gap acceptance model based on decelerating approach fails.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays entry ≥1.5s or clears with ≥2s TTC against non-yielding cross traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Systematic rule-violator distribution shift vs. compliant training data.

scenarios.name: blind-corner-stop-runner
scenarios.description: At a blind T with parked trucks limiting sight to 25m, a pickup crosses the major road at full speed through its stop sign directly across ego's path.
scenarios.mechanism: Crossing trajectory materializes inside the visible horizon (<1.5s) with no approach deceleration signature to trigger early detection.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego enters only after verifying gap; if violated, achieves ≥0.5m lateral miss or stops within available distance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Occluded high-speed violators with minimal pre-contact evidence.

scenarios.name: street-race-takeover-weave
scenarios.description: Two tuned cars begin a street race beside ego at 110km/h in a 65 zone, weaving through gaps ≤1.2 car-lengths on both sides of ego simultaneously.
scenarios.mechanism: Dual high-speed weavers compress ego's lateral options from both sides with closure speeds 45km/h above flow priors.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds lane with ≥0.8m min clearance and avoids reactive overcorrection; max lateral jerk bounded.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-agent extreme-speed threading around a fixed ego anchor.

scenarios.name: racer-shoulder-pass
scenarios.description: Racer uses the right shoulder at 130km/h to pass a congested platoon, then cuts back into ego's 1.5s gap at differential 60km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Shoulder region priors treat as non-travel; cut-in lands with TTC<1s from an unexpected origin with no signal.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects shoulder entrant by 2s TTC and opens gap to ≥1.8s within 3s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Out-of-distribution entry origin plus violent gap capture.

scenarios.name: sideshow-donut-intersection
scenarios.description: At 1am a sedan performs donuts circling the center of a large intersection at 40km/h while ego approaches on green.
scenarios.mechanism: Rotating obstacle sweeps across every approach with tangential speed 40km/h and unpredictable radius growth into ego's path.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego refuses entry (full stop ≥10m before box) until rotation radius stays clear ≥2s continuously.
scenarios.trainingValue: Circular motion class absent from standard trajectory priors.

scenarios.name: sideshow-crowd-blockade
scenarios.description: Sideshow spectators form a semi-circle 5m inside the crosswalk filming two spinning cars; a spectator steps backward into ego's lane without looking.
scenarios.mechanism: Crowd boundary is dynamic and encroaching; individual retro-step occurs with zero approach kinematics to detect.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥8m from crowd line and creeps only with ≥2m pedestrian clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Human-wall interaction with emergent single-actor breaches.

scenarios.name: freeway-reverse-missed-exit
scenarios.description: Driver realizes missed exit, stops in ego's 100km/h lane, and reverses 80m along the lane toward ego with hazards on.
scenarios.mechanism: Negative longitudinal velocity in a high-speed lane inverts closure logic; brake lights (stopped/reversing) give misleading intent signal.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects negative lead velocity within 1s and changes lanes with ≥1.5s margin or stops ≥30m short.
scenarios.trainingValue: Velocity-sign violation in motion prediction.

scenarios.name: reverse-down-arterial
scenarios.description: After overshooting a turn, driver backs up 40m against 45km/h arterial traffic in the curb lane, then swings forward across ego's lane to correct.
scenarios.mechanism: Reverse motion followed by immediate forward cut combines two opposing anomalies into one continuous unpredictable path intersecting ego's lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego tracks reverse phase, keeps ≥2s effective gap, and anticipates forward swing with ≥0.8m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound reverse-then-forward maneuver sequences.

scenarios.name: inner-lane-uturn-cross3
scenarios.description: Driver in the inner through lane (not turn lane) signals late and initiates a U-turn sweeping across three lanes of 55km/h traffic including ego's.
scenarios.mechanism: U-turn initiation from a through-lane position invalidates lane-based intent inference; swept path crosses ego lane at shallow angle with low closing rate masking urgency.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects lateral path deviation ≥2s before lane-line crossing; yields or passes behind with ≥1s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Origin-lane/maneuver mismatch breaking map-conditioned intent priors.

scenarios.name: arterial-multipoint-turn
scenarios.description: Driver attempts a three-point turn mid-block on a 2-lane arterial at rush hour, pausing broadside in ego's lane while opposing traffic flows.
scenarios.mechanism: Broadside stationary phase presents maximum frontal area perpendicular to flow with zero legal precedence; duration unknown so gap acceptance is ill-defined.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops before the sweep envelope, resumes only after vehicle aligns parallel; min standoff 5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Mid-block multi-phase maneuvers with indefinite hold times.

scenarios.name: trailer-sway-fishtail
scenarios.description: A pickup towing a lightly loaded box trailer hits 95km/h; trailer yaw oscillates growing to ±1.5m, swinging the trailer body across the lane line into ego's adjacent lane repeatedly.
scenarios.mechanism: Trailer articulation angle diverges from tow-vehicle heading, so predicting from the truck alone underestimates swept envelope crossing into ego's lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego models combined vehicle+trailer envelope, holding ≥0.8m from max trailer excursion or dropping back ≥3s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Articulated-body envelope prediction beyond rigid-vehicle assumptions.

scenarios.name: trailer-sway-jackknife
scenarios.description: Trailer sway escalates until the combo jackknifes at 30° and slides to a stop straddling both lanes 150m ahead of ego at highway speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Progressive instability gives 2–3s of visible precursor (growing yaw amplitude) that ego must read to pre-position before the blockage forms.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reads precursor by 3s before jackknife, selects open lane and completes change before blockage; min clearance 1m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Instability forecasting from oscillation growth signatures.

scenarios.name: hillstart-rollback-learner
scenarios.description: Stalled learner on a steep 12% uphill roll back 3m toward ego stopped close behind at a light, restarts, stalls again and rolls twice more.
scenarios.mechanism: Repeated negative creep on grade contradicts stopped-at-light priors; rollback magnitude grows each cycle eroding safety margin monotonically.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains ≥4m initial stack gap, tracking rollback and preserving ≥1.5m minimum through all stalls.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grade-dependent reverse micro-motion in queues.

scenarios.name: learner-stall-loop
scenarios.description: Learner stalls mid-intersection during a left turn, restarts, proceeds 2m, stalls again — occupying the box through two full signal cycles while ego waits on the conflicting approach.
scenarios.mechanism: Intermittent motion makes the conflict zone occupied indefinitely; ego's crossing-window estimator receives alternating feasible/infeasible states.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego refrains from committing until target vehicle exits box entirely; no entry during any stall pause.
scenarios.trainingValue: Indefinite-duration occupancy with intermittent progress.

scenarios.name: medical-drift-across-lanes
scenarios.description: Driver suffering a medical event drifts right at 2°/s at 90km/h, crosses ego's lane diagonally, clips the barrier and rebounds back across both lanes ahead of ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Slow constant-curvature drift lacks the jerk signature of deliberate lane changes, delaying classification until barrier rebound reverses direction unpredictably.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego classifies drift by 3s TTC, decelerates ≥5km/h per second, and clears rebound path with ≥1.5s margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gradual incapacitation trajectories versus discrete maneuver taxonomy.

scenarios.name: slumped-driver-dead-lane
scenarios.description: Unconscious driver's car coasts to rest at walking pace in the middle lane at night with no lights or hazards, discovered by ego at 100km/h behind a tall SUV occluding until 120m.
scenarios.mechanism: Dark stationary object in travel lane appears with occlusion-delayed exposure, leaving ~2.5s to full stop from detection.
scenarios.successSignature: Detection to response ≤300ms; achieved decel ≤ -7 m/s²; stop or lane-change completed with ≥0.5m clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Unlit stationary hazards with occlusion-compressed reaction budget.

scenarios.name: phone-drift-blindspot-side
scenarios.description: Texting driver in the lane beside ego drifts left at highway speed, closing the lateral gap to 0.4m alongside ego's rear door over 4 seconds.
scenarios.mechanism: Slow monotonic lateral approach with no blinker defeats lane-keeping priors; threat develops parallel rather than converging, evading TTC salience.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego monitors lateral gap, nudges away ≥0.3m and alerts; min sustained gap restored ≥1.2m within 2s of 1.0m threshold.
scenarios.trainingValue: Parallel-drift threat class where longitudinal TTC is undefined.

scenarios.name: rumble-overcorrect-swerve
scenarios.description: Distracted driver drops two wheels onto the shoulder rumble strip at 110km/h, then yanks a 4m/s² overcorrection cutting across ego's lane front bumper-to-bumper.
scenarios.mechanism: Rumble-drop is the observable precursor; overcorrection converts a self-correcting event into a violent unsignaled cut-in within 1s.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego predicts overcorrection from rumble onset, lifts throttle achieving ≥2s TTC through the swerve arc.
scenarios.trainingValue: Precursor-triggered counterfactual prediction (drift→panic correction).

scenarios.name: hitandrun-debris-field
scenarios.description: After a two-car collision ahead, one car flees; the other spins to rest leaking fluid while bumper fragments scatter across ego's lane over 40m, unmarked, traffic swerving unpredictably.
scenarios.mechanism: Fleeing vehicle generates erratic secondary conflicts while scattered small debris forces distributed swerving by others, making neighbor trajectories unstable around ego.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego navigates debris at reduced speed with zero tire strikes and ≥0.8m clearance to all swervers.
scenarios.trainingValue: Post-crash chaos with compound static+dynamic hazards.

scenarios.name: fleeing-driver-cutthrough
scenarios.description: Driver who just sideswiped a parked car flees at speed, cutting through a 12-car queue via a 1.5m gap between ego and a bus, mirror-fold close.
scenarios.mechanism: Escape-driven gap selection accepts clearances half of learned norms, with approach speed 30km/h above queue flow.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds lane and speed steady; fleeing car passes with ≥0.3m clearance without ego evasive steer.
scenarios.trainingValue: Panic-speed gap threading adjacent to ego skin.

scenarios.name: ghost-signal-forever
scenarios.description: Driver cruises with right blinker on for 3km through multiple intersections, never turning; ego must decide whether to overtake in the 'freed' left lane or treat signal as noise.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal evidence decoupled from behavior corrupts the primary intent channel; overtaking decisions conditioned on indicators become unreliable exactly when passing opportunities matter.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego weights observed trajectory over indicator within 10s, completing pass with standard clearances and zero incorrect gap commitments.
scenarios.trainingValue: Conflicting intent-evidence fusion under stale signals.

scenarios.name: unsignaled-sudden-turn
scenarios.description: Driver travels 400m with clean indicators, then without signal brakes 40% and darts into a gas station cut crossing ego's near lane at 15km/h differential.
scenarios.mechanism: Absence of expected signal before maneuver strips the anticipation window; combined brake-plus-cut masks which action is primary.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego responds to kinematics alone, achieving ≥1.5s TTC or clean stop ≥5m from cut throat.
scenarios.trainingValue: Indicator-absent maneuver detection from motion onset only.

scenarios.name: contradictory-signal-parkleft
scenarios.description: Driver flashes left signal for 8s approaching a left-turn pocket, then abruptly swerves right into a parallel-parking spot on the opposite curb, cutting across ego's path.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal asserts intent opposite to executed path; trust-the-indicator policies commit ego to accelerate into the vacated space at the exact moment of the right cut.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego defers commitment until wheel angle confirms direction; aborts acceleration with ≥1s margin to cut path.
scenarios.trainingValue: Deliberate or accidental signal-path contradiction stress-tests intent fusion polarity.

scenarios.name: fastlane-crawler-20mph
scenarios.description: Driver camps in the passing lane at 30km/h on a 100km/h freeway, tapping brakes whenever anyone approaches within 30m, trapping ego behind with dense adjacent-lane traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Speed differential of 70km/h plus punitive brake taps eliminates both overtake-from-behind and safe gap windows, forcing multi-lame negotiation under harassment.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego escapes via right lanes with zero <1s headway events and no reaction to brake taps beyond safe decel.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sustained blockade plus provocation requiring patience-preserving policy.

scenarios.name: shoulder-running-congestor
scenarios.description: During a jam, driver uses the right shoulder at 60km/h past stopped traffic, then forces back in directly ahead of ego's creeping car with <0.5m clearance demand.
scenarios.mechanism: Non-travel surface used as express lane produces closure at 55km/h relative to a queue priors model as static.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects shoulder entrant ≥3s ahead, sets firm gap; admits only at ≥1.5s headway else blocks legally.
scenarios.trainingValue: Queue-relative high-speed intruders from excluded regions.

scenarios.name: roundabout-counterflow
scenarios.description: Tourist enters a two-lane roundabout counterclockwise, meeting ego head-on at the yield line while a third car orbits normally between them.
scenarios.mechanism: Directional inversion inside circular geometry yields head-on closure masked until exit geometry resolves; normal orbiting car constrains ego's dodge options.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego halts before the yield line permanently once counterflow confirmed; standoff ≥8m maintained.
scenarios.trainingValue: Direction-of-travel violation in loop topology.

scenarios.name: railroad-track-freeze
scenarios.description: Driver stops with vehicle straddling active rail crossing gates down, panics, lurches forward and back repeatedly as ego approaches on the roadway behind and a train horn sounds.
scenarios.mechanism: Alternating lurch/stop on the crossing creates an unpredictable obstruction precisely where ego's own escape is gated by barriers.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥15m from nearest rail and does not proceed until track is clear for ≥5s continuous.
scenarios.trainingValue: Life-critical static hazard compounded by erratic occupant motion.

scenarios.name: median-crossover-uturn
scenarios.description: Driver uses an emergency median crossover to U-turn across a divided highway, swinging wide into ego's high-speed lane while a following SUV copies the same maneuver 3s later.
scenarios.mechanism: Two consecutive crossovers convert one crossing conflict into repeated ones; ego clearing the first swing meets the second at similar geometry with shifted timing.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego handles both swings with ≥2s TTC each, no acceleration into either conflict envelope.
scenarios.trainingValue: Repeated-conflict cadence and imitation behavior chaining.

scenarios.name: red-light-chase-platoon-breaker
scenarios.description: Road-rage pursuer runs a fresh red at 80km/h chasing a car that ran it 2s earlier, crossing ego's green-light path at the far side of a wide intersection.
scenarios.mechanism: First violator draws attention right; second violator arrives on nearly identical trajectory 2s later exploiting ego's post-first-threat recovery.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego remains stopped through both incursions, resuming ≥3s after last violator clears.
scenarios.trainingValue: Clustered violations exploiting recovery-period vulnerability.

scenarios.name: dark-unlit-vehicle
scenarios.description: Car with no headlights or taillights cruises at 50km/h at midnight, effectively invisible until ego's beams catch it 60m out in ego's own lane after a curve.
scenarios.mechanism: Reflectance-only detection at 60m at 90km/h closing leaves ~2s; absence of taillight prior removes the standard far-range cue entirely.
scenarios.successSignature: Detection at ≥55m; ego slows to allow ≥2s TTC and passes or follows at compliant headway.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sensor-physics edge: photometric-only hazard acquisition.

scenarios.name: ramp-reverse-up-exit
scenarios.description: Driver takes exit ramp, realizes error at the bottom, and reverses up the entire 200m curving ramp in darkness against ego descending at 70km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Sustained reverse motion through a curvature-limited sightline means each crest reveals only 40–70m of the reversing vehicle; closing geometry compounds per segment.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops upon first negative-velocity detection, standoff ≥20m held until ramp clears.
