scenarios.trainingValue: Persistent reverse motion with progressive sightline disclosure.

scenarios.name: draglaunch-yellow-crossclear
scenarios.description: Two cars stage at a red; on green they launch at full throttle, but cross-traffic from the previous phase is still clearing — one racer threads the clearing box while the other locks brakes sideways into ego's approach lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Launch acceleration 8× traffic norms combined with panic ABS stop mid-box creates a spinning lateral obstacle entering ego's right-of-way at the phase transition.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds at stop line through the entire incursion, entering only ≥4s after racers' paths clear.
scenarios.trainingValue: Launch-dynamics outliers colliding with phase-transition timing.

scenarios.name: wheelie-through-box
scenarios.description: Motorcyclist pops a sustained wheelie crossing a signalized intersection at 100km/h in a 50 zone, headlight pitching skyward and degrading ego's detection of the shrinking visible profile.
scenarios.mechanism: Pitched-up posture reduces radar cross-section and displaces the headlight cue upward; ego's tracker loses association mid-crossing.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego maintains track through posture change and never accelerates while motorcycle occupies box; min clearance 1.5m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Pose-dependent signature degradation of vulnerable road users.

scenarios.name: flat-tow-sagging-rope
scenarios.description: Disabled sedan towed by SUV on a stretchy rope sags to the pavement mid-street; rope snaps taut when the SUV brakes, whipping the towed car forward into ego's following gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Two vehicles behave as loosely coupled mass with slack/taut transitions producing impulsive relative velocity invisible to single-object trackers.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats pair as coupled unit with variable length; maintains ≥3s gap to the rear element through both slack and taut phases.
scenarios.trainingValue: Flexible-coupling dynamics violating rigid multi-body priors.

scenarios.name: phantom-yield-chain-reaction
scenarios.description: Driver in a traffic circle stops abruptly to yield to a pedestrian 20m from the curb who shows no crossing intent; three followers brake-react in sequence, the last swerving into ego's adjacent lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Courtesy yield to a non-threat seeds a braking wave whose terminal swerve lands in ego's lane 4s after the initiating stimulus, beyond naive causal tracing.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates propagation, reducing speed 20% before the wave arrives and keeping ≥1.5s TTC to the terminal swerver.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-hop causal chains where the threatening act is third-generation downstream.

scenarios.name: cab-dispute-panic-brakes
scenarios.description: Occupants argue loudly (visible gesticulation); driver alternately slams brakes (-6 m/s²) then accelerates (+3 m/s²) in ego's lane for 500m with no external cause.
scenarios.mechanism: Endogenous conflict drives decel profile uncorrelated with any road feature; ego's scene-based expectation module finds no predictor and must fall back to pure reactive control at high excitation amplitude.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego sustains ≥3s headway across all pulses, executes early lane change within 5s of pattern recognition.
scenarios.trainingValue: Scene-unexplainable longitudinal oscillation forcing reactive-mode control.

scenarios.name: sidewalk-shortcut-cheater
scenarios.description: Driver facing a 300m queued left skips the queue, mounts the sidewalk, and drives 80m past pedestrians and a bus shelter to cut into the turn at its throat, forcing ego (lawfully waiting) to brake as the cheater merges at 25km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Off-roadway travel region then re-entry at the merge point ego considers secured; re-entry angle steep and speed double the queue's.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields re-entry with ≥1.2s TTC while flagging; zero pedestrian-proximity compromise (≥2m to any pedestrian).
scenarios.trainingValue: Off-network traversal with unlawful re-entry competing for ego's secured slot.

scenarios.name: residential-follow-slow-local-traffic
scenarios.description: Ego follows a sedan driving 25 km/h on a 40 km/h residential street for several blocks.
scenarios.mechanism: Lead vehicle's low speed causes ego to regulate headway instead of overtaking on the narrow street.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway 1.5-2.5 s, longitudinal accel within ±1.5 m/s², no lane-edge encroachment.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline car-following under speed mismatch without overtaking pressure.

scenarios.name: single-side-parked-residential-lateral-position
scenarios.description: Parked cars line one side; ego shifts laterally within lane while an oncoming car passes.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced lane width from parked cars forces lateral offset timed against oncoming traffic.
scenarios.successSignature: ≥0.8 m clearance to parked cars, ≥1.0 m to oncoming, lateral rate ≤0.5 m/s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline lateral positioning in reduced-width cross-sections.

scenarios.name: all-way-stop-orderly-rotation
scenarios.description: Four-way stop with three vehicles proceeding strictly by arrival order.
scenarios.mechanism: Arrival-order right-of-way makes ego hold then depart when first in sequence.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop at bar, departs only when first, ≥1 s gap after prior vehicle clears.
scenarios.trainingValue: Normative all-way-stop rotation without hesitation or aggression confounds.

scenarios.name: uncontrolled-residential-intersection-crossing
scenarios.description: Ego crosses an uncontrolled T-intersection with a distant crosser requiring no yield.
scenarios.mechanism: Distant crosser's presence triggers scan-and-proceed rather than yield-and-wait.
scenarios.successSignature: Approach ≤30 km/h, proceeds with ≥5 s time-gap, no hard braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Calibrated gap acceptance at the most common intersection type.

scenarios.name: speed-hump-comfort-crossing
scenarios.description: Ego traverses two speed humps paced behind a minivan.
scenarios.mechanism: Vertical road profile forces planned decel before each hump and re-accel after, paced off the lead.
scenarios.successSignature: ≤20 km/h over humps, accel within -2 to +1 m/s², headway ≥1.5 s kept.
scenarios.trainingValue: Comfort-bounded vertical-profile handling and preview speed planning.

scenarios.name: sidewalk-pedestrian-no-conflict-pass
scenarios.description: A pedestrian walks a dog on the parallel sidewalk for a block with no crossing.
scenarios.mechanism: Sustained parallel pedestrian presence demands monitoring without any maneuver.
scenarios.successSignature: No speed perturbation |Δv|<0.3 m/s, continuous pedestrian tracking, path unchanged.
scenarios.trainingValue: Calibrates monitor-without-overreaction to prevent phantom braking.

scenarios.name: residential-night-low-speed-drive
scenarios.description: Night drive through dim residential streets at posted 35 km/h with oncoming traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced visual range caps safe speed; oncoming headlights add glare adaptation load.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed ≤limit with ≥2 s headway, lane center ±0.25 m, correct low-beam behavior.
scenarios.trainingValue: Night-domain nominal anchor for perception-limited speed selection.

scenarios.name: cul-de-sac-negotiation
scenarios.description: Ego turns around a cul-de-sac bulb with one reverse move past a parked SUV.
scenarios.mechanism: Dead-end bulb geometry forces a multi-point turn clearing a parked vehicle and curb radius.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn within pavement (≤0.3 m curb margin), reverse ≤10 km/h, correct-lane exit within 60 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Low-speed multi-point maneuvering baseline on public road infrastructure.

scenarios.name: trash-collection-day-narrow-pass
scenarios.description: Ego flows past trash bins and a stopped collection truck on collection morning.
scenarios.mechanism: Bins narrow the corridor so ego pre-selects an offset; the stopped truck makes the pass slow-but-flowing.
scenarios.successSignature: ≥1.0 m clearance or full stop with ≥1.5 m buffer, resumes within 5 s of clear path.
scenarios.trainingValue: Routine obstruction-offset behavior distinguishing narrowing from blockage.

scenarios.name: light-snow-residential-cautious-cruise
scenarios.description: Light snow dusts a residential street; traffic moves 10-15 km/h below the limit.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced surface friction lowers the comfortable speed band and lengthens stopping distance.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed within traffic flow, headway ≥3 s, decel ≤1.5 m/s², no wheel-slip-inducing inputs.
scenarios.trainingValue: Winter nominal anchor for friction-aware speed and spacing.

scenarios.name: signalized-red-stop-and-go
scenarios.description: Ego stops at a red light behind two queued cars, then accelerates on green.
scenarios.mechanism: Signal state and standing queue cause staged deceleration, stop, and launch.
scenarios.successSignature: Comfortable decel ≤2 m/s², stop fully behind stop bar/queue (≥2 m gap), launches ≤2 s after green.
scenarios.trainingValue: Core signalized-intersection stop-and-go cycle for everyday distribution.

scenarios.name: protected-left-green-arrow
scenarios.description: Ego executes a protected left on a green arrow with opposing traffic stopped.
scenarios.mechanism: Green-arrow phase creates an exclusive window whose duration bounds turn completion speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Enters on green arrow, completes within phase, accel ≤2 m/s², stays in correct receiving lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline protected-phase turn geometry and phase-timing compliance.

scenarios.name: permitted-left-adequate-gap
scenarios.description: Ego makes a permitted left across two oncoming lanes using a clearly adequate 6 s gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Oncoming flow forces ego to judge a gap and commit within its window.
scenarios.successSignature: Enters with ≥5 s time-gap to nearest oncomer, completes without forcing oncoming decel >0.5 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Ground-truth gap acceptance for the highest-risk routine maneuver.

scenarios.name: right-turn-on-red-complete-stop
scenarios.description: Ego turns right on red after a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Red signal plus cross flow requires full stop, scan, and entry through an adequate gap.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop ≥2 s before turning, yields to all crosswalk users, enters with ≥4 s gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline RTOR compliance including pedestrian priority.

scenarios.name: yellow-light-lawful-stop
scenarios.description: Ego stops comfortably for a yellow light at a distance where stopping is clearly feasible.
scenarios.mechanism: Yellow onset at moderate distance triggers the stop-vs-go decision resolved as a smooth stop.
scenarios.successSignature: Decel 1.5-2.5 m/s², stops fully behind bar, no creep into crosswalk.
scenarios.trainingValue: Calibrates yellow-phase decision boundary under clearly-feasible conditions.

scenarios.name: walk-signal-pedestrian-yield
scenarios.description: Ego yields at a signalized crosswalk to pedestrians crossing on the walk signal, then proceeds on green.
scenarios.mechanism: Active walk phase legally blocks the turn path, making pedestrian clearance the gating condition for ego's turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Stops before crosswalk, proceeds only after full clearance, no encroachment during walk phase.
scenarios.trainingValue: Normative signalized VRU yielding for turn-on-green interactions.

scenarios.name: midblock-raised-crosswalk-yield
scenarios.description: Ego slows for a pedestrian at a midblock raised crosswalk with flashing beacon.
scenarios.mechanism: Beacon and raised table legally require yielding; the pedestrian's entry into the crosswalk gates ego's speed profile.
scenarios.successSignature: Yields with ≥2 m stop margin before crosswalk, crosses table ≤25 km/h, resumes smoothly.
scenarios.trainingValue: Midblock yielding baseline distinct from signalized crossings.

scenarios.name: signaled-lane-change-arterial
scenarios.description: Ego signals and changes lanes on a 50 km/h arterial into a clearly adequate gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Upstream turn restriction (lane becomes left-only) causes a planned, signaled lane change.
actors: rear car in target lane 80 m back
scenarios.successSignature: Signal ≥3 s before move, gap ≥2.5 s time-headway at completion, lateral rate ≤1 m/s, no brake from affected driver.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline discretionary lane change with full signaling compliance.

scenarios.name: queue-stop-behind-standing-queue
scenarios.description: Ego approaches a 150 m standing queue at a red light and decelerates smoothly into the last gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Standing queue length and closing speed dictate a single planned deceleration profile to the end of queue.
scenarios.successSignature: Single smooth decel ≤2 m/s², final gap ≥2 m to stopped lead, no late hard braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Approach-and-join-queue baseline, the most frequent urban decel event.

scenarios.name: left-turn-pocket-dwell-then-complete
scenarios.description: Ego enters a left-turn pocket, waits one signal cycle for oncoming traffic, then completes on the permitted phase.
scenarios.mechanism: Oncoming flow density forces dwell in the pocket until a gap or phase change permits completion.
scenarios.successSignature: Fully within pocket while waiting, no blocking of through lane, completes with ≥5 s gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Turn-pocket dwell-and-complete behavior under realistic oncoming demand.

scenarios.name: transit-bus-curbside-lawful-pass
scenarios.description: Ego slows behind a bus stopped at a curb-side stop, then passes it using the adjacent lane when clear.
scenarios.mechanism: The stopped bus blocks the lane, causing a legal lane-change pass once the adjacent gap is adequate.
scenarios.successSignature: Stops ≥3 m behind bus, signals and changes with ≥2.5 s gap, no re-entry closer than 1 s to passed vehicle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Routine bus-stop negotiation common on urban corridors.

scenarios.name: bike-lane-pass-with-clearance
scenarios.description: Ego passes a cyclist riding in a marked bike lane at 22 km/h, changing lanes where required by the 1 m rule.
scenarios.mechanism: Cyclist's sustained presence in the bike lane triggers the legal passing-clearance maneuver at reduced speed.
scenarios.successSignature: ≥1.0 m lateral clearance (or full lane change), pass speed differential ≤15 km/h, signal used if lane change.
scenarios.trainingValue: Ground-truth lawful cyclist passing, a top VRU interaction class.

scenarios.name: right-turn-yield-distant-cyclist
scenarios.description: Ego turns right across a bike lane on green, timing the turn before an approaching cyclist arrives.
scenarios.mechanism: Cyclist's approach on straight-ahead green requires ego to yield until the gap allows a clean turn.
scenarios.successSignature: Yields until cyclist gap ≥4 s, no crossing of cyclist path, completes turn without cyclist braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline right-hook avoidance geometry with compliant behavior.

scenarios.name: single-lane-roundabout-entry-exit
scenarios.description: Ego yields to a circulating vehicle, enters a single-lane roundabout, and exits at the second leg.
scenarios.mechanism: Yield-at-entry rule plus circulating vehicle timing gate ego's entry and exit path.
scenarios.successSignature: Stops/yields at entry line when occupied, enters with ≥3 s gap, circulates 20-30 km/h, correct-lane exit.
scenarios.trainingValue: Normative yield-at-entry roundabout behavior for the growing roundabout fleet.

scenarios.name: two-way-stop-yield-and-cross
scenarios.description: Ego at a two-way stop yields to cross traffic, then crosses or turns when a clear gap arrives.
scenarios.mechanism: Cross street has right-of-way, so ego must wait out cross flow and select an adequate gap.
scenarios.successSignature: Full stop, waits for ≥6 s gap, crosses without inducing cross-traffic decel.
scenarios.trainingValue: Gap acceptance at two-way stops where ego is the minor approach.

scenarios.name: channelized-right-slip-lane-merge
scenarios.description: Ego turns right via a channelized slip lane and merges into arterial traffic through an adequate gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Slip-lane geometry delivers ego at low speed to a yield point where arterial flow gates the merge.
actors: arterial car 70 m back at 55 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Yields at merge point, accelerates to ≥90% of traffic speed within 100 m of merge, gap ≥3 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Slip-lane acceleration-merge baseline distinct from highway ramps.

scenarios.name: dual-left-turn-lane-discipline
scenarios.description: Ego turns left from the outer of two dual left-turn lanes, tracking its lane through the turn.
scenarios.mechanism: Parallel dual-turn geometry requires path discipline so ego's arc does not encroach on the inner turning vehicle.
actors: car turning from inner left lane
scenarios.successSignature: Stays within own turn path (≥0.5 m separation from inner vehicle), completes into correct dual receiving lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-lane turn path-keeping, a common geometry error source.

scenarios.name: designated-u-turn-execution
scenarios.description: Ego performs a legal U-turn at a designated median opening after yielding to oncoming traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Median opening geometry and oncoming flow require a yielded, single-sweep U-turn path.
scenarios.successSignature: Waits for ≥6 s gap, completes in one sweep within median width, no reverse needed.
scenarios.trainingValue: Legal U-turn baseline for divided-highway navigation.

scenarios.name: rail-crossing-routine-transit
scenarios.description: Ego crosses an active light-rail crossing with gates up and no train present, following a car across.
scenarios.mechanism: Track presence imposes the legal check-and-cross routine; the absent train means gates stay up and flow continues.
scenarios.successSignature: Never stops on tracks, crosses with ≥1.5 s headway to lead car, no unnecessary stop before tracks.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline grade-crossing compliance without the emergency variant.

scenarios.name: arterial-commute-following-overcast
scenarios.description: Ego cruises in flowing 45 km/h commute traffic on an overcast morning arterial.
scenarios.mechanism: Platoon flow speed oscillations cause continuous headway regulation via mild accel/decel.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway 1.5-2.5 s, accel ≤1.2 m/s², speed tracks platoon within ±3 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dense-distribution anchor: ordinary commute car-following under flat light.

scenarios.name: night-arterial-headlight-following
scenarios.description: Ego follows traffic on a lit arterial at night with oncoming headlights in adjacent lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Night glare and reduced contrast raise detection latency, requiring slightly wider headway at the same speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway ≥2 s at 45-50 km/h, stable lane keeping ±0.3 m, no glare-induced speed dips >5 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Night nominal following behavior with realistic glare sources.

scenarios.name: light-rain-arterial-extended-following
scenarios.description: Ego follows traffic in light rain on an arterial, using extended gaps and smooth inputs.
scenarios.mechanism: Wet pavement lengthens stopping distance so the correct nominal response is wider headway and gentler decels.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway ≥2.5-3 s, decel ≤1.5 m/s², wiper-appropriate speed, no hydroplaning-inducing speeds.
scenarios.trainingValue: Wet-weather nominal anchor distinguishing routine adaptation from emergency handling.

scenarios.name: highway-cruise-following-distance
scenarios.description: Ego cruises at 100 km/h in a highway lane holding steady headway behind a truck.
scenarios.mechanism: Lead vehicle's steady speed and occasional 5 km/h drifts cause continuous small headway corrections.
scenarios.successSignature: Time-headway 1.8-2.5 s, accel within ±1 m/s², lane center ±0.2 m over 5 km.
scenarios.trainingValue: The single most common driving state; anchors highway cruise distribution.

scenarios.name: on-ramp-acceleration-merge-gap
scenarios.description: Ego accelerates up a 300 m on-ramp and merges into a 90 km/h lane through an adequate gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Ramp geometry and target-lane speed force acceleration to match flow and time the gap at the gore.
scenarios.successSignature: Reaches ≥95% of lane speed by merge point, enters gap ≥2.5 s to leader and follower, signal ≥3 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Baseline ramp merge with adequate gaps — prerequisite before hostile-merge edge cases.

scenarios.name: highway-signaled-lane-change
scenarios.description: Ego changes from lane 2 to lane 3 at 100 km/h with a clean 4 s gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Slower vehicle ahead in lane 2 motivates a planned overtaking lane change into an ample gap.
scenarios.successSignature: Signal ≥3 s, gap ≥3 s at completion, lateral rate ≤1.2 m/s, no response from lane-3 driver.
scenarios.trainingValue: High-speed discretionary lane-change baseline.

scenarios.name: highway-overtake-slower-vehicle
scenarios.description: Ego overtakes a slower truck in the passing lane and returns right after clearing it.
scenarios.mechanism: Speed differential creates the overtake; clearance past the truck gates the safe return maneuver.
scenarios.successSignature: Passes with ≥1 m lateral clearance, returns only when truck visible in mirror with ≥2.5 s headway.
scenarios.trainingValue: Complete pass cycle (overtake plus return) at nominal differentials.

scenarios.name: being-overtaken-maintain-lane
scenarios.description: Ego holds lane and speed while two vehicles overtake it on the left at varying differentials.
scenarios.mechanism: Adjacent-lane overtaking vehicles create transient lateral and aerodynamic proximity demands with no ego action required.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed variation ≤2 km/h, lane center ±0.25 m, no defensive swerve or brake response.
scenarios.trainingValue: Stability-under-pass anchor to prevent reactive overcorrection to adjacent traffic.

scenarios.name: exit-ramp-deceleration-curve
scenarios.description: Ego exits a highway via a 250 m deceleration lane and a right-hand curve at posted ramp speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Exit geometry imposes a two-stage decel: lane speed on the taper, then ramp curve speed.
scenarios.successSignature: Decel ≤2.5 m/s² on taper, curve speed within ±5 km/h of posted, stays in ramp lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exit maneuver baseline covering speed-transition and curve following.

scenarios.name: highway-night-following
scenarios.description: Ego follows traffic at 95 km/h at night on a highway with only headlight illumination of lead vehicles.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced lead-vehicle contrast at night demands wider headway for equal braking margin.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway ≥2.5 s at 95 km/h, correct low-beam use, lane center ±0.3 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Night highway cruise anchor for perception-degraded following.

scenarios.name: hov-access-zone-entry
scenarios.description: Ego enters an HOV lane through a designated dashed buffer access zone at highway speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Only the dashed buffer segment legally permits crossing, so the access-zone location gates the maneuver timing.
scenarios.successSignature: Crosses buffer only within dashed zone, signal ≥3 s, gap ≥3 s to HOV-lane traffic.
scenarios.trainingValue: Legal-restriction-gated maneuver baseline (managed-lane compliance).

scenarios.name: following-heavy-truck-buffer
scenarios.description: Ego follows a box truck at 90 km/h on a highway with an extended following gap.
scenarios.mechanism: The truck's blocked forward sightline and large blind zones justify a visibly longer headway than car-following.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway ≥3 s (≈80+ m at 90 km/h), position visible in truck mirrors, no dwell in blind spots.
scenarios.trainingValue: Vehicle-class-dependent following policy baseline.

scenarios.name: light-snow-highway-lane-keeping
scenarios.description: Ego cruises at 80 km/h in light snowfall on a highway with trace snow on lane edges.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced friction and partially obscured edge lines require lower speed, wider gaps, and steadier steering.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed ≤80 km/h, headway ≥3 s, lane center ±0.35 m despite obscured edges, decel ≤1.5 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Winter highway nominal anchor for lane-keeping under degraded markings.

scenarios.name: toll-plaza-lane-selection-and-payment
scenarios.description: Ego selects an open electronic-toll lane at a toll plaza, decelerates through, and accelerates out.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane closure pattern and toll-barrier geometry force lane selection and a controlled slow pass through the gantry.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane choice 50+ m ahead, decel ≤2 m/s² to ≤30 km/h at gantry, ≥0.5 m lateral clearance to adjacent-lane cars.
scenarios.trainingValue: Structured low-speed infrastructure navigation with lane-choice decisions.

scenarios.name: work-zone-open-lane-through-pass
scenarios.description: Ego drives through an active work zone with cones narrowing the shoulder but the travel lane fully open.
scenarios.mechanism: Cone taper narrows the cross-section, requiring a steady lateral offset and reduced posted speed without any obstruction.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed ≤posted work-zone limit, ≥1 m clearance to cones, steady lane position without drift toward workers.
scenarios.trainingValue: Routine work-zone traversal baseline (open lane) before closure/flagger variants.

scenarios.name: rural-speed-transition-deceleration
scenarios.description: Ego decelerates from 90 km/h rural road to 50 km/h town limit across a transition zone.
scenarios.mechanism: Posted-limit change and denser roadside development define a legal speed ramp ego must track.
scenarios.successSignature: Reaches 50 km/h within 100 m past the sign, decel ≤2 m/s², no overshoot above limit.
scenarios.trainingValue: Speed-regulation baseline for limit transitions, common on rural commutes.

scenarios.name: parallel-parking-public-street
scenarios.description: Ego parallel parks into a 7 m gap between parked cars on a public street using one reverse maneuver.
scenarios.mechanism: Gap length relative to ego footprint forces the standard reverse-arc path with mirror-checked clearances.
scenarios.successSignature: Parks within 0.3 m of curb, ≤2 maneuvers, ≥0.6 m clearance to both neighbors, within 90 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Canonical low-speed precision maneuver on public roads.

scenarios.name: departing-parallel-parking-into-gap
scenarios.description: Ego reverses out of a parallel parking spot into the travel lane through an adequate gap.
scenarios.mechanism: Parked geometry requires reverse-arc exit whose timing is gated by travel-lane gaps.
scenarios.successSignature: Reverse ≤8 km/h, enters travel lane with ≥4 s gap, no contact risk to neighbors, signal before merge.
scenarios.trainingValue: Parking-departure baseline complementing parking entry.

scenarios.name: curbside-pickup-stop-reenter
scenarios.description: Ego stops at an empty curbside pickup zone with hazard lights, dwells 30 s, then re-enters traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Pickup-zone purpose causes a legal curb stop whose re-entry is gated by passing traffic gaps.
scenarios.successSignature: Stops fully within zone (≤0.3 m from curb), hazards on within 2 s, re-enters with ≥3 s gap.
scenarios.trainingValue: Planned curb-stop-and-reenter cycle for ride-hail/delivery operations.

scenarios.name: perpendicular-parking-public-lot
scenarios.description: Ego reverse-parks into a perpendicular space in a public surface lot with light pedestrian traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: Bay geometry and adjacent parked cars define the reverse-arc path; roaming pedestrians require creep-speed vigilance.
scenarios.successSignature: Reverse ≤8 km/h, centered in bay ±0.25 m, stops for any pedestrian within one bay width, completes ≤60 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Lot navigation and reverse bay parking baseline (special-site infrastructure).

scenarios.name: yield-emergency-vehicle-pull-right
scenarios.description: Ego pulls right and stops when an ambulance with siren approaches from behind on an arterial.
scenarios.mechanism: Siren and lights legally compel pull-right-and-stop, a routine lawful response to a clear emergency path.
scenarios.successSignature: Signals and pulls right within 5 s, full stop with right lane edge clearance, resumes ≥3 s after ambulance passes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Nominal emergency-vehicle yielding baseline before occluded/siren-ambiguous variants.

scenarios.name: Dense Flowing Highway 15 Percent Gaps
scenarios.description: Sustained cruising in free-flowing but dense freeway traffic where every inter-vehicle gap sits near the 15th-percentile margin for the speed.
scenarios.mechanism: High density caps achievable headway, so any lane change by a neighbor instantly converts ego's legal gap into an under-minimum one, forcing continuous micro speed adjustments rather than a single braking event.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway never below 0.9 s sustained >1 s; jerk under 2 m/s^3; zero hard decel above 3 m/s^2 over 10 km.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches margin management under density pressure without any fault by other agents.

scenarios.name: Highway Weave Segment Through Traffic
scenarios.description: Traversing a 2 km weave where entering ramp traffic crosses the ego lane toward an exit.
scenarios.mechanism: Merging vehicles consume adjacent-gap space at a fixed rate, so ego must meter its own longitudinal position to keep a usable buffer on both flanks simultaneously.
scenarios.successSignature: Minimum lateral gap to merging vehicle >1.5 m; speed variance under 8 km/h; zero abort maneuvers.
scenarios.trainingValue: Exercises simultaneous lead and flank gap control in fully cooperative flow.

scenarios.name: Dense Platoon With Cut-In Absorption
scenarios.description: Following within a moving platoon at 90 km/h where neighboring lanes run slightly faster, inviting frequent courtesy cut-ins ahead of ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Faster adjacent lane makes ego's gap the most attractive insertion point; each absorbed cut-in halves available headway and requires smooth re-opening of the margin while holding platoon pace.
scenarios.successSignature: Post-cut-in headway restored to target within 4 s; decel never above 2.5 m/s^2; zero unsafe lateral closure.
scenarios.trainingValue: Repeated benign cut-in absorption builds comfort-profile calibration.

scenarios.name: Heavy Truck Shadowing at Safe Distance
scenarios.description: Cruising behind a tractor-trailer convoy at 80 km/h where the trucks occlude all forward visibility beyond two vehicle lengths.
scenarios.mechanism: Occlusion removes lead-of-lead information, so ego must infer flow changes from brake-light latency and truck sway, demanding tighter baseline headway discipline plus readiness margin.
scenarios.successSignature: Headway held 2.2-2.7 s continuously; lateral offset biased 0.3 m in-lane away from truck for sensor clearance; zero late reactions to truck brake events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Perception-denied car-following with purely kinematic cues.

scenarios.name: Slow Truck Overtake Chain on Climbing Lane
scenarios.description: Passing a queue of slow trucks using a short climbing lane while opposing heavy traffic flows past.
scenarios.mechanism: The climbing lane ends at a fixed point, creating a closing-rate budget: ego may pass only when opposing gap plus remaining lane length jointly suffice, requiring continuous recomputation.
scenarios.successSignature: Overtake completed with >3 s time-to-opposing-vehicle at merge-back; no forced oncoming braking; lane-change initiated only when pass feasibility margin >20 percent.
scenarios.trainingValue: Two-sided gap arithmetic under a hard geometric deadline.

scenarios.name: Metered Ramp Cycle Entry Timing
scenarios.description: Joining dense-but-flowing freeway traffic through a ramp meter running 4-s cycles at moderate density.
scenarios.mechanism: The meter delivers fixed-size green windows whose usable value depends on mainline gap arrival phase; ego must stage acceleration so it launches within its window and lands in a real gap rather than forcing one.
scenarios.successSignature: Launch inside own green window 100 percent; merge with mainline gap >3 s TTC; queue restart delay <1 s per cycle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Phased launch timing fused with mainline gap prediction.

scenarios.name: Toll Plaza Lane Selection Under Flow
scenarios.description: Approaching an open-road toll plaza where lanes split into exact-change, transponder-only, and cash variants with different queue speeds.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane choice made 300 m out commits ego to that queue's discharge rate; misjudging relative queue speeds forces late swerves, so ego must continuously re-rank lanes while closing at 100 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Final lane committed >150 m before gore; zero gate-area lateral maneuvers; selected queue clears within 20 percent of best available.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-queue stochastic ranking at highway closure rates.

scenarios.name: Arterial Turn Bay Threaded Deceleration
scenarios.description: Negotiating a 6-lane arterial where dedicated left-turn bays begin abruptly every 400 m with queued waiting vehicles.
scenarios.mechanism: Queued turn-bay vehicles back into the adjacent through lane, so ego must detect bay taper early and pre-select lane position before the queue spillback reaches its travel path.
environment: urban arterial with alternating turn bays
scenarios.successSignature: Zero late lane changes inside taper; min longitudinal gap to spilled queue >2 m; lateral shift completed >40 m before obstruction.
scenarios.trainingValue: Anticipatory positioning against predictable recurring encroachment.

scenarios.name: Continuous Block Lane Function Discipline
scenarios.description: Dense arterial grid where every block changes permitted lane usage (left-only, left-through, right-only) signed per approach.
scenarios.mechanism: Lane-function changes make the previously correct lane illegal at the next signal, so ego must re-plan lane assignment every 200 m from overhead signage while maintaining flow.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct functional lane occupied >150 m before each intersection; zero last-moment lane changes under 30 m from stop bar.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sustained signage reading fused with lane planning at block frequency.

scenarios.name: Dual Left Turn Pair Tracking
scenarios.description: Consecutive intersections with dual left-turn lanes where the pair funnels back into three receiving lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Turn-pair geometry compresses two exit streams into three entry lanes with ambiguous assignment, so ego must hold a tight arc terminating in an unambiguous lane center without crossing the interior line.
scenarios.successSignature: Never crossing pair divider line; exit heading error <2 degrees; min lateral gap to twin-turn vehicle >1.2 m throughout arc.
scenarios.trainingValue: Precise low-speed arc control amid symmetric ambiguity.

scenarios.name: Right Turn Bay Shared With Queue Spillback
scenarios.description: Reaching a right-turn pocket whose storage is full because the cross-street is congested, with through queue occupying the adjacent lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Pocket saturation means the turn can be entered only from a narrow slot between stopped through vehicles, requiring creep-out negotiation with drivers who must momentarily shift.
scenarios.successSignature: Entry executed with zero closure below 1 m; through-queue speed disturbance <3 km/h; turn completed on first accepted gap >4 s TTC.
scenarios.trainingValue: Slot-entry negotiation in saturated but orderly conditions.

scenarios.name: Bus Pullout Reentry Yield Timing
scenarios.description: Corridor where buses repeatedly leave and re-enter curb pullouts, each reentry claiming the lane ego occupies.
scenarios.mechanism: Each bus signaling reentry creates a mandatory yield point; ego must modulate speed so the bus merges without stopping, sustaining a rolling yield cadence over many blocks.
scenarios.successSignature: Every bus merge accepted with ego headway >2 s after merge; bus never fully stops during reentry; ego delay vs free-flow <15 percent.
scenarios.trainingValue: Courteous rolling-yield rhythm repeated to stability.

scenarios.name: Truck Blind Spot Linger Avoidance
scenarios.description: Pacing a multi-lane segment beside several trucks whose side zones overlap ego's lane position choices.
scenarios.mechanism: Any steady-state speed matching a truck places ego in its blind spot indefinitely; ego must deliberately phase-shift speed to traverse blind-spot windows quickly and never dwell.
actors: 4 trucks in adjacent lanes at similar cruise speed
scenarios.successSignature: Time co-located in any truck blind-spot window <5 s per encounter; zero dwelling matches; lateral clearance >1.5 m during passes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Blind-spot exposure budgeting as a routine skill.

scenarios.name: Concrete Barrier Canyon Following
scenarios.description: Following traffic in a narrowed roadway with concrete barriers on both sides and no shoulder, behind a loaded flatbed.
scenarios.mechanism: Barrier confinement eliminates recovery space, raising required precision of headway and in-lane centering since any drift risks scraping geometry rather than grass.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral position within +/-0.25 m of lane center 95 percent of time; headway >1.8 s; zero barrier-proximity alarms.
scenarios.trainingValue: Centering precision elevated by unforgiving static boundaries.

scenarios.name: Long Downgrade Convoy Brake Patience
scenarios.description: Descending a 6 percent grade for 4 km behind loaded trucks governed to 60 km/h with passing prohibited.
scenarios.mechanism: Grade makes stopping distance grow while convoy speed stays low, so ego must manage extended following distance growth and brake-free speed holding without any overtaking option.
scenarios.successSignature: Zero service-brake applications beyond pace adjustments; headway grown >=3 s versus flat baseline; engine-speed management smooth throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grade-aware patience and thermal-margin discipline without events.

scenarios.name: Winding Rural Road Speed Adaptation
scenarios.description: Sustained driving on a forest two-lane with consecutive curves posted 70-90 km/h below tangent speeds.
scenarios.mechanism: Each crest or curve hides exit geometry until mid-corner, so appropriate speed is set by sight-line distance, and ego must continuously recompute corner speed from visible width and curvature.
scenarios.successSignature: Corner entry speed within 10 percent of curvature-derived comfortable limit; lateral acceleration <3 m/s^2; zero lane-line crossings.
scenarios.trainingValue: Continuous curvature-speed mapping without any hazard event.

scenarios.name: Crest-Limited Sight Distance Corridor
scenarios.description: Rural road series where every third crest truncates sight distance to under 120 m at 80 km/h legal speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Short sight lines cap usable speed below the posted limit on crests only, so ego must modulate crest-by-crest based on measured visibility rather than holding constant cruise.
actors: occasional farm equipment emerging from field drives
scenarios.successSignature: Speed matched to sight distance on every crest (stopping-distance <= sight distance); smooth profile, zero abrupt releases.
scenarios.trainingValue: Per-sightline speed governance distinct from blanket limits.

scenarios.name: Rural Curve Camber Shift Sequence
scenarios.description: Alternating cambered curves where adverse crown reverses lateral support direction between bends.
scenarios.mechanism: Adverse camber adds effective lateral demand beyond geometry alone, so identical-radius corners need different entry speeds depending on crown direction, punishing memorized pacing.
scenarios.successSignature: Entry speed differs correctly >=8 km/h between equal-radius opposite-camber curves; max lateral accel 2.8 m/s^2; tracking error <0.3 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Surface-geometry sensitivity layered onto curvature control.

scenarios.name: Farm Vehicle Encounter Pacing
scenarios.description: Meeting a wide combine harvester half in the lane on a narrow rural road with soft shoulders.
scenarios.mechanism: Combine width forces ego nearly onto the shoulder edge; safe passage depends on precise lateral placement computed from measured widths at combined closing speed 115 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral gap to combine >0.8 m; zero wheel-off onto soft shoulder; speed reduced to <=40 km/h before meeting point.
scenarios.trainingValue: Width-arithmetic passing at speed on unforgiving edges.

scenarios.name: Rural Curve Cyclist String Meeting
scenarios.description: Descending winding rural road meets an uphill string of five club cyclists legally occupying the shoulder line.
scenarios.mechanism: Curve geometry plus cyclist spacing forces ego to time its pass between curve apex and each rider, adjusting laterally within a narrow corridor at 70 km/h while oncoming traffic may appear mid-pass.
scenarios.successSignature: Passing clearance >1.5 m to every rider; pass completed before apex or aborted cleanly before commitment point; zero oncoming conflicts.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sequential VRU clearance arithmetic inside curve timing.

scenarios.name: Downtown Pedestrian Wall Compliance
scenarios.description: Midday CBD street where crosswalks discharge continuous pedestrian streams overlapping ego's green phases legally.
scenarios.mechanism: Pedestrian density keeps conflict points occupied at every corner; ego must proceed through shared phases only at walking-compatible speeds, converting signal timing into a continuous speed schedule.
scenarios.successSignature: Zero conflict-point entries with pedestrian TTC <3 s; average speed >=60 percent of limit; all yields completed before encroaching crosswalk.
scenarios.trainingValue: Throughput-versus-compliance balance under saturating VRU presence.

scenarios.name: Crosswalk Surge Anticipation
scenarios.description: Approaching a mid-block signalized crossing where pedestrian platoons form predictably from a transit stop upstream.
scenarios.mechanism: Transit alighting creates a deterministic wave reaching the crossing about 40 s after each bus, so optimal behavior is anticipatory deceleration timed to the platoon rather than reactive stopping.
scenarios.successSignature: Deceleration begins before platoon enters crosswalk; stop avoided entirely >=50 percent via timing; zero late braking above 3.5 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Schedule-based prediction replacing event reaction.

scenarios.name: Shared Street Mixed Pace Negotiation
scenarios.description: Low-speed shared-space street where pedestrians, cyclists, and cars intermingle with no lane markings at 20 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Absence of priority markings makes progress a continuous mutual-spacing negotiation; ego must hold a crawl that lets others resolve ordering around it without asserting right-of-way aggressively.
scenarios.successSignature: Maintained clearance >1.5 m to all VRUs; progress maintained >=12 km/h average; zero freeze events over 300 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Fluid mixed-order negotiation without rules to lean on.

scenarios.name: Sidewalk Cafe Doorstep Clearance
scenarios.description: Curbside restaurant block where diners step between parked cars toward the sidewalk edge unpredictably but lawfully.
scenarios.mechanism: Door openings and seated diners shrink usable lateral corridor intermittently, so ego must pre-shrink lateral buffer near seating clusters and restore it after, block-long.
scenarios.successSignature: Lateral offset adjusted >=1 m before each occupied parking spot; no closure under 1 m to any person; steady speed profile.
scenarios.trainingValue: Micro-geography driven buffer modulation at block scale.

scenarios.name: Event Crowd Egress Stream
scenarios.description: Stadium-dispersal period where police-controlled pedestrian rivers cross arterials in synchronized surges every cycle.
scenarios.mechanism: Surge periodicity presents alternating open and flooded crossings; correct play is cycle-timed progression through green windows at crowd-compatible acceleration.
scenarios.successSignature: Each green window used with start-loss under 2 s; zero encroachments during surge; total corridor delay within 1.5x optimal.
scenarios.trainingValue: Periodic crowd-flow exploitation under full compliance.

scenarios.name: Transit Mall Mixed Compliance Corridor
scenarios.description: Driving a transit mall where buses have priority lanes, taxis load at marked bays, and general traffic crawls lawfully at 20 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Priority-lane boundaries shift effective capacity dynamically as buses glide past; ego must hold its restricted lane while yielding at every marked bus-priority merge point without stalling.
scenarios.successSignature: Zero priority-lane dwell >5 s at any merge point; min bus passing gap 1.5 m; corridor transit within 120 percent of walk-par time budget.
scenarios.trainingValue: Priority hierarchy maintenance at crawl speeds amid dense company.

scenarios.name: School Zone Active Hours Crawl Discipline
scenarios.description: School-street segment during arrival bell window with crossing guard cycles and lawful 30 km/h limit.
scenarios.mechanism: Guard-held gaps open on irregular human timing, so ego must track the guard's paddle cadence and launch precisely on release without overshooting the zone's strict speed envelope.
scenarios.successSignature: Zone speed never exceeds 32 km/h; launch within 1.5 s of guard release; full stop at every guard signal.
scenarios.trainingValue: Human-paced launch timing inside rigid statutory speed bounds.

scenarios.name: Dismissal Pickup Line Slalom
scenarios.description: School dismissal period where parents double-park in a lawful staggered pickup line, leaving a single weaving channel.
scenarios.mechanism: Each parked-and-waiting car pinches the lane at irregular intervals, so ego must weave a continuous S-path through alternating gaps at walking-adjacent speed while children move between cars under supervision.
scenarios.successSignature: Channel maintained without stops >10 s; min gap to any person 1.5 m; zero cone contacts; speed <=20 km/h throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sustained slalom precision around supervised but mobile children.

scenarios.name: School Bus Caravan Loading Rhythm
scenarios.description: Street with staggered school buses at successive stops, each lawfully loading with flashers while passing legality varies by median.
scenarios.mechanism: Successive bus flasher patterns force a stop-go-go-stop rhythm; ego must reset expectation at each bus since passing legality differs by median configuration, testing per-vehicle rule-state tracking.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct stop/go decision per bus per median rule; zero motion violations; smooth restarts keeping headway to boarding children.
scenarios.trainingValue: Per-vehicle legal-state switching repeated under time pressure.

scenarios.name: Playground-Edge Slow Corridor
scenarios.description: Park-edge street where recess activity sends balls and supervised groups to the fence line, none entering the road.
scenarios.mechanism: Controlled-but-present children create persistent latent risk demanding lower operational speed than legality alone, exercising conservative selection absent any triggering event.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed held <=25 km/h past active frontage; lateral position biased away from fence 0.5 m; zero unnecessary stops.
scenarios.trainingValue: Risk-appropriate conservatism calibrated above minimum legality.

scenarios.name: Roundabout String Continuous Yield-Go
scenarios.description: Chaining five roundabouts on an avenue where each circulating stream arrives just dense enough to require brief yield-then-go.
scenarios.mechanism: Gap acceptance repeats every 150 m; each decision couples exit-side acceleration with next-entry deceleration, so hesitation compounds into corridor-level throughput loss.
scenarios.successSignature: Average entry delay <3 s per ring; zero stop-within-ring; accepted gaps all >4.5 s; pedestrian yields at every splitter.
scenarios.trainingValue: Repetition-hardened gap acceptance with carryover momentum.

scenarios.name: Turbo Roundabout Spiral Exit Threading
scenarios.description: Large turbo-style roundabout requiring pre-selection among spiral lanes that terminate into exits.
scenarios.mechanism: Spiral markings funnel vehicles laterally whether ready or not, so ego must commit to lane choice before entry and track the forced drift while holding separation from parallel circulants.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct spiral occupied from entry; lateral separation >1 m during forced drift; exit taken without counter-steer corrections.
scenarios.trainingValue: Geometry-forced lateral commitment under continuous company.

scenarios.name: Mini-Roundabout Truck Sweep Allowance
scenarios.description: Historic-district mini-roundabouts where delivery trucks sweep over the central dome across ego's entry path.
scenarios.mechanism: Truck off-tracking claims circulating space dynamically, so ego must withhold entry when a large vehicle approaches even though a nominal gap exists, judging by vehicle class not just distance.
scenarios.successSignature: No entry initiated when truck sweep intersects path; false-hold rate <20 percent; average entry delay <5 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Class-conditioned gap judgment beyond kinematics alone.

scenarios.name: Roundabout Pedestrian Splitter Cadence
scenarios.description: Roundabout entries where splitter-island refuges are occupied most cycles by waiting pedestrians ego must yield to twice per ring.
scenarios.mechanism: Double-yield points sandwich the circulation, so ego's speed profile must fit a moving window between four successive yield obligations per roundabout transit.
scenarios.successSignature: All four yields honored with full stops only when occupied; ring transit under 12 s; zero second-go delays from poor exit timing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound yield scheduling inside one small geometry.

scenarios.name: Roundabout U-Turn Continuity
scenarios.description: Using roundabouts for successive U-turns where the movement spans all exits and crosses every circulating lane.
scenarios.mechanism: U-turn paths traverse the full ring, so ego must merge across multiple circulating streams sequentially while preserving enough ring speed to reach the fourth exit without stopping mid-ring.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane transitions all with gaps >4 s; ring speed never below 15 km/h; correct exit reached without hesitation stops.
scenarios.trainingValue: Full-ring multi-stream sequencing as routine navigation.

scenarios.name: Green Wave Speed Locking
scenarios.description: A 12-intersection arterial timed for 50 km/h progression where ego starts one cycle late relative to the band.
scenarios.mechanism: Offset timing rewards exact band speed; starting out of phase means catching the wave requires holding precisely the design speed for 3 km, since any surplus hits cascading reds.
scenarios.successSignature: >=9 of 12 signals met at green; instantaneous speed within +/-2 km/h of band; zero catch-up bursts above 2 m/s^2.
scenarios.trainingValue: Long-horizon adherence to an invisible timing structure.

scenarios.name: Green Wave Recovery After One Miss
scenarios.description: Coordinated corridor where one unplanned pause (curbside delivery) drops ego out of the progression band.
scenarios.mechanism: Missing one green shifts ego against offsets such that brute acceleration guarantees further misses; recovery demands computing feasible catch-up rate and accepting partial-band reentry.
scenarios.successSignature: Reentry to progression within 3 intersections; approach speeds never above limit +5 km/h; total added delay <45 s.
scenarios.trainingValue: Strategic loss recovery versus greedy sprinting.

scenarios.name: Half-Cycle Pedestrian Phase Squeeze
scenarios.description: Coordinated avenue where mid-corridor pedestrian-only phases shorten effective green bands to narrow windows.
scenarios.mechanism: Exclusive ped phases steal cycle time asymmetrically, making the attainable green band barely wider than one platoon; ego must sit within the platoon's speed envelope exactly.
environment: 90 s cycles with 15 s ped-only phases
scenarios.successSignature: Platoon-relative position stable (never isolated); band entry success >=80 percent; zero band-chasing speed violations.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tight-window progression riding a platoon rather than the signal.

scenarios.name: Queue Spillover Metered Approach
scenarios.description: Corridor driving where downstream queues periodically spill back past upstream intersections, converting greens into storage-limited admissions.
scenarios.mechanism: Green lights become meaningless when exit storage is full; ego must meter approach speed to arrive exactly as discharge frees space instead of joining a frozen box junction.
environment: grid corridor with known spillover intersections
scenarios.successSignature: Never entering intersection without exit-path clearance; arrival timed to discharge within 5 s; zero blocked-box events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Storage-aware signal response decoupled from light color.

scenarios.name: Adaptive Signal Pace Discovery
scenarios.description: Corridor with adaptive signals whose timings respond to detected demand, so no fixed offset exists to learn.
scenarios.mechanism: Adaptive control makes each intersection's state depend on ego's own contribution to queues; ego must infer the controller's implied pacing from observed phase patterns and settle into the emerging rhythm.
scenarios.successSignature: Stops reduced >=40 percent versus naive cruise over 10 intersections; inferred pace stable after 3 intersections; no aggressive catch-up events.
scenarios.trainingValue: Online rhythm inference for non-stationary controllers.

scenarios.name: Curbside Bus Lane Leapfrog Courtesy
scenarios.description: Right-lane shared bus/bike corridor where ego may use the curb lane between buses but must shed it before each arrival.
scenarios.mechanism: Bus schedule creates recurring lane-claim events; ego must leapfrog between general lanes and curb lane on a timetable inferred from observed bus spacing, yielding each claim smoothly.
scenarios.successSignature: Curb lane vacated >100 m before each bus; cyclist buffer >1.5 m always; zero bus impeds.
scenarios.trainingValue: Timetable-driven lane citizenship on shared right-of-way.

scenarios.name: Floating Bus Stop Bike Weave Cadence
scenarios.description: Protected bike lane weaving behind floating bus stops, crossing ego's right-turn path at each stop.
scenarios.mechanism: Each bus stop forces bikes into mixed traffic briefly, injecting cyclists directly into ego's deceleration path exactly where ego also turns; a continuous scan-and-yield rhythm is required.
environment: arterial with floating island stops every 600 m
scenarios.successSignature: Yield-before-turn at every stop location; min bike gap 2 s; zero cyclist speed reductions caused by ego.
scenarios.trainingValue: Recurring geometric VRU injection handled as routine rhythm.

scenarios.name: Shared Right Lane Turn Across Peloton
scenarios.description: Narrow right lane shared by buses, bikes, and right-turners where ego threads turns across the bike stream at 30 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: Turning across a continuous bike stream requires selecting micro-gaps in the peloton; wrong choice stalls the lane, so gap selection quality directly sets corridor throughput.
scenarios.successSignature: Turn executed in first acceptable bike gap >3 s; no peloton braking induced; queue position advanced each cycle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Fine-grained stream-crossing gap picking under audience.

scenarios.name: Night Rain Reduced Sensation Cruise
scenarios.description: Freeway cruise in steady night rain where lane lines are wet-reflected and contrast halved yet fully adequate at proper speed.
scenarios.mechanism: Reduced retroreflectivity lengthens perception latency, so ego must convert sensing uncertainty into modest speed reduction and widened headway rather than confidence-equivalent behavior.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed scaled <=85 percent of dry baseline; headway >=2.5 s; zero dropout-induced jerks; steering smoothness maintained.
scenarios.trainingValue: Graceful sensing degradation compensation as everyday skill.

scenarios.name: Night Rain Urban Signal Glare Binding
scenarios.description: Downtown night drive in rain where signal heads double in glare and puddles mirror conflicting light sources.
scenarios.mechanism: Mirrored phantom signals from puddle reflections compete with real heads, so ego must bind signal state to physical head position rather than brightest appearance while wet pavement extends stopping distance.
scenarios.successSignature: Correct real-head binding at every signal; decel reserve >=30 percent maintained; zero phantom-signal responses.
scenarios.trainingValue: Source-binding perception under optical multiplicity.

scenarios.name: Wet Night Unlit Rural Persistence
scenarios.description: Unlit rural road at night in drizzle where centerline retroreflection is the sole guidance for 8 km.
scenarios.mechanism: With guidance reduced to sparse reflectors, ego must hold lane via intermittent evidence, interpolating between confirmations at reduced speed without overcorrecting on noise.
scenarios.successSignature: Lane tracking error <0.4 m RMS; speed <=70 km/h matched to confirmation spacing; zero reflector-post proximity under 1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Sparse-evidence guidance endurance at honest speeds.

scenarios.name: Night Rain Truck Spray Overtake Window
scenarios.description: Night-rain two-lane overtaking where truck spray blinds the passing zone until committed and oncoming headlights arrive in wet shimmer.
scenarios.mechanism: Spray curtain hides the oncoming lane during approach, so overtake decisions must be made from pre-spray headlight geometry with extra margin banked for degraded mid-pass vision.
scenarios.successSignature: Overtakes only with oncoming headway >12 s equivalent; pass duration minimized via clean exit line; zero mid-pass hesitations.
scenarios.trainingValue: Margin-rich decision-making when verification is impossible.

scenarios.name: Work Zone Reduced Speed Full Compliance
scenarios.description: 2 km work zone with posted 55 km/h limit (down from 90), lane shift, and workers present behind barriers, no incursions.
scenarios.mechanism: The posted reduction exists because barrier offset shrinks lateral tolerance; ego must sustain exactly the reduced speed and centered tracking for the whole zone despite empty-looking lanes tempting acceleration.
scenarios.successSignature: Speed <=57 km/h for 100 percent of zone; chicane tracking error <0.3 m; zero worker-side buffer excursions.
scenarios.trainingValue: Statutory speed discipline against perceptual temptation.

scenarios.name: Work Zone Night Chicane Shift
scenarios.description: Night-time work zone chicane where temporary reflector lines define an S-shift lit only by portable towers.
scenarios.mechanism: Temporary geometry replaces permanent lanes, so ego must trust and follow short reflector runs through the shift while traffic drums maintain 55 km/h flow with no shoulder refuge.
scenarios.successSignature: Shift negotiated with tracking error <0.35 m; speed held 53-58 km/h; zero brake-light cascade contributions.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporary-geometry obedience under minimal visual assurance.

scenarios.name: Moving Maintenance Convoy Shadowing
scenarios.description: Following a paint-striping convoy operating at 30 km/h on a live freeway where passing is prohibited by work zone rules.
scenarios.mechanism: Convoy speed far below design speed combined with a no-passing rule forces extended patience; ego must manage platooning including gap breathing and brake-free speed holding for the operation's length.
scenarios.successSignature: Gap oscillation <±3 m; zero attempted passes; speed changes only at the convoy's own pace changes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Extended sub-limit patience with rule-locked options.

scenarios.name: blind-crest-stalled-car
scenarios.description: Rural two-lane crest with limited sight distance conceals a stalled sedan parked half in the travel lane just past the summit.
scenarios.mechanism: The vertical curve's sag point hides the obstruction until ~60 m, leaving under 3 s at 90 km/h to perceive, decide, and check the opposing lane for a legal pass.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego decelerates to ≤30 km/h before sightline opens; required decel stays under 4 m/s² with no lane violation unless the opposing lane is verifiably clear ≥150 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Tests perception latency and go/no-go overtaking logic at crest-limited sight distance, a classic run-off-road and head-on generator.

scenarios.name: blind-crest-overtake-straddle
scenarios.description: An impatient driver overtakes a slow tractor beginning on the far side of a blind crest, entering ego's lane head-on.
scenarios.mechanism: Crest curvature hides both the slow leader and the passer until the passer is committed to the maneuver, compressing ego's decision window to roughly 2 s at combined closing speed 180 km/h.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects the straddling vehicle, slows, and steers right within available shoulder achieving TTC ≥2.5 s at closest approach.
scenarios.trainingValue: Head-on avoidance on crests demands early micro-cues (dust, shadow, roofline); training this beats reacting at visibility onset.

scenarios.name: crest-hides-sharp-horizontal-curve
scenarios.description: Immediately after a blind crest the road breaks sharply left behind a rock cut, with the curve's chevron signs positioned below the sightline break.
scenarios.mechanism: The vertical and horizontal curves overlap so the deflection is invisible until the crest is committed at 80 km/h; advisory 35 km/h geometry demands ~5 m/s² lateral capability that straight-line speed cannot supply.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reduces speed below 45 km/h before the deflection point, holding lateral acceleration ≤3.5 m/s² through the bend.
scenarios.trainingValue: Speed selection must anticipate hidden geometry from cues, not just visible signs — a persistent AV weakness on unfamiliar alignments.

scenarios.name: hairpin-mirror-tour-bus
scenarios.description: Mountain hairpin with a convex mirror on the apex; a tour bus takes the wide outside line through the bend.
scenarios.mechanism: The rock-cut wall eliminates direct sight lines, making the mirror the only information source; the bus's swept path occupies most of ego's exit lane, converting a routine bend into a mutual-yield negotiation.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reads the mirror image, stops fully clear of the apex before the bus's front crosses the conflict point, with ≥0.5 m clearance when it passes.
scenarios.trainingValue: Forces an AV to interpret distorted convex-mirror evidence and yield in a no-rule environment where geometry alone sets right-of-way.

scenarios.name: switchback-climbing-cyclist-hidden
scenarios.description: Descending a switchback, a cyclist climbing on the inside of the bend emerges from behind the rock cut directly into ego's exit path.
scenarios.mechanism: The cut slope blocks sight of the inside line while ego's braking and steering are already saturated by the 9% downhill grade, so the cyclist appears inside the physically minimum stopping distance.
scenarios.successSignature: Entry speed pre-managed so that remaining decel demand when the cyclist is revealed stays ≤6 m/s² with lateral miss distance ≥1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Corner-speed entry must be set by worst-case occluded-line assumptions; punishes AVs that trust post-corner perception.

scenarios.name: consecutive-switchback-queue-stop
scenarios.description: On stacked switchbacks, the convex mirror shows a queue of three cars, and the middle car halts mid-bend around a blind corner above ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Mirror geometry cannot reveal which queue element is stationary; the stopped car becomes visible only as ego rounds the lower bend, inside its stopping envelope on the adverse grade.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds at the previous bend's exit once a queue is detected rather than committing, maintaining ≥10 m stack spacing.
scenarios.trainingValue: Teaches conservative commitment under multi-bend partial observability where backing up may be the only recovery.

scenarios.name: one-lane-bridge-yield-violation
scenarios.description: Single-lane steel truss bridge with YIELD-TO-ONCOMING plates; a loaded grain truck enters mid-span despite ego's established right of way.
scenarios.mechanism: The bridge's width allows no simultaneous passage, and the truck's entry decision occurs before ego is visually confirmed from its cab height, so the convention collapses at the moment of commitment on both sides.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops before the approach nose within 2 s of detecting the truck's commitment, keeping full vehicle inside the approach wedge.
scenarios.trainingValue: Priority conventions on structures are social contracts; AVs must detect their breakdown early and retreat cleanly.

scenarios.name: passing-place-reverse-required
scenarios.description: On a narrow lane with passing places every 200 m, ego meets an oncoming van between places and the van driver expects ego, being closer, to reverse.
scenarios.mechanism: Geometry provides no meeting point, so the constraint propagates backward: whoever is nearer a passing place must reverse, and ego's route choice at 40 km/h determines whether a 100 m reverse is needed.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either reaches a passing place and clears it before the meet, or initiates controlled reverse into the nearest bay completing clearance in <45 s without leaving the paved/grass edge line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Structured reversing maneuvers driven by topology are nearly absent from AV datasets yet routine on rural networks.

scenarios.name: narrow-bridge-pedestrian-refuge-conflict
scenarios.description: Old masonry bridge carries one traffic lane plus a footway; two vans meet mid-span while a pedestrian waits at the entrance footway ego is about to pass.
scenarios.mechanism: The meeting vans stop and one reverses, pinning ego beside the footway exactly where the waiting pedestrian steps around the stopped vans into the carriageway.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego anticipates the pinch and holds 8 m before the entrance until the meet resolves, never having a pedestrian within 1.5 m laterally while stationary in the pinch.
scenarios.trainingValue: Structural bottlenecks couple vehicle negotiation with vulnerable users; static planning must precede the bottleneck, not react inside it.

scenarios.name: lane-drop-short-taper-aggressive-merge
scenarios.description: Freeway lane drop with a 150 m taper 300 m after the overhead sign; a driver in the ending lane rides it to the gore and forces in at the last 30 m.
scenarios.mechanism: The short taper plus queue in the through lanes makes zipper cooperation fail; the forced merge arrives with closing speed ~25 km/h and zero shoulder beyond the gore barrier.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego creates or preserves a 25 m gap in anticipation, achieving merge acceptance with TTC ≥3 s and no decel beyond 3 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Predictive gap management at geometric chokepoints is a core highway competency and a frequent crash generator.

scenarios.name: lane-drop-sign-occluded-by-truck
scenarios.description: A box truck travels in the lane scheduled to end, its trailer completely occluding the overhead LANE ENDS sign and the taper ahead from ego following in the same lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Sign information arrives only when ego changes lanes or the truck does; if ego stays, the taper's physical end appears as a sudden barrier at ~120 m reaction range.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego infers the closure from map data and surrounding flow (vehicles leaving the lane) and changes lanes ≥200 m before the taper regardless of sign visibility.
scenarios.trainingValue: HD-map priors must override degraded visual confirmation — a key robustness property for occlusion-heavy traffic.

scenarios.name: dropped-lane-gore-barrier-noshoulder
scenarios.description: Construction converts a lane drop's usual breakdown shoulder into continuous concrete barrier; a disabled car sits in the dropped lane 100 m before the taper.
scenarios.mechanism: Removal of the shoulder means the standard recovery (obstacle in ending lane → shoulder) is physically impossible, forcing an earlier, longer merge decision under time pressure.
environment: temporary concrete barrier along both sides
scenarios.successSignature: Ego merges ≥150 m upstream of the disabled vehicle with a smooth 1.5 m/s² lateral profile and never approaches the barrier closer than 1 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shoulder availability is a hidden state variable in route planning; planners must consume barrier geometry, not assume recoverable margins.

scenarios.name: peak-shoulder-running-abrupt-end
scenarios.description: Hard shoulder opens as a peak-hour running lane via gantry, then terminates in a 200 m merge taper where the general lanes are already jammed.
scenarios.mechanism: Drivers in the shoulder lane accumulate speed differential up to 40 km/h relative to the jammed through lanes, so the taper end demands a forced insertion with high closing speed and angry competitors for gaps.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego begins blending at taper start reaching ≤15 km/h differential at insertion point; no full stop in the taper and TTC ≥2.5 s at merge.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dynamic lane configuration plus speed-differential merging stresses prediction and courtesy modeling jointly.

scenarios.name: dynamic-shoulder-switched-mid-segment
scenarios.description: While ego is mid-segment on the opened hard shoulder, the gantry ahead switches to red X closing the shoulder lane immediately.
scenarios.mechanism: The control change arrives faster than natural egress: ego has ~400 m to leave a lane whose left boundary is solid barrier, competing with all shoulder traffic receiving the same instruction.
actors: broken-down car just beyond the X
scenarios.successSignature: Ego completes lane change within 350 m of the X with indicator-led, gap-checked maneuver; failure to merge triggers controlled stop before the obstruction with hazards.
scenarios.trainingValue: Infrastructure commands create instantaneous constraint flips that test reactive planning latency bounds.

scenarios.name: escape-ramp-entrance-blocked
scenarios.description: On a 7 km 6% descent, a runaway-tractor-trailer situation develops and the gravel escape ramp entrance is partially blocked by a stranded SUV that missed the ramp earlier.
scenarios.mechanism: The geometry funnels all failing trucks to one ramp whose usable width is halved, so ego observes a brake-smoking truck swerve toward the ramp while its trailer sweeps across ego's downhill lane.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects brake-fade indicators ≥500 m upstream, vacates the right lane and ramp approach, maintaining ≥100 m separation when the truck commits.
scenarios.trainingValue: Grade-driven thermal failures are predictable from geometry plus observed behavior; AVs must reason over other vehicles' physical limits.

scenarios.name: descent-brake-fade-leader-swerve
scenarios.description: Following a passenger car down an 8% grade, the leader's brakes visibly fade (smoke, wandering line) and it drifts across the centerline while decelerating irregularly.
scenarios.mechanism: Sustained grade heating degrades the leader's control faster than ego's, creating an unpredictable lead trajectory whose lateral excursions appear with less than 2 s warning at 70 km/h.
environment: tight horizontal curves within the grade
scenarios.successSignature: Ego increases following distance to ≥4 s upon first instability cue and executes a right-side dodge holding TTC ≥2 s at each excursion.
scenarios.trainingValue: Classifying another vehicle's incipient mechanical failure from motion signatures enables preemptive rather than reflexive evasion.

scenarios.name: crawl-lane-truck-exit-at-crest
scenarios.description: On a sustained climb with a signed slow-vehicle crawl lane, a heavily loaded truck exits the crawl lane back into the through lane exactly at the crest where through traffic accelerates.
scenarios.mechanism: The truck's speed peaks at the crest while through-lane cars accelerate out of the grade, minimizing the speed difference window and maximizing closure rate at precisely the point where the climb lane ends.
actors: slower truck remaining in crawl lane
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either completes a pass of the exiting truck ≥3 s before its lane change or drops back ≥50 m behind it, never straddling alongside within 30 m of the crest.
scenarios.trainingValue: Overtaking decisions must integrate grade-speed profiles; naive gap acceptance at crests produces classic heavy-vehicle sideswipes.

scenarios.name: two-lane-roundabout-inner-exit-cut
scenarios.description: In a two-lane roundabout, ego circulates in the outer lane while an inner-lane driver exits across ego's path from the left without signaling.
scenarios.mechanism: Inner-lane geometry permits legal exit only from the outer lane at most entries, but drivers habitually cut across; the spiral's short arc gives ego ~1.5 s between the cutter's rotation onset and path intersection at 40 km/h.
environment: landscaped central island blocking far-side view
scenarios.successSignature: Ego predicts the cut from the vehicle's reduced tangential radius ≥40 m out, yielding with ≤2 m/s² decel and zero conflict inside the weave area.
scenarios.trainingValue: Rule-violation likelihood varies systematically with geometry; roundabout competence requires probabilistic yield models, not rule-following assumptions.

scenarios.name: roundabout-wrong-way-entry-head-on
scenarios.description: A disoriented driver enters a multilane roundabout counter-clockwise against circulation, presenting head-on to ego mid-weave.
scenarios.mechanism: The splitter island and landscaping conceal the wrong-way entrant until they are already on the circulatory carriageway, collapsing ego's options to decelerate-and-dodge among circulating traffic on both flanks.
actors: circulating cars ahead and behind ego
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves ≥1.5 m lateral offset from the ghosting vehicle while decelerating ≤5 m/s², without contact with circulating neighbors.
scenarios.trainingValue: Counter-flow events in channeled geometry are rare but catastrophic; detection must come from heading, not lane membership.

scenarios.name: turbo-roundabout-map-marking-conflict
scenarios.description: Turbo roundabout with raised spiral lane dividers conflicts with an HD map that models conventional concentric lanes; a stopped van in the correct spiral lane blocks ego mid-circulation.
scenarios.mechanism: Raised dividers physically prevent the lane change the (wrong) map suggests, so ego must re-plan a stop-and-queue maneuver inside circulating flow while entry traffic assumes it will keep moving.
environment: turbo roundabout with mountable raised spirals
scenarios.successSignature: Ego rejects the invalid lane-change plan, stops with ≥10 m behind the van, and resumes within 1 s of gap opening without crossing any raised divider.
scenarios.trainingValue: Physical channelization outranks digital priors; testing map-geometry disagreement prevents mountable-curb strikes and stalls in live circulation.

scenarios.name: tight-corner-articulated-bus-sweep
scenarios.description: Ego waits at a tight 90° urban corner as an articulated bus turns right, its rear section sweeping across the adjacent lane and the cycle lane ego shares.
scenarios.mechanism: Off-tracking of the articulated rear follows a radius up to 3 m tighter than the front axle, so space ego legitimately occupies at the corner's entry is consumed by the trailer mid-turn with ~1 s of visible onset.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds ≥2.5 m behind the bus's trailer pivot line through the turn, entering the corner only after the rear axle clears, with no encroachment into the opposing lane.
scenarios.trainingValue: Long-vehicle swept-path prediction is a distinct skill from trajectory tracking; corner geometry dictates where to wait.

scenarios.name: box-truck-offtrack-oncoming-left-turn
scenarios.description: Making a tight protected left, ego meets a box truck turning right from the opposite direction whose cab takes the inner line while its body off-tracks into ego's receiving lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The intersection's corner radius is below the truck's design minimum, so its rear wheels cross the centerline into ego's target lane while its cab appears correctly positioned, deceiving gap-acceptance judgments.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego delays its turn start by ≥2 s versus nominal, clearing the intersection after the truck's trailer axle passes the conflict point with ≥1 m residual margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Turn sequencing against large vehicles requires modeling their rear-axle path, not their cab trajectory.

scenarios.name: trailer-tail-swing-at-corner
scenarios.description: A semi reversing into a loading dock across ego's street swings its trailer front-end (tail swing) over the sidewalk and into ego's lane as it jackknifes into the bay.
scenarios.mechanism: During the initial reverse, the trailer's street-side corner arcs outward opposite to the steer direction, intruding up to 2 m into the traffic lane for about 3 s while the driver's mirrors cover neither region well.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops ≥4 m from the predicted tail-sweep arc when the reverse begins, resuming only after the tractor-trailer aligns below 20° articulation.
scenarios.trainingValue: Reverse maneuvers invert normal sweep geometry; predicting them separates mature planners from purely forward-driving policies.

scenarios.name: tunnel-portal-blackhole-stopped-car
scenarios.description: At a bright-to-dark tunnel portal on a sunny day, a stopped car sits 40 m inside the entrance in the shadow band where contrast adaptation is worst.
scenarios.mechanism: Portal luminance ratio exceeds 10:1, so the human-equivalent and camera exposure both lose detail exactly over the obstacle; the geometric constraint (no shoulder, adjacent wall) removes dodge space discovered only after entry.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego modulates exposure/detection to register the obstacle ≥80 m inside, braking to ≤30 km/h before passing with ≥1 m wall clearance.
scenarios.trainingValue: Perception degradation is spatially correlated with structural confinement; safety cases must couple sensor physics with geometry.

scenarios.name: tunnel-wrong-way-unidirectional-bore
