scenarios.description: Inside a unidirectional tunnel, a driver who entered via the exit ramp approaches ego head-on in the center lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Tunnel walls remove all lateral escape beyond 0.8 m and eliminate U-turn or shoulder options, so the head-on threat must be answered purely longitudinally within a bore whose lanes are narrower than open road.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego achieves ≥2.5 s TTC via combined braking and maximal lane offset, stopping fully if closure continues, without contacting tunnel wall or neighbor vehicles.
scenarios.trainingValue: Constrained-corridor head-ons test the extreme of longitudinal-only evasion where standard dodge heuristics fail.

scenarios.name: tunnel-emergency-niche-blocked-breakdown
scenarios.description: A car has broken down in the travel lane 150 m past a tunnel emergency lay-by that is already occupied by a parked van; ego must traverse between them as tunnel traffic closes up behind.
scenarios.mechanism: The niche — the designated safe harbor — is consumed, so the standard response to the lane blockage is unavailable, and ego's stop location determines whether following tunnel traffic can still flow around both obstacles.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego passes the breakdown with ≥1.2 m clearance and positions itself not blocking the next niche, enabling following vehicles to keep ≥1 lane flowing throughout.
scenarios.trainingValue: Resource-consumption reasoning (who gets the safe harbor) is a coordination layer absent from simple obstacle avoidance.

scenarios.name: underpass-flash-flood-stranded-car
scenarios.description: Storm water accumulates in a rail underpass dip; a sedan is already stalled mid-bowl and its driver stands on the roof while upstream traffic keeps descending into the flood.
scenarios.mechanism: The sag vertical geometry ponds water invisibly from the approach — the surface looks wet-but-passable until commit depth; the stranded car proves the depth, and wake waves from a retreating bus raise effective depth over the crown of the dip.
actors: stalled sedan with driver on roof
scenarios.successSignature: Ego infers impassability from the stranded vehicle and standwater cues ≥50 m before the flood line, executing a U-turn or reverse uphill without entering water above 0.15 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Dips convert rain into trap geometry; reading other victims' states is often the only reliable depth sensor.

scenarios.name: underpass-poststorm-debris-subsurface
scenarios.description: After the pump system drains a flooded underpass, standing sheets remain hiding a displaced manhole cover and washed-in branches in the low lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Residual sheet water optically masks the sunken cover and debris while the wet surface doubles braking distances; the lead bus displaces water sideways exactly as ego enters the masking zone.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego selects the higher lane, holds ≥3 s headway, and registers/avoids the masked depression with steering inputs ≤0.5 Hz and no wheel drop.
scenarios.trainingValue: Post-event states differ from both dry and peak-flood cases; training the drained-but-hazardous interval closes a real operational gap.

scenarios.name: skew-rail-crossing-second-train
scenarios.description: At a 30° skewed passive rail crossing (crossbucks only), a long manifest freight occupies the crossing for 90 seconds; as its rear clears, a second train appears on the parallel track behind it.
scenarios.mechanism: The skew forces vehicles to cross track-aligned one at a time and blocks the view of the second track; drivers queued behind ego launch the instant the first train passes, but the second track remains occupied for another 20 seconds.
actors: second approaching train on adjacent track
environment: crossbucks and crossbuck signs only, no gates
scenarios.successSignature: Ego holds ≥15 m from the nearest rail until both tracks verify clear for ≥400 m in both directions, ignoring flank launches.
scenarios.trainingValue: Multi-track skew geometry defeats the 'train gone = safe' heuristic that causes many grade-crossing fatalities.

scenarios.name: skewed-crossing-stall-ahead-spillback
scenarios.description: Approaching a skewed ungated crossing in a queue, the car ahead stalls with its frame straddling the tracks while the gate-less crossing offers no warning to the through road behind.
scenarios.mechanism: Skew plus hump profile increases stall probability exactly where a stalled vehicle blocks both the crossing and ego's egress, so ego's stopping distance must be planned to leave the 'clear the tracks' escape wedge intact.
actors: train approaching from the oblique sightline
environment: limited storage between intersection and rails
scenarios.successSignature: Ego stops such that its rear stays ≥8 m from the nearest rail and maintains a path to clear the tracks in ≤6 s if the warning devices activate.
scenarios.trainingValue: Queue spillback onto crossings couples intersection and rail dynamics; positioning policy must encode escape geometry.

scenarios.name: gate-fault-flashing-no-gates-train
scenarios.description: At an active crossing, the lights flash and bell rings but the gates remain raised due to a fault; a high-speed intercity train is 25 seconds out.
scenarios.mechanism: Conflicting signals (active warnings + raised barriers + preceding cars crossing) create ambiguity that delays compliant stopping, while the skewed sightline shows the train latest of all approaches.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego treats active warnings as authoritative regardless of gate state, stopping ≥15 m from rails within 3 s of the flash detection.
scenarios.trainingValue: Hardware-disagreement resolution at crossings is life-critical; AVs must rank evidence sources explicitly.

scenarios.name: retail-strip-entrance-density-gauntlet
scenarios.description: Suburban retail strip with curb cuts every 30 m; ego passes a queue of stopped cars while an SUV exits a hidden mid-block driveway at speed across the sidewalk.
scenarios.mechanism: Stopped queue vehicles mask both the driveway openings and the exiting vehicles' approach, so the SUV's nose appears in ego's lane with under 1.5 s margin while the sidewalk-level exit path bypasses normal intersection scanning.
actors: delivery van double-parked at a cut
environment: arterial frontage with 8+ entrances per 250 m
scenarios.successSignature: Ego caps speed at 30 km/h in the gauntlet with ≥1.2 m lateral buffer from the queue, responding to emerging noses within 0.8 s with decel ≤5 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: High-entropy frontage roads reward speed governance by occlusion structure rather than posted limits.

scenarios.name: loading-dock-midblock-crossing-chaos
scenarios.description: A delivery truck parks mid-lane at a store's loading cut with hazards on; pedestrians shuttle between it and the shop as cars swing around it across the opposing lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The mid-block obstruction generates a self-organized detour pattern whose conflicts (opposing-lane swerves, pedestrian dashes behind the truck) emerge at unpredictable times and locations along the block.
environment: loading cut recess too small for the truck
scenarios.successSignature: Ego either waits for a verified-clear opposing lane before passing or holds position ≥5 s, recording zero pedestrian proximity events under 2 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Informal traffic orders around obstructions dominate real urban risk; scenario coverage here improves urban acceptance rates.

scenarios.name: gas-exit-diagonal-lane-crossing
scenarios.description: A car exits a mid-block fuel station intending the far-side arterial lanes, crossing ego's two near lanes diagonally at a shallow angle while slowing indecisively.
scenarios.mechanism: Diagonal multi-lane crossings produce continuously changing conflict geometry: the exiting car's projected path intersects each lane at different times, defeating single-gap acceptance and forcing per-lane re-evaluation every second.
actors: queue spilling back from the station
environment: station queue overflowing to the curb
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects the diagonal intent ≥3 s prior from heading-rate, easing to ≤40 km/h and preserving ≥2 s TTC in whichever lane the projection intersects next.
scenarios.trainingValue: Shallow-angle multi-lane merges from access points are a top urban crash type and stress continuous re-planning.

scenarios.name: median-crossover-u-turn-fast-cut
scenarios.description: At a divided arterial median opening, a pickup executes a U-turn from the opposing directional roadway across all three of ego's lanes from a standstill.
scenarios.mechanism: The crossover's geometry lets the pickup enter ego's roadway perpendicular and accelerate slowly, so its path intersects successive lanes with increasing closing speeds; ego in lane 3 at 65 km/h has ~4.5 s from first movement to conflict.
environment: divided arterial with unrestricted median openings
scenarios.successSignature: Ego classifies the perpendicular entry ≥4 s out, achieving ≥3 s TTC via combined 3 m/s² decel and lane drift toward the median, never requiring emergency ABS-level braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Median openings mix intersection and mid-block kinematics; per-opening risk varies enormously with gap structure.

scenarios.name: crossover-emergency-vehicle-uturn
scenarios.description: An ambulance with lights activates a median crossover U-turn; upstream traffic yields erratically — some brake hard, some accelerate to beat it — as ego approaches the opening in the adjacent lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The emergency U-turn freezes normal flow into an unpredictable mosaic of yielders and non-yielders, and the ambulance's own acceleration profile depends on gaps others grant, producing a joint behavior equilibrium ego must sample safely.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego adopts a conservative posture (≥3 s headway, ready-stop) within 100 m of the opening and resolves its action only from the ambulance's actual heading, with zero false-yield collisions modeled.
scenarios.trainingValue: Emergency-induced coordination breakdowns test social-prediction layers that pure rule engines lack.

scenarios.name: wrong-way-entry-via-crossover
scenarios.description: A driver intending a left turns into the crossover and continues down ego's directional carriageway against flow, appearing head-on in the median-side lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Wide medians designed for truck U-turns permit wrong-way continuation; the error becomes visible mainly as a headlight pair in an unexpected lane, and the median barrier denies ego any left dodge.
environment: wide depressed median with dual crossovers
three lanes each way at 70 km/h
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies counterflow ≥300 m out via heading classification, moves right with indicator and moderates speed to maintain ≥4 s TTC at pass-by.
scenarios.trainingValue: Wrong-way driving concentrates at design-forgiving geometry; detection latency here is the difference between incident and headline.

scenarios.name: chipseal-fresh-gravel-highway-curve
scenarios.description: Fresh chip-seal leaves 30 mm of loose aggregate across a sweeping 55-km/h highway curve; a motorcyclist ahead loses front traction and lowsides into ego's lane.
scenarios.mechanism: Surface friction drops from ~0.8 to ~0.5 µ precisely on the curve where lateral demand is highest, so the rider's fall is caused by the friction-radius coupling, and the sliding bike crosses into ego's lane within 1.5 s.
actors: chip-seal spreader truck parked on shoulder
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reduces to surface-appropriate speed (≤45 km/h) entering the treated section, gains ≥2.5 s TTC on the rider, and brakes only in the verified-clean strip near the fog line.
scenarios.trainingValue: Friction heterogeneity demands per-segment speed adaptation and selective braking-zone choices rarely covered in standard corpora.

scenarios.name: gravel-patch-hides-potheads-swerve
scenarios.description: A resurfacing project leaves an unmapped gravel transition strip whose ruts hide deep potholes; the lead sedan swerves violently into ego's lane to avoid one at 70 km/h.
scenarios.mechanism: The potholes are invisible under loose stone until wheel contact, so the leader's evasion is triggered at the last instant and directed into the only open lane — ego's — while ego itself is navigating the same low-friction strip.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego pre-positions ≥0.8 m left-of-center-of-lane and absorbs the swerve with ≤4 m/s² combined decel, keeping ≥0.5 m clearance through the strip.
scenarios.trainingValue: Unmapped localized surface defects induce second-order vehicle behaviors; AVs must model surface effects on others, not just themselves.

scenarios.name: county-gravel-transition-dust-cloud
scenarios.description: A paved route transitions without warning onto washboarded county gravel; the lead SUV raises a dust cloud while washboard oscillations degrade its heading control.
scenarios.mechanism: Surface change destroys both visibility (dust) and the leader's predictability (bounce-induced yaw), so ego's sensing and prediction degrade simultaneously exactly when stopping distance doubles.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects the transition within 30 m, extends headway to ≥5 s, and maintains stable tracking (lateral error <0.4 m) inside the dust cloud at ≤40 km/h.
scenarios.trainingValue: Compound degradation (visibility + friction + leader stability) tests graceful performance falloff rather than binary handling.

scenarios.name: bridge-deck-isolated-ice-spin
scenarios.description: In near-freezing dawn with clear dry approaches, a shaded river bridge deck holds an isolated ice patch; the car ahead crosses it and rotates 90°, stalling broadside across both lanes.
scenarios.mechanism: Thermal isolation makes bridge friction diverge discontinuously from approach friction, so the leader's loss is unpredictable from prior surface evidence; the spin-out converts a friction event into a stationary blockage inside ego's stopping distance.
actors: second car threading past the wreck
scenarios.successSignature: Ego infers elevated bridge-ice probability from temperature-plus-structure, pre-slows to 45 km/h, and arrests with ≥10 m behind the spun car while blocking nothing on the bridge itself.
scenarios.trainingValue: Structure-modified microclimate friction is a canonical AV winter failure; scenarios teach predictive rather than reactive surface models.

scenarios.name: expansion-joint-cyclist-instability
scenarios.description: At a bridge approach, open 60 mm expansion joints run parallel to travel; a cyclist ahead catches a wheel in the gap and wobbles violently across the shoulder into ego's lane edge.
scenarios.mechanism: Joint orientation parallel to travel traps narrow wheels, and the resulting instability emerges deterministically from geometry × vehicle width, giving ego under 2 s from wobble onset to lane intrusion.
actors: ego in adjacent lane at 50 km/h
environment: bridge approach with worn expansion joints
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects joint-parallel cycling risk ≥100 m out, shifts lane position 1 m left and passes with ≥1.5 m clearance, decel ≤2 m/s².
scenarios.trainingValue: Static infrastructure defects interacting with vulnerable users generate predictable-but-rare dynamics worth explicit training mass.

scenarios.name: bridge-joint-crater-barrier-edge
scenarios.description: A failed expansion joint leaves a 120 mm step and cavity occupying the right half of the right lane against a rigid bridge parapet — the only dodge is into the adjacent lane's traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: The defect sits where the parapet removes the shoulder option entirely, so every evasion transfers risk to the neighboring lane; at 80 km/h impact would damage suspension, but swerving creates sideswipe exposure.
actors: cars ahead straddling or swerving the joint
environment: highway bridge with failed joint filler
scenarios.successSignature: Ego identifies the defect ≥150 m out and negotiates a cooperative gap into the inner lane (or slows to let the joint pass under the wheelbase straight), with max 2 m/s² lateral and zero parapet proximity under 0.5 m.
scenarios.trainingValue: Constrained-defect navigation requires joint negotiation with adjacent traffic — cooperative maneuvering under hard structural boundaries.

scenarios.name: offset-T-right-then-left-sightline
scenarios.description: Right-then-left offset T-intersection: a car turning from the minor road right leg pulls out on ego's near side while its view was blocked by the building on the far leg's corner.
scenarios.mechanism: The offset places the minor-road driver's sight triangle behind a masonry corner building for ego's approach direction specifically; the driver commits based on a gap check valid only for the other direction, entering ego's lane with ~2.5 s margin.
actors: parked van further narrowing the minor approach
environment: corner building creating asymmetric sight triangles
scenarios.successSignature: Ego applies protective decel ≥2 m/s² whenever a minor-road occupant reaches the stop line with ego within the occluded sight envelope, achieving ≥2 s TTC at all releases.
scenarios.trainingValue: Asymmetric sight geometry makes gap decisions direction-dependent — a subtle failure mode for symmetric-interaction-trained planners.

scenarios.name: offset-T-crossing-speed-misjudge
scenarios.description: Left-then-right offset T: crossing traffic from the far leg accelerates through what it believes is one continuous crossing but the stagger inserts an extra conflict point with ego's through path.
scenarios.mechanism: The offset lengthens the crossing path beyond the driver's single-gap mental model, so mid-crossing hesitation places their vehicle exactly at ego's lane line at the moment ego arrives, converting their gap error into ego's emergency.
environment: left-right offset T with 12 m stagger
scenarios.successSignature: Ego projects the hesitation pattern ≥2.5 s ahead and resolves via controlled 4 m/s² decel to a full stop ≥3 m before the conflict point, protecting its own follower via graduated braking.
scenarios.trainingValue: Third-party path-length misjudgments propagate into ego's dynamics; prediction must encode driver workload, not just kinematics.

scenarios.name: offset-T-opposing-left-hidden-conflict
scenarios.description: At a right-left offset T on a crest approach, an opposing vehicle turning left across ego's lanes has its conflict point hidden in the vertical sag, so both parties discover the interaction late.
scenarios.mechanism: The stagger positions the opposing turn's sweep through a sag where neither party sees the other's approach speed accurately, compressing judgment of gap sufficiency at the exact point where evasive options are fewest.
actors: minor-road car waiting to exit between the offsets
scenarios.successSignature: Ego covers the brake ≥100 m before the hidden conflict zone and completes resolution with ≥2.5 s TTC or a full stop before the sag, never entering the zone alongside a crossing vehicle.
scenarios.trainingValue: Vertical geometry corrupts speed perception for all agents; ego must compensate for everyone's misperception, not just its own.

scenarios.name: construction-chicane-cyclist-squeeze
scenarios.description: Work-zone serpentine barriers force a 40 km/h S-bend through the opposing lane while the cycle lane is closed, delivering cyclists into the same narrowed chicane as motor traffic.
scenarios.mechanism: The chicane halves usable width exactly where cyclists merge into it, and the barrier walls block the sightline needed to time entries — each approach becomes a blind slot negotiation with two-wheeled participants.
actors: cyclists merging at the chicane entry
environment: urban work zone with concrete barrier chicane
closed cycle lane with diversion signage
scenarios.successSignature: Ego threads the chicane at ≤25 km/h with ≥1.5 m passing distance from cyclists, never entering while the opposing queue's head is within the slot.
scenarios.trainingValue: Temporary geometry redistributes vulnerability; AVs must handle merged modal mixes inside artificially constrained slots.

scenarios.name: channelizing-island-apron-cut
scenarios.description: At a channelized right turn with a triangular island and painted-mountable apron, an SUV cuts straight over the apron while a pedestrian stands in the island's refuge waiting to cross ego's exit leg.
scenarios.mechanism: The illegal apron cut relocates the vehicle conflict from where geometry says it belongs to where ego has no scanning routine, and the refuge pedestrian steps on the assumption that island protection equals path protection.
actors: legitimate turning truck behind the SUV
scenarios.successSignature: Ego detects apron traversal ≥2 s before conflict and yields the crossing with ≤3 m/s² decel, holding until the refuge pedestrian's crossing completes with ≥1.5 m lateral margin.
scenarios.trainingValue: Channelization shapes expectations that violations exploit; training must cover conflict relocation, not just conflict presence.

scenarios.name: dead-end-surprise-stop-reverse
scenarios.description: On a street signed as through-route on ego's map but physically ended by newly installed bollards, the lead car discovers the closure at the last moment and stops, then reverses toward ego.
scenarios.mechanism: Map-vs-world divergence means both ego and the leader learn the truth only at the terminal sightline; the leader's panic reverse converts a routing failure into a longitudinal emergency with on-street parking removing dodge space.
actors: resident stepping out to move a bin
environment: residential street recently terminated with bollards/planters
scenarios.successSignature: Ego reconciles map mismatch ≥80 m early via visual evidence (bollards visible, no continuing pavement), stopping with ≥15 m behind any leader and managing the leader's reverse to ≥5 m standoff.
scenarios.trainingValue: Map staleness at network topology level is operationally common; the compounded behavioral cascade is high-value training signal.

scenarios.name: subsidence-overnight-narrow-unlit
scenarios.description: Overnight pavement subsidence prompts cone placement that deletes the outer 1.2 m of a single lane each way on an unlit rural road, with one cone cluster knocked into the remaining lane.
scenarios.mechanism: The unplanned narrowing leaves exactly one navigable stripe with no illumination; the displaced cone occupies the survival space, so passing requires precise lateral placement guided only by retroreflectors at 60 km/h.
actors: oncoming car also threading the gap
maintenance worker returning to collect cones
environment: subsidence crater with cones and a steel plate
scenarios.successSignature: Ego threads the 2.6 m gap at ≤40 km/h with ≥0.3 m clearance to cone and opposing vehicle combined, verifying worker absence before commit.
scenarios.trainingValue: Degraded-infrastructure nights combine minimal margins with minimal sensing; robustness here indicates deployment readiness.

scenarios.name: freeze-midbox-red
scenarios.description: Hesitant driver enters intersection on late yellow, freezes at 5km/h dead center as cross traffic gets green and flows around on both sides.
scenarios.mechanism: Stationary obstacle inside the box while conflicting streams get right-of-way creates simultaneous multi-approach negotiation with no lawful precedent.
scenarios.successSignature: Ego yields and routes around with ≥0.7m clearance, or waits without entering until box clears.
scenarios.trainingValue: Right-of-way ambiguity plus in-box stationary actor.
